finding_summary: Phactr1 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and Tub in 217 P MY Pineal Glut were isolated single-gene FDR<0.10 events rather than broad pathway recoveries.
finding_consequence: These genes are useful as sentinel readouts for those low-complexity responders but should not be over-read as complete cortical or pineal Ankrd11 programs.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Ankrd11 loss generated a sparse, posterior-biased response: 6 of 23 measured neuronal groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene and the only multi-gene responders were 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
finding_consequence: A canonical chromatin regulator did not produce a pan-neuronal transcriptional collapse in this P16 mosaic loss-of-function assay; its detectable acute output was concentrated in thalamic and midbrain/pons/myelencephalon neurons with small but coherent signatures.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Setdb1 loss most consistently derepressed the gamma-protocadherin cluster, with 15 up-regulated Pcdhga/Pcdhgb gene-cell events across six responder groups.
finding_consequence: This is the clearest recovery of SETDB1's neuronal cPcdh-repressive role in the P16 acute mosaic assay, but the response is gamma-cluster biased and only appears in a subset of neurons rather than as universal postmitotic derepression.
literature_rationale: Neuronal Setdb1 loss directly derepresses clustered protocadherins in the matching direction. The six observed groups remain descriptive placement because gamma bias and absence elsewhere were not power-accounted selectivity claims.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 022 L5 ET CTX Glut; 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Setdb1 perturbation increased transcripts encoding its own silencing machinery, Atf7ip and Tasor, in thalamic, midbrain and cerebellar responders.
finding_consequence: ATF7IP stabilizes nuclear SETDB1 and TASOR is the scaffold of HUSH, so their induction looks like either derepression of cofactor loci or a compensatory attempt to rebuild SETDB1/HUSH activity after LoF.
literature_rationale: Repeated induction of Atf7ip and Tasor supports a coherent feedback observation, but their known functional relationship with SETDB1 does not show that Setdb1 loss induces their transcription.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Ctcf was a strong negative Setdb1 neighbor and reversed the Setdb1 protocadherin direction in thalamic and midbrain neurons.
finding_consequence: The opposing FDR-level overlap is mechanistically coherent with SETDB1 shielding cPcdh from excess CTCF occupancy: Setdb1 loss raises gamma Pcdh expression, whereas Ctcf perturbation lowers the same gamma Pcdh genes.
literature_rationale: Ctcf is active and reverses ten Setdb1 overlaps, including multiple gamma protocadherins; the supplied Setdb1-CTCF occupancy and Ctcf-loss evidence predicts this opposition.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Naa15, not a textbook SETDB1 partner, was the strongest validated positive data-driven comparator, sharing six FDR-level Setdb1 genes in the same direction.
finding_consequence: The a priori complex members were mostly unmeasured or nonconvergent, whereas the data nominate a restricted Naa15-overlapping thalamic/midbrain module marked by Tasor, Abhd12b, Smtn, Nin and Tcea2.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The robust Setdb1 response was heavily concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, while most cortical and hippocampal classes were weak.
finding_consequence: A broadly expressed chromatin repressor produced a sharply uneven postnatal neuronal surface: 151 TH alone contributed 27 of 45 significant downstream events, and recurrent non-Pcdh anchors such as Ccdc84 and Zmym6 were largely thalamo-cortical rather than global.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 022 L5 ET CTX Glut

finding_summary: Measured H3K9/DNA-methylation relatives did not phenocopy Setdb1: Dnmt3a, Kdm4b and Kdm4c were flat, and Ehmt1 shared only three 151 TH genes.
finding_consequence: The Setdb1 signature is not a generic consequence of disturbing DNA methylation or H3K9 methylation balance; the recovered Pcdh/HUSH-like surface is comparatively SETDB1-specific in this screen.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Two Munc13 presynaptic release genes decreased rather than increased: Unc13a was the only CNU-LGE hit and Unc13c was part of the 151 TH signature.
finding_consequence: Most SETDB1-significant genes were derepressed, but selected neuron-function transcripts can move downward, indicating a secondary cell-state adjustment rather than simple global transcriptional release.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: An active Vps35 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut produced a response largely distinct from the Vps54 program, showing that the Vps54 signature is not a generic endosome-to-Golgi trafficking response.
finding_consequence: The Vps54 phenotype is therefore not simply the default output of perturbing any endosome-to-Golgi trafficking gene in the same cells.
literature_rationale: The ledgers establish that both targets participate in endosomal trafficking but in different complexes. This shared broad pathway context is insufficient to predict their transcriptomic correlation, leaving the observed divergence without a specific literature bridge.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The Vps54-positive thalamic signature was dominated by loss of differentiated neuronal, neurite, and secretory markers rather than by induction of lysosomal genes.
finding_consequence: The strongest corrected genes point to reduced neuronal process and neurotransmission state: neurofilament/tubulin genes, Unc13a, Cpe, Pcsk2, Vgf, Atp1a3, Gabrd, Prkcg, Lingo1, Cntn1, Ntm, and Slitrk3 were all lower after Vps54 perturbation.
literature_rationale: Numerous same-direction neuronal, neurite, and secretory genes establish a coherent maintenance-withdrawal program. Target-specific Vps54 motor-neuron maintenance failure is directly compatible at the qualitative effect level; thalamic placement is descriptive context.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The only Vps54 responder did not transcriptionally activate the lysosomal, UPR/ISR, autophagy, or sphingolipid programs expected from severe GARP disruption.
finding_consequence: MPR/cathepsin-D trafficking and sphingolipid imbalance are central GARP phenotypes in other systems, but Ctsd, Ctsb, Ctsl, Lamp1/2, Tfeb, Sqstm1, Atf4, Ddit3, Hspa5, Xbp1, Sptlc, Cers, Ormdl, Sgms1, Sgpl1, and Ugcg were all FDR=1.0 here. The thalamic phenotype therefore looks like a restricted neuronal-state response, not a broad lysosomal stress transcriptome.
literature_rationale: The locally active 45-gene response makes absence of broad lysosomal, UPR/ISR, autophagy, and sphingolipid transcriptional activation informative. The sources establish physical trafficking and lipid lesions but do not predict either the tested RNA programs or their absence.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Vps54 converged with Grin1, Pitpna, V-ATPase Atp6v0c, and Rab7 perturbations on the same thalamic genes, with same-direction overlap for every overlapping FDR gene.
finding_consequence: The data-driven neighbors were not just textbook GARP members. The strongest interpretable convergence links Vps54 to endolysosomal acidification/Rab7 and thalamic excitability perturbations in the same cell class, placing its 45-gene signature in a broader membrane-trafficking/excitability module.
literature_rationale: All principal comparators are active and show substantial coherent same-direction overlap, so the atlas convergence is biological rather than neighbor geometry. The supplied literature specifically bridges Vps54 to Rab7 but does not complete the generalized Grin1/Pitpna/V-ATPase module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Negative signature neighbors were real but lower-overlap; Wdfy3 was the clearest opposite perturbation, reversing Jun, Stmn4, Kctd16, Nefm, and Nav2 in 151.
finding_consequence: This preserves the data-nominated anti-signature without over-weighting it: Nrg2 and Alx3 were more negative by correlation but had one or zero FDR overlaps, whereas Wdfy3 had five corrected genes in the opposite direction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Acute Vps54 perturbation was sharply concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: this group alone had any corrected downstream DE, with 45 genes at FDR<0.10, whereas 20 other measured neuronal groups had zero.
finding_consequence: VPS54/GARP biology is core membrane trafficking, but the screen does not show a pan-neuronal housekeeping collapse; it nominates a single thalamic excitatory state as the autonomous transcriptional responder in this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: A small remodeling arm accompanied the thalamic down-state: Jun, Stmn4, Kctd16, Rreb1, Ppm1b, Zc3h6, Cnnm1, and Phf14 were up while Egr1 and Lef1 were among the strongest down-regulated genes.
finding_consequence: The immediate-early response is split, not simply activity up or activity down: Jun rose despite Egr1 falling almost one log2 fold, which is consistent with a stress/remodeling state coupled to depressed neuronal-output genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The only same-GARP subunit present in the screen, Vps53, tracked the 45-gene Vps54 thalamic vector at the logFC level but failed to produce any corrected downstream gene in that cell group.
finding_consequence: Vps53 was the third-ranked positive neighbor by restricted correlation, yet it had 0 FDR<0.10 downstream genes in 151 and only three corrected hits across its whole measured surface. Shared GARP membership therefore produced a subthreshold shadow of Vps54 rather than a full phenocopy.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Canonical retrograde-tethering neighbors did not phenocopy Vps54: Stx16, Cog4, and Cog5 were flat in 151, and Vps35 produced its own 30-gene thalamic response with only two Vps54 overlaps.
finding_consequence: The Vps54 signature is not the generic output of disrupting any endosome-to-Golgi or Golgi-tethering factor in this screen. That divergence keeps the thalamic program attached to Vps54-specific GARP dosage/state rather than collapsing it into a broad vesicle-traffic label.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Pgk1 partially converged with Gapdh but was not phenocopied by the other assayed glycolytic knockdowns.
finding_consequence: The result refines glycolysis pathway membership by showing that adjacent enzymatic perturbations are not transcriptomically interchangeable in the Pgk1-sensitive thalamic state.
literature_rationale: Shared pathway membership and functional-network proximity do not establish that Pgk1 should be phenocopied by Gapdh or by the other glycolytic knockdowns.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The broad Pgk1 response in TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut repressed RNA-processing genes and converged with spliceosome perturbations U2af2, Prpf6, Cdc40, Snrnp70, and Tpr.
finding_consequence: Cross-perturbation convergence turns a short Pgk1 DEG list into a named nuclear RNA-processing module that would not be predicted from glycolysis alone.
literature_rationale: Several active spliceosome perturbations reproduce a coherent signed RNA-processing module, supporting a biological comparator relationship despite absent target-specific literature. The sparse 145 response does not defensibly place the full program and is excluded.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Proteasome, UFM1-conjugation, and nuclear-pore perturbations converged with Pgk1 on the same TH RNA-processing coordinates.
finding_consequence: This expands the Pgk1 phenotype from glycolysis toward a thalamic RNA/protein-homeostasis state: Psmb4, Psmc5, Uba5, Ufc1, and Tpr broadly affected 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and moved many Pgk1-down genes in the same direction.
literature_rationale: The proteasome, UFM1, and nuclear-pore comparators are strongly active and repeatedly move the Pgk1 RNA-processing coordinates in the same direction. This supports atlas convergence without a literature bridge; the sparse 145 component is not a defensible full-program placement.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Pgk1 loss repressed a neuronal membrane and synaptic-adhesion transcript set in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, including Nrxn1, Astn1, Grm1, Ptprn2, and Ptprm.
finding_consequence: Genes such as Nrxn1, Astn1, Grm1, Ptprn2, Ptprm, Cyp46a1, and Psap show that the Pgk1 signature contains a secondary neuronal-state component rather than only nuclear RNA factors.
literature_rationale: Narrowing removes the heterogeneous cholesterol and lysosome umbrella while retaining a coherent signed group of neuronal membrane, receptor, and adhesion genes in a well-engaged, well-powered group.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The two cortical Pgk1 effects were single-gene biomarkers: Gal3st3 down in L4/5 IT and Dab1 up in L2/3 PIR/AON/ENT.
finding_consequence: These FDR-significant hits preserve real cortical response points without overcalling a broad cortical pathway from a one-gene signature.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut

finding_summary: Pgk1 loss caused a sparse, highly cell-type-restricted response with 30 downstream FDR<0.10 gene×cell hits across four of 23 tested groups and 26 hits concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: PGK1 is a ubiquitous glycolytic enzyme, so the dominant dataset result is not ubiquitous stress but a selective thalamic transcriptional readout in the P16 postmitotic neuronal setting.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The expected glycolysis-family comparison mostly failed: Gapdh partially converged with Pgk1 in TH neurons, whereas Gpi1, Tpi1, Eno1, Hk1, Pfkm, and Slc2a1 did not.
finding_consequence: Sequential glycolysis genes are not interchangeable perturbations in this assay, arguing that the Pgk1 response is gated by step-specific thresholds or noncanonical coupling rather than by uniform loss of glycolytic flux.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Pgk1 did not induce the transcriptional HIF, ISR, UPR, or autophagy program expected from severe glycolytic or glutamine-deprivation stress.
finding_consequence: The absent stress signature, together with Hspa5 down-regulation, refines PGK1 autophagy literature to stressed cancer/hypoxia contexts and argues that normal juvenile neurons were not pushed into a comparable transcriptional emergency.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The largest Pitpna response lowers a thalamic synaptic/calcium module.
finding_consequence: Prkcg, Atp2a2, Ramp3, Gabra4, Lrrc7, and Grin2b were all lower in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, placing the postnatal Pitpna signature in signaling, receptor, and Ca2+-handling genes rather than in a generic UPR or neurofilament-collapse program.
literature_rationale: The concordant repression of synaptic, receptor, signaling, and calcium-handling genes forms a coherent program in a well-powered Pitpna perturbation. PITPNA biology supplies a membrane-signaling bridge but does not predict this signed thalamic transcriptional state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Pitpna also hits a thalamic neurite/microtubule arm.
finding_consequence: Tubb3, Tubb4a, Tubb4b, and Nin were lower while Stmn4 was higher in the same 151 cells, a cytoskeletal pattern that converged in Atp6v0c, Rab7, and Vps54 perturbations and suggests that altered endomembrane lipid traffic is coupled to neurite-structure genes.
literature_rationale: The signed tubulin/Nin/Stmn4 arm is coherent, and Atp6v0c, Rab7, and Vps54 are active comparators with directional convergence on that arm. The target-to-endomembrane bridge is specific, but no supplied source predicts the cytoskeletal program or comparator convergence.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Endolysosomal and retrograde-trafficking perturbations, not PITP family members, are the closest positive cross-screen neighbors.
finding_consequence: Vps54, Cltc, and Atp6v0c were the top three restricted-signature neighbors, and Atp6v0c/Rab7/Vps54 re-used the same 151 genes that Pitpna changed. This nominates an endomembrane trafficking module as the measured transcriptional output of Pitpna loss.
literature_rationale: Atp6v0c, Rab7, and Vps54 have informative response surfaces and extensive same-sign overlap with Pitpna, supporting an endomembrane-trafficking convergence beyond neighbor rank alone. The literature connects PITPNA to endosomal phosphoinositides but not to the observed signed neuronal program or cross-perturbation convergence.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Pitpna loss produced a narrow, subcortical transcriptional surface rather than a pan-neuronal phosphoinositide-loss program.
finding_consequence: The screen did not miss Pitpna globally: only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut had downstream FDR<0.10 genes, whereas 19 measured groups were flat and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: The small 217 P MY Pineal Glut response combines induction of secretory/repair-associated genes with loss of selected adhesion or membrane genes.
finding_consequence: Ptprn, Grn, Tpt1, Reep3, Cadm3, Pomgnt2, and Ube2ql1 were induced while Cdh18, Cx3cl1, Tmem63b, and Aifm3 were lower, so the pineal/P-MY effect is not just Jun/Crem but a mixed remodeling state.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: PI4K and PITPNM/VAP-family related targets fail to phenocopy Pitpna in this assay.
finding_consequence: Pi4ka and Pi4kb are plausible lipid-kinase partners of a PI-transfer protein and Pitpnm3/Vapb are lipid-contact candidates, yet none shared a Pitpna FDR gene and Pitpnm3/Vapb were completely flat across the 22 matched cell groups.

finding_summary: Gigyf2 perturbation lowered a synaptic and neuronal-signaling transcript program in 155 MB Glut, anchored by FDR-supported Nptn and Adcy8 decreases and supported by concordant Gabrb2, App, Grin1, and Cx3cl1 changes.
finding_consequence: A synaptic tail offers a candidate neuronal readout of GIGYF2 loss that is closer to circuit vulnerability than the core translation-repression machinery itself.
literature_rationale: The references establish important GIGYF2 functions but do not identify the reported synaptic RNA program as a downstream consequence. The STRING enrichment is derived from the experimental response genes and is not independent literature support for a Gigyf2-to-program relationship.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Gigyf2 perturbation recurrently increased Xbp1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut neurons.
finding_consequence: GIGYF2-4EHP loss is expected to increase translation from problematic or paused messages; an Xbp1/Selenok pulse is a plausible snRNA-visible secondary response to that proteostatic burden.
literature_rationale: The recurrent signed Xbp1 effect survives removal of the unsupported Xbp1/Selenok program and compensation claims. GIGYF2 quality-control literature supplies a plausible burden route but does not predict Xbp1 induction directly.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The strongest Gigyf2 responders repeatedly up-regulated RNP and spliceosomal genes, with Rsrp1, Luc7l2, and Snrnp70 recurring across 151 and 155.
finding_consequence: A cytoplasmic cap-repression/RQC perturbation propagated back to nuclear RNA-processing factors, suggesting secondary RNA-homeostatic compensation rather than a simple direct client-mRNA release.
literature_rationale: Repeated up-regulation of Rsrp1, Luc7l2, and Snrnp70 across two responder groups supports a coherent RNA-processing program despite the opposing Hnrnpu observation. GIGYF2 literature establishes post-transcriptional surveillance disruption but not induction of nuclear spliceosomal genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The Pvalb response consisted of a single significant row, Fndc1 down-regulation.
finding_consequence: It preserves a real, FDR-significant interneuron-specific effect while avoiding over-interpretation as a multi-gene pathway.

finding_summary: Gigyf2 produced only 42 downstream FDR<0.10 cell-group x gene hits and they were confined to five measured neuronal groups, with the strongest loads in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
finding_consequence: A broadly expressed, developmentally important translational repressor did not create a pan-neuronal snRNA phenotype after P16 mosaic LoF; the transcriptional response was a state-restricted secondary stress program.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Measured 4EHP/GYF post-transcriptional relatives did not phenocopy Gigyf2: Gigyf1, Cnot1, Tnrc6a, Tnrc6b, and Eif4e were weak, non-overlapping, or mixed in direction on the Gigyf2 features.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Tsc1 and Tsc2 shared a small same-direction subset of Gigyf2 MB/TH genes but their overall signatures were far broader.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Actb and Actg1 perturbations were transcriptionally nonreciprocal: Actb loss induced Actg1 and Flna, whereas engaged Actg1 perturbation did not reproduce the Actb compensation signature.
finding_consequence: The result argues against treating the two cytoplasmic actin paralogs as interchangeable in neuronal perturbation screens.
literature_rationale: Prior work specifically supports noninterchangeability of the two actin loci, but it does not complete the bridge to the particular reciprocal compensation pattern measured here. The result extends that biology rather than directly reproducing a documented transcriptional relationship.

finding_summary: Actb loss induces a recurrent Flna/Actg1 compensation module across 17 neuronal responder groups.
finding_consequence: Flna and gamma cytoplasmic actin are the only broadly recurrent transcripts in an otherwise 39-row signature, marking the response as cytoskeletal compensation rather than generic injury.

finding_consequence: This separates a membrane-lipid and signaling branch from the otherwise upward cytoskeletal compensation program.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut

finding_summary: Nptx2 up-regulation links the cytoskeletal Actb perturbation to a sparse glutamatergic synaptic-output marker.
finding_consequence: Nptx2 was the only synaptic/signaling transcript recurrently significant beyond Flna and Actg1, making it a candidate nuclear reporter of altered post-synaptic actin state.

finding_summary: Sin3a, Zbtb7a, and Xpo1 were the strongest positive Actb signature neighbors after excluding self-transcripts.
finding_consequence: The top convergent perturbations were chromatin and nuclear-export genes rather than actin-family genes, revealing a screen-defined Flna/Actg1/Nptx2-responsive state that was not obvious from prior actin biology.

finding_summary: Brd4, Trrap, Atp6v0c, and Srsf1 opposed the Actb thalamic 151 signature.
finding_consequence: The same genes that Actb induced in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut can be actively repressed by broad chromatin, lysosomal, and splicing perturbations, arguing the Actb state is directional and not a rank-test artifact.

finding_consequence: The result turns a negative comparator screen into biology: beta-actin loss elicits gamma-actin up-regulation, but perturbing gamma-actin or upstream actin remodelers is usually transcriptionally buffered in the P16 neuronal assay.

finding_summary: Actb P16 loss did not recover the cell-cycle, ISR/UPR, apoptotic, or embryonic migration programs expected from germline Actb loss and human ACTB/ACTG1 cortical-malformation alleles.
finding_consequence: The acute neuronal result refines disease interpretation: postmitotic LoF mainly triggers compensation, whereas the severe disease literature points to earlier and allele-specific actin dysfunction.

finding_summary: Smc1a perturbation elicited a substantial downstream response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut but no downstream response in 155 MB Glut despite convincing Smc1a transcript depletion there.
finding_consequence: The result converts a ubiquitous cohesin subunit into a sharply state-restricted postnatal neuronal response: 34 non-self DE genes were detected in a thalamic Grin2c/Prkcd group, whereas MB Glut had only self-RNA depletion and twenty other measured neuronal groups had no robust downstream DE.
literature_rationale: The global state-restriction claim is underpowered, but the compound finding contains a valid local boundary: 151 has 34 downstream genes, whereas an independently engaged 155 group has only Smc1a self-depletion. The separately retained 151 programs supply the biological content of the positive response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The 151 TH response centers on repression of calcium, NMDA-receptor, and postsynaptic genes.
finding_consequence: Loss of Grin2c, Grin2a, Atp2a2, Atp2b1, Pcp4, Necab2, Kcns2, and Lrrc7 gives the Smc1a signature a neuron-physiology axis rather than a generic injured-cell axis; Grin2c itself is a marker of the responding class.
literature_rationale: The multi-gene repression of calcium, glutamate-receptor, and postsynaptic functions is coherent within 151 TH. SMC1A's cohesin role plus direct postmitotic-neuron cohesin-loss evidence completes the chain to same-direction repression of synaptic and signaling programs.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Smc1a also represses a 151 TH extracellular-matrix and neurite/surface-cue module.
finding_consequence: Ptprm, Spon1, Sema5a, Slit3, Adamts2, Adamts19, Dner, and Pcdh1 fall in the same TH cells, indicating that the response is not limited to ion-channel transcripts but reaches adhesion, secreted-cue, and matrix genes likely controlled by long-range regulatory architecture.
literature_rationale: Eight concordantly repressed adhesion, guidance, and matrix genes define a coherent module. SMC1A is a core cohesin component, and neuronal cohesin depletion directly represses adhesion, development, connectivity, and guidance programs; exact TH genes or loops are unnecessary for program-level agreement.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The strongest data-driven positive neighbors were not arbitrary: they were Nipbl, Stag2, and Smc3, all on the cohesin axis.
finding_consequence: Nipbl and Stag2 reproduced large same-direction subsets of the Smc1a TH genes, and Smc3 had the highest restricted-signature cosine despite no individual Smc3 FDR genes. This cross-perturbation convergence makes the 34-gene Smc1a signature much more credible than a lone target result.

finding_summary: The main 151 signature centers on synaptic and neurite genes, not on a classical lysosomal or unfolded-protein transcriptional program.
finding_consequence: Down-regulated Grin2b, Kcnc2, Rims3, L1cam, Atp2a2, and Sez6l2 together with up-regulated Brsk1, Cttnbp2, Lrrc7, Ppp1r9b, Ache and Dgkz point to synaptic/excitability remodeling as the detectable nuclear output of Vps35 loss in this thalamic class.
literature_rationale: The powered group-151 response forms a coherent synaptic and excitability-remodeling program directly consistent with impaired receptor trafficking, spine maturation, and glutamatergic transmission after Vps35 deficiency.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The Vps35 transcriptional surface did not recover the expected lysosomal, autophagy, UPR/ISR, APP, or mitophagy marker programs.
finding_consequence: Because these secondary programs would be visible in snRNA-seq if strongly activated, their absence argues that the P16-P37 neuron-autonomous response did not reach a canonical lysosomal-stress state, even in 151 where Vps35 had a real 30-gene signature.
literature_rationale: The robust group-151 response makes absence of a strong canonical lysosomal RNA state informative, and direct VPS35-knockout RNA-seq predicts the opposite result. Group 054 and the broader UPR, APP, and mitophagy generalization are not independently powered or bridged and are excluded.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Serac1 was the only corrected Vps35-responsive transcript in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
finding_consequence: The isolated Serac1 increase is a candidate marker of a weak organelle-membrane response in CNU-MGE neurons, but it did not expand into a broader corrected mitochondrial, lysosomal, or stress signature.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA

finding_summary: Vps35 loss was not globally inert: the corrected response was concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with a much narrower one-gene response in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
finding_consequence: A core retromer gene produced a sparse, cell-type-selective nuclear response after P16 mosaic loss of function, so the absence of DE in most groups cannot be treated as a pan-neuronal consequence of Vps35 biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 054 CNU-MGE GABA

finding_summary: A secreted/extracellular set was selectively induced within the 151 response.
finding_consequence: Coch, Ptgds, Hapln4, Cthrc1 and Pcsk1n rose in the same thalamic group that down-regulated several synaptic membrane genes, suggesting a local compensatory or state-shift component in addition to canonical retromer cargo sorting.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The nearest data-driven neighbors of the Vps35 restricted signature were not retromer genes.
finding_consequence: Celf2, Ctnnb1, Zbtb7a and Tsc1 shared more Vps35 marker directions, whereas Apc, Arid2 and Camta1 opposed them; this nominates a thalamic stress/state axis that was discovered from the screen rather than from the retromer textbook pathway.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Among retromer-proximal measured perturbations, Rab7 partially converged with Vps35 but WASH/RME-8/Retriever/SorL1/App/autophagy comparators did not phenocopy it.
finding_consequence: The screen separates a Rab7-sensitive thalamic endosomal axis from the WASH, DNAJC13, APP/SorL1 and core-autophagy branches that dominate much of the prior Vps35 literature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 054 CNU-MGE GABA

finding_summary: Wdfy3 loss recurrently reduced Stmn4 in both 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
finding_consequence: A recurrent axonal/synaptic readout can be used as a compact marker for Wdfy3-sensitive neuronal states, but the midbrain signal is too narrow to define a full pathway.
literature_rationale: The references establish WDFY3 roles in aggrephagy, neurodevelopment, connectivity, and synaptic biology, but none documents a WDFY3-to-Stmn4 regulatory relationship.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The Wdfy3 151 program was not phenocopied by the measured core-autophagy and SQSTM1-pathway perturbations.
finding_consequence: Although ALFY/WDFY3 physically bridges SQSTM1 cargo to ATG5-ATG12-ATG16L and LC3 machinery, the observed neuronal transcriptome is not a generic readout of those neighboring autophagy nodes.
literature_rationale: The target-to-pathway relationship is specific and mechanistic, but physical or pathway adjacency does not itself predict transcriptomic interchangeability. The observed non-equivalence therefore refines an unresolved expectation rather than contradicting a documented one.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The strong Wdfy3 151 response lacked an FDR-supported DVL/canonical-Wnt transcriptional program.
finding_consequence: The disease mechanism may be stage and allele dependent: Wnt/DVL effects are prominent in brain-size models, whereas the thalamic perturbation exposed a synaptic/AP-1 module.
literature_rationale: A specific directional WDFY3–DVL3–Wnt mechanism is documented, but absence of significant Wnt-associated transcripts alone is not directional disagreement. The bridge from pathway activity to an obligatory detectable RNA signature in this setting remains incomplete.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The 151 response was a mixed neuronal maintenance program: AP-1 immediate-early genes and synaptic/secretory transcripts decreased while a smaller set of glutamate, axonal, lipid-flippase, and MAPK-linked transcripts increased.
finding_consequence: This nominates the biology actually firing after P16 Wdfy3 loss; the significant genes were Jun, Jund, Scg2, Chgb, Syt1, Syt11, Gpm6a, Kcnc2, Tspan7, and Shisa9 on the down side, with Gls, Nefm, Nav2, Atp11c, Rell2, Mapk8, Kcnk4, and Aifm3 up.
literature_rationale: The 151 response is a coherent mixed neuronal-maintenance state supported by 32 DEGs and adequate local power. Literature directly supports only the induced neurofilament arm, leaving the broader signed program incompletely bridged.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The closest positive Wdfy3 neighbors were not aggrephagy genes: Dctn1 and Celf2 had the strongest whole-rank convergence in 151, while Cacna1g and Csnk2b were sparse same-direction neighbors for Jun/Stmn4-centered features.
finding_consequence: This keeps the data-nominated module separate from the textbook WDFY3 complex: Dctn1 shared 13 Wdfy3 significant features in the same direction and Celf2 shared 15, whereas the direct autophagy comparators did not.
literature_rationale: The corrected relationship is limited to the informative Dctn1 and Celf2 convergence supported by coherent same-direction overlaps. Sparse or unavailable Cacna1g, Csnk2b, and Herc2 evidence cannot carry broader convergence or autophagy non-phenocopy claims.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Grin1, Slc6a17, Vps54, Rab7, and Atp6v0c ran against the Wdfy3 151 signature, often reversing Jun, Stmn4, Kctd16, Gpm6a, Scg2, and the Gls/Nefm/Nav2 arm.
finding_consequence: The strongest anti-neighbor was Grin1 with 13 of 13 shared Wdfy3 FDR genes in the opposite direction; the lysosomal Rab7/Atp6v0c opposition shows that blocking late endolysosomal acidification is not equivalent to losing the WDFY3 cargo scaffold.
literature_rationale: Grin1, Rab7, and Atp6v0c are active comparators with coherent opposite-direction overlap, supporting a narrowed divergence claim. Slc6a17 and Vps54 are too weak or locally limited to support the generalized comparator list.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Wdfy3 did not behave like PTEN/TSC/mTOR macrocephaly comparators in P16 neurons.
finding_consequence: Tsc1 and Tsc2 generated hundreds to thousands of FDR genes across many groups, and Pten was broader than Wdfy3, whereas Wdfy3 had only 33 significant gene-cell hits; this supports interpreting WDFY3-associated brain-size disease as embryonic Wnt/cargo-clearance biology rather than an acute postmitotic mTOR-like transcriptome.
literature_rationale: Tsc1, Tsc2, and Pten informatively establish a much broader response than Wdfy3. Mtor and Rptor are excluded as underpowered, and the breadth divergence does not by itself prove that embryonic Wnt or cargo-clearance biology is the causal disease mechanism.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Stmn4 was the only transcript reproducibly reduced in both Wdfy3 responder groups.
finding_consequence: The recurrence of Stmn4, with logFC -0.389 in 151 and -0.663 in 155, makes it the most compact marker of the Wdfy3 postmitotic neuronal effect, while the stronger 151 program shows that the MB signal is a restricted remnant rather than a full phenocopy.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Wdfy3 produced a real postnatal neuronal transcriptomic response almost exclusively in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with only Stmn4 recurring in 155 MB Glut and no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in the other 20 measured groups.
finding_consequence: The response surface is a thalamic/midbrain-restricted postmitotic-neuron phenotype, not a broad replay of WDFY3 cortical progenitor biology or a pan-neuronal autophagy collapse.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Perturbing direct or adjacent autophagy machinery did not phenocopy Wdfy3 in this neuronal screen.
finding_consequence: Despite WDFY3-p62-ATG5/ATG16L/LC3 physical coupling in aggrephagy, Sqstm1, Atg5, Atg16l1, Map1lc3a, Becn1, Rb1cc1, and Rptor were flat or far weaker than Wdfy3 in the matched groups, so the measured 151 program is not a generic core-autophagy response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The Atp2b1 thalamic response is an induced activity/calcium-adaptation program led by Fos, Nr4a1, Vgf, Cck, Opn3 and Chml.
finding_consequence: Reduced PMCA1 Ca2+ extrusion should prolong cytosolic Ca2+ signals; the recovered genes are a transcriptional readout of that predicted calcium-to-nucleus coupling rather than an unrelated stress signature.
literature_rationale: The coherent induced activity/calcium-adaptation program follows a complete target-specific chain from ATP2B1 loss through elevated cytosolic calcium to activity-dependent FOS/NR4A1-like transcription. Its placement in group 151 is descriptive rather than a selectivity claim.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Atp2b1 loss also up-regulated synaptic-vesicle, secretory and neuropeptide-associated genes including Ptprn, Syt7, Slc6a17, Pacsin2, Ap1s1, Cck and Vgf.
finding_consequence: The response extends beyond immediate-early factors into a plausible secretory-output adaptation, consistent with thalamic neurons compensating for disturbed calcium handling at vesicle release sites.
literature_rationale: Multiple concordantly induced vesicle, secretory, and neuropeptide genes define a coherent secondary program in group 151. The literature connects calcium-dependent transcription to synaptic function but does not specifically predict this signed ATP2B1-loss program or prove compensation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Gabrb2 and Slc12a5 perturbations converge on the same 151 TH activity module, sharing same-direction FDR<0.10 induction of Nr4a1, Fos, Vgf, Opn3, Chml or Ptprn with Atp2b1.
finding_consequence: The strongest robust neighbors were not PMCA-family genes but inhibitory-transmission perturbations, implying that this thalamic state funnels reduced Ca2+ extrusion and altered GABA/Cl- handling into a common activity-dependent transcriptional module.
literature_rationale: Gabrb2 and Slc12a5 are active matched-surface comparators with coherent same-direction activity-gene overlap. Target-specific chains from each perturbation to hyperactivity/calcium-dependent transcription predict the coarse convergence.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: SERCA2/Atp2a2 loss shared the thalamic Fos/Chml/Vgf-like arm but added a large ER-stress and integrated-stress program that Atp2b1 lacked.
finding_consequence: Both pumps perturb Ca2+ handling, but only the ER pump generated Ddit3, Chac1, Xbp1 and Shmt2 induction; PMCA1 loss in the same cell class therefore appears to produce plasma-membrane Ca2+ signaling adaptation without a broad ER-stress bounce-back.
literature_rationale: Both perturbations are informative in the identical group: they share an activity-like arm, while Atp2a2 uniquely produces a broad ER/ISR response that the powered Atp2b1 surface lacks. Literature supports SERCA-associated ER stress but does not directly establish the ATP2B1 absence arm or exact shared genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Top negative neighbors inverted the Atp2b1 neuropeptide/activity axis: Tardbp reduced Vgf, Opn3 and Syt7, and Ntrk2 reduced Vgf and Atp2a2 in 151 TH.
finding_consequence: The inversion argues that the Atp2b1 up-regulation of Vgf/Opn3/Syt7 is not a generic thalamic perturbation artifact; related activity-survival perturbations can drive the same genes down.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Atp2b1 produced one robust downstream response: 26 FDR<0.10 genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and zero FDR<0.10 downstream genes in the other 21 measured classes.
finding_consequence: ATP2B1/PMCA1 is broadly detected and is a core calcium-extrusion pump, so the P16 mosaic LoF phenotype is not a simple expression map; the transcriptomic consequence is sharply state/cell-type restricted.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Same-family Atp2b2 and Atp2b3 did not phenocopy Atp2b1 in 151 TH despite strong self-transcript reductions.
finding_consequence: A PMCA-family prior would predict overlap among plasma-membrane Ca2+ pumps; Atp2b2 showed only a subthreshold same-direction trace and Atp2b3 showed no convergence, making the PMCA1 thalamic response isoform-selective in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The disease-relevant ATP2B1 calcium-export axis was measurable after P16 only as a narrow thalamic transcriptional adaptation, not as a pan-neuronal developmental-delay or seizure-like program.
finding_consequence: Human ATP2B1 variants impair Ca2+ export and cause neurodevelopmental phenotypes, but those variants arise throughout development and can perturb protein localization; the mouse P16 sparse LoF result refines the risk to a postmitotic thalamic calcium-transcription node.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut program coupled loss of developmental/synaptic transcripts, including Nr2f1, Pcdh7, Lhx9, Pcdh10, Grik2, Camk2d, Map1b, and Sox2, to gains in Igfbp5, Tnr, Cx3cl1, Gabrd, Kalrn, Car4, and Slitrk5.
finding_consequence: The significant genes are not a generic nucleolar, ISR, or apoptosis module; they look like a local identity-and-connectivity retuning program in a thalamic glutamatergic class.
literature_rationale: Direct neuronal Kmt2a deletion supports the downregulated developmental, transcriptional, and synaptic arm. It does not establish the coordinated upregulated extracellular and receptor arm, leaving a consequential component of the combined retuning program incomplete.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Kmt2d was the strongest negative Kmt2a neighbor: in 151 it produced 433 downstream genes and inverted all three shared Kmt2a FDR genes, including Car4, Cry2, and Cfap74.
finding_consequence: The result argues that a KMT2A-family loss and a KMT2D-family loss do not simply reduce one common H3K4 program in thalamic neurons; related chromatin writers can push the same responsive genes in opposite directions.
literature_rationale: Both thalamic perturbation surfaces are active, and all shared significant genes are oppositely signed. Direct neuronal genetics independently establishes opposing KMT2A and KMT2D functions, supporting the qualitative divergence.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Kmt2a loss produced a sharply thalamus-centered response: 25 of the 30 downstream FDR<0.10 gene-by-cell effects lay in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while five other responding groups contained only one FDR-significant downstream gene apiece.
finding_consequence: The screen does not support a ubiquitous neuronal Kmt2a maintenance program after P16; it nominates one thalamic/hypothalamic glutamatergic class as the main postmitotic transcriptional responder.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut; 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The expected Set1/MLL relatives were measurable but did not phenocopy: Kmt2b had a 58-gene 151 response with no shared Kmt2a FDR genes, Setd1a was far broader and active in GABA groups where Kmt2a was null, Kmt2e was small, and Kmt2c was flat in 151.
finding_consequence: The nulls are not because acute chromatin-writer CRISPR is invisible in this assay; they expose paralog- and cell-class partitioning within the H3K4 methyltransferase family.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 052 Pvalb Gaba; 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Srebf2 perturbation reversed the Marchf6-induced sterol-gene program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
finding_consequence: Opposite movement of the same genes under Srebf2 loss supports SREBP2-regulon identity for the Marchf6-induced module.
literature_rationale: The literature explicitly connects MARCHF6 to degradation of cholesterol-pathway enzymes and cholesterol flux, and independently identifies SREBP2 as a coordinated activator of cholesterol-biosynthesis genes. These links form a complete same-direction chain supporting the observed reversal under Srebf2 perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Amfr perturbation failed to reproduce the Marchf6 sterol program in the two principal Marchf6-responsive glutamatergic populations.
finding_consequence: The contrast argues against a generic ERAD-E3 explanation and highlights a Marchf6-specific branch of sterol transcriptional control in the responsive neurons.
literature_rationale: The literature supplies a specific cholesterol-ERAD relationship for both ligases, making the comparison biologically grounded. It does not, however, provide a decisive expectation for transcriptomic phenocopy or non-phenocopy, so the observed divergence is an inference rather than agreement or disagreement.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The induced genes comprised a coherent SREBP feedback circuit, not isolated sterol enzymes: Marchf6 raised Insig1 and Srebf2 together with early, middle, and late cholesterol biosynthesis genes in 151 and 155.
finding_consequence: A coordinated mRNA increase implies a secondary homeostatic transcriptional state downstream of disturbed ER sterol handling rather than only direct stabilization of MARCHF6 protein substrates.
literature_rationale: The coordinated SREBP-feedback and cholesterol-biosynthesis response in both powered groups directly matches MARCH6-knockdown evidence. Neuronal cell identity is a contextual limitation, not a missing program-level edge.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Marchf6 perturbation did not elicit a coordinated UPR/ISR or ferroptosis transcriptome in the neuronal screen.
finding_consequence: Separates the juvenile mosaic brain response from known chronic POMC-neuron and ferroptosis phenotypes and prevents over-reading Acsl4 as a full ferroptotic state.
literature_rationale: The absence test is informative only in the two main responders, where target engagement and the sterol program demonstrate local assay power. The sources establish ER-stress and ferroptosis effects in other contexts but do not require the queried RNA panel in these broad neuronal groups.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Mib1, Dctn1, Chp1, Tsc1, Tsc2, and Dync1h1 were data-driven positive Marchf6 neighbors that converged on the same neuronal sterol genes.
finding_consequence: Shows that the Marchf6 program belongs to a recurrent screen module and was not an isolated artifact of Marchf6 gRNAs or its own differential expression.
literature_rationale: All six comparators have measurable surfaces and reproduce signed significant Marchf6 sterol-program coordinates, supporting an empirical convergence relationship. The cell placement is restricted to the two groups with the coherent Marchf6 sterol program, and no supplied literature bridges the comparator targets mechanistically to Marchf6.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Marchf6 loss induced a sterol/SREBP transcriptional response in 5 of 21 measured groups, with the broad response concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
finding_consequence: Identifies a narrow postmitotic neuronal window in which perturbing an ER cholesterol E3 ligase is converted into a detectable nuclear mRNA program.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Srebf2 was the pathway antipode of Marchf6, while Srebf1 was inert in this assay.
finding_consequence: Directly roots the Marchf6-upregulated genes in a SREBP2 cholesterol branch and shows that a related SREBP family member does not phenocopy the state.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Amfr, Vcp, Hmgcr, and Srebf1 failed to reproduce Marchf6 in the matched responder groups.
finding_consequence: The negative comparator result rejects a generic ERAD or one-enzyme cholesterol explanation and sharpens the phenotype to a Marchf6/SREBP2 feedback state.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Nptx2 and Scg2 were recurrently induced in both Grin2a cortical responders, with Nptx2 the top gene in each group and Bdnf additionally FDR-significant in L2/3 IT neurons.
finding_consequence: A secreted activity-dependent synaptic module is the most reproducible RNA consequence of sparse postnatal GluN2A loss.
literature_rationale: Two explicit directional links form a complete Grin2a-to-Bdnf-to-Nptx2 chain predicting reduced signaling after Grin2a loss. The informative dataset instead shows Bdnf and recurrent Nptx2 induction, so the documented expectation is opposite for the program's core.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: The top positive Grin2a restricted-signature neighbors were Kcnb1, Pde4d, Atxn10, and Gabrg2; Kcnb1 independently induced Bdnf, Scg2, and Nptx2 in L4/5 IT neurons.
finding_consequence: The Grin2a cortical state can be approximated by perturbations outside the receptor complex, nominating Nptx2/Scg2/Bdnf as markers of a broader excitability/homeostatic module.
literature_rationale: Kcnb1 is locally active and reproduces the signed Bdnf/Scg2/Nptx2 core, supporting a positive relationship. Pde4d is null and the other ranked neighbors lack equivalent local validation, so they are excluded from the corrected claim.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Grin2b was anti-similar to Grin2a in the cortical responder features and had an active opposite-direction L2/3 signature, including Cckbr and Zbtb1 down where Grin2a drove them up.
finding_consequence: A same-family NMDA-receptor subunit does not phenocopy GluN2A loss; the chronic postnatal transcriptomic consequences of removing Grin2a and Grin2b are directionally distinct.
literature_rationale: Grin2b is active in both relevant cortical surfaces and shows a strongly opposite signed relationship to Grin2a. Distinct GluN2 signaling supports divergence, but does not predict the full chronic anti-signature or exact marker signs.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: The L2/3 Grin2a signature induced neuromodulatory feedback genes Cckbr, Adora1, Rgs2, Penk, Inhba, Ptgs2, and Wfs1.
finding_consequence: The direction suggests an adaptive chronic state after receptor loss rather than a passive drop in activity-regulated RNAs.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Grin2a produced a real downstream transcriptomic response only in cortical IT glutamatergic neurons: 27 genes in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and 2 genes in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, versus 0 in the other 20 recovered groups and missing rows for 215 MB Dopa.
finding_consequence: The result localizes the chronic P16 LoF response to a narrow cortical IT context rather than to all neurons that could carry NMDA receptors.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Grin2a L2/3 IT loss produced a mixed synaptic-remodeling signature: Pcdh15, Cadm4, Sema4a, Stxbp2, Rimbp2, and Slc6a17 were induced, while Ptprd, Nyap2, Plch2, Osbpl1a, and Exd2 were reduced.
finding_consequence: The downstream state extends beyond canonical activity genes into cell-adhesion, release, and phospholipid/plasticity-linked transcripts, consistent with structural compensation over weeks.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Obvious NMDAR and Ca2+-activity pathway comparators did not recover the Grin2a Nptx2/Scg2 module: Grin1 was downstream-flat despite significant self knockdown, and Grin2d, Grin3a, Dlg4, Fyn, Camk2b, Camk2g, Camk4, Creb1, and Ntrk2 had 0 downstream FDR genes in both matched Grin2a responder groups; Mef2c was only partially overlapping.
finding_consequence: The screen argues against a generic receptor-complex or linear CaMK/CREB module and instead points to a GluN2A- and cortical-state-specific adaptation.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: In Ski-responsive cortical and thalamic neurons, Ski loss did not induce the expected canonical SMAD/TGF-beta/BMP transcriptional program.
finding_consequence: SKI is curated as a SMAD-binding TGF-beta/BMP corepressor, so the absence of adjusted Smad7/Id/Junb/Serpine1 induction and the weak correlations to receptor, SMAD, and corepressor perturbations indicate cell-state or threshold gating of the canonical pathway.
literature_rationale: Direct mechanistic studies establish SKI as a SMAD-associated repressor of both TGF-beta and BMP-responsive transcription. The observed failure to induce the nominated canonical program therefore conflicts directionally with the documented expectation rather than merely reflecting a context mismatch.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Ski loss produces an unusually substantial 27-gene transcriptomic response in L2-3 IT cortical glutamatergic neurons, identifying this measured class as an informative Ski-responsive context without proving absolute exclusivity.
finding_consequence: This converts a mostly flat screen into a precise postnatal neuronal map: the perturbation can produce a transcriptomic response, but it is confined to two glutamatergic classes.
literature_rationale: The positive cortical response survives removal of the unsupported two-class exclusivity claim. The four-gene 151 response is descriptive because that group is highly response-prone.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: The 007 cortical response centers on up-regulated neuronal adhesion and neurite/synaptic patterning transcripts.
finding_consequence: The largest Ski response is not an embryo-like apoptosis program; it is a mature-neuron remodeling signature involving cell-surface and projection-associated genes.
literature_rationale: The rare 27-gene 007 response contains a coherent, predominantly up-regulated adhesion and neurite-patterning program. Ski-dependent neuralization and NCAM provide a target-specific connection, but the gain-of-function embryonic model does not predict this signed postnatal loss-of-function program.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: The most robust data-driven convergence was non-canonical: Mib1, the second-ranked positive restricted neighbor, shared Pde4a, Ptprf and Rfx3 up-regulation with Ski in 007.
finding_consequence: Nearest-neighbor analysis prevents forcing the signature into Ski's textbook SMAD pathway; a Notch-ligand ubiquitination target better matched the measured L2/3 signature than did SMAD or TGFβ-receptor perturbations.
literature_rationale: The corrected claim is limited to Mib1, which is active in 007 and shares same-direction Pde4a, Ptprf, and Rfx3 effects with Ski. Flat receptor-pathway comparators and cosine ordering cannot support broader convergence or non-phenocopy claims, and no literature bridge specifically connects Ski and Mib1 loss.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Sin3a, a Ski-associated corepressor-network target, was a broad responder but did not phenocopy Ski.
finding_consequence: This rejects a generic corepressor-collapse explanation for the 31-gene Ski surface: Sin3a loss changed hundreds to thousands of genes in several classes and even drove Spock2 opposite to Ski in 151.
literature_rationale: Sin3a is strongly active on the relevant surface, yet differs sharply from Ski in breadth and opposes the Ski Spock2 effect in 151, making the non-phenocopy informative. Direct SKI-mSIN3A complex membership validates the comparison but does not predict transcriptomic equivalence or the observed divergence.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The mouse CRISPR LoF surface should not be interpreted as a Shprintzen-Goldberg syndrome phenocopy.
finding_consequence: Shprintzen-Goldberg variants stabilize SKI and attenuate TGFβ-responsive transcription; the screen instead delivered postnatal sparse LoF and showed no broad canonical TGFβ target shift, so disease extrapolation is allele- and stage-limited.
literature_rationale: The dataset supports a bounded absence of a broad canonical TGFβ transcriptional program in the two Ski-responsive groups. Patient variants directly differ mechanistically from simple loss by preventing phospho-SMAD binding and stabilizing SKI, so the literature directly supports the allele-specific non-phenocopy warning.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: A small nuclear-regulatory branch of the 007 signature increased Chd3, Rfx3 and Macroh2a1.
finding_consequence: The responder program contains secondary chromatin and transcription-factor changes rather than only terminal neuronal markers, consistent with Ski loss being buffered through other nuclear regulators.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Neuropeptide and secretory markers were cell-type split: Penk and Chgb decreased in 007 whereas Cck increased in 151.
finding_consequence: Ski loss does not impose one universal secretory-neuropeptide state; the direction depends on the neuronal class in which the perturbation is read out.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ski loss produced a compact up signature of Cck, L1cam, Spock2 and Ywhah.
finding_consequence: The 151 response is statistically real despite small effect sizes and shares the adhesion/remodeling flavor of 007 through L1cam and Spock2 rather than a canonical SMAD immediate-response set.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Ski perturbation in 007 produced a mixed membrane lipid and second-messenger signature, with Pde4a, Plch2 and Slc27a1 up but Acsl3 and Atp8a2 down.
finding_consequence: This separates the L2/3 response from a simple all-up transcriptional derepression model and nominates membrane trafficking or phospholipid remodeling as a local consequence of Ski loss.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Acute postnatal Ski loss uncoupled from canonical TGFβ/BMP-SMAD target induction and from measured receptor/SMAD knockout phenotypes.
finding_consequence: The expected Id/Smad7/Skil/Serpine1/Cdkn1a-Junb/Klf module was absent, and nearly every measured pathway node was flat in the Ski-responsive groups; Ski's P16-P44 neuronal effect is therefore not a simple release of a ligand-driven SMAD program.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: In Tbr1-responsive glutamatergic groups, canonical developmental layer-6, WNT, and GRIN2B-associated targets failed to show an FDR-supported program despite detectable downstream transcriptional responses.
finding_consequence: Published Tbr1 mutants alter Wnt7b, Fezf2, and other identity genes; their absence here suggests that the assayed state captures a later or buffered transcriptional output rather than the full developmental Tbr1 program.
literature_rationale: Genetic, binding, and transcriptional studies provide target-specific directional expectations for multiple nominated genes and programs. Their supported absence in responsive Perturb-seq groups is therefore opposite to the documented developmental response, although the later experimental state limits transportability.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut

finding_summary: Acute P16 Tbr1 loss of function produced a compact response restricted to forebrain glutamatergic classes, with real FDR<0.10 signal in 001 L5-6 IT, 005 L4-5 IT CTX, 009 L2-3 IT PIR/AON/ENT, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB cells and no significant downstream genes in 19 other measured classes.
finding_consequence: The positive surface follows the known pallial projection-neuron biology of Tbr1 rather than a whole-brain or pan-neuronal stress response, even though editing was delivered broadly by AAV.
literature_rationale: The forebrain-glutamatergic distribution remains meaningful after comparison with highly response-prone null subcortical groups, although uncertain target engagement limits individual nulls. Tbr1 expression in matching neuronal territories supports plausibility but is not perturbation evidence producing this response distribution.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut; 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut

finding_summary: L5/6 IT and L4/5 IT cortical responders shared a Dkk3-down/Cpne6-up module accompanied by changes in membrane, neurite and synaptic genes such as Igsf9b, Ppfia4, Scube1, Sgsm1, Rtn4, Rtn4r, Kcna1 and Slc24a2.
finding_consequence: The recurrent genes nominate a maintenance and connectivity module that is visible after postnatal Tbr1 perturbation, whereas the classical embryonic Fezf2/Bcl11b fate switch is not.
literature_rationale: Repeated Dkk3-down and Cpne6-up changes with compatible membrane and neurite genes support a compact program in two adequately measured cortical groups. No supplied source specifically bridges Tbr1 loss to this signed program.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: The NP-CT-L6b-OB responder was unidirectional and centered on Cacna1g, Cpne6, Gaa and C1qtnf4 induction.
finding_consequence: The strongest single Tbr1-induced transcript in the screen was Cacna1g in a class containing corticothalamic and L6b neurons, aligning the acute response with the deep corticofugal lineage in which Tbr1 is classically required.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut

finding_summary: The robust cross-perturbation phenocopies of Tbr1 were not TBR1-network transcription factors but Ppp2r1a, Psmb4, Psmc1 and Ap2s1, which recapitulated same-direction subsets of Dkk3, Cpne6, Ppfia4, Scube1, Sgsm1, Ly6e and Gaa.
finding_consequence: This separates the measured P16 Tbr1 state from the textbook embryonic TBR1 cascade and suggests that part of the compact signature is a homeostatic membrane/proteostasis state shared with phosphatase, proteasome and vesicle-adaptor perturbations.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut

finding_summary: P16 mosaic Tbr1 perturbation did not recover the expected embryonic Fezf2/Bcl11b, Bcl6/Cdh9, Auts2/Sox5, Reln or Grin2b programs at FDR<0.10.
finding_consequence: The absent canonical genes explain why this screen should not be read as a miniature embryonic Tbr1 knockout: it captures residual postmitotic maintenance biology after cortical neuron specification, not the early fate switch that dominates the literature and disease-gene ChIP reports.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut; 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut

finding_summary: Cask, Satb2, Pax6, Foxp2, Bcl11b, Cux1, Cux2, Reln, Neurod2, Sox5, Auts2 and Bcl11a perturbations had zero FDR<0.10 genes in the four Tbr1 responder groups, and the small Foxg1 and Grin2b signatures shared no significant Tbr1 genes.
finding_consequence: Directly testing the obvious TBR1-associated developmental and protein-interaction network prevents a misleading assumption that every known TBR1 partner phenocopies Tbr1 in this postnatal mosaic assay.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut; 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut

finding_summary: Med13 and Med23 partially reproduced the Med15 thalamic down-program, whereas Med12 and Cdk8 did not despite informative matched-cell measurements.
finding_consequence: The response cannot be explained as generic loss of any Mediator subunit; it separates a Med15/Med13/Med23-sensitive neuronal regulon from CDK8-module or other Mediator perturbations with larger cell counts.
literature_rationale: The structural, interaction, and complex-membership references provide general shared-complex context, not the specific subunit-selective target-to-program bridge required for this focal finding.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Med15 perturbation did not induce the canonical SREBP2 cholesterol-target decrease in thalamic neurons, although Srebf2 perturbation robustly produced that program in the same assay.
finding_consequence: The dataset argues that the neuronal Med15 program is not simply the canonical SREBP2 cholesterol-biosynthesis program; Srebf2 knockout robustly lowered sterol genes that Med15 perturbation left nonsignificant.
literature_rationale: The target-to-program bridge is direct and directional. However, nonsignificance under weak target engagement is not evidence of true biological disagreement, even though the matched Srebf2 perturbation confirms that the assay can detect the sterol program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response preferentially lowered synaptic and calcium/excitability genes.
finding_consequence: Genes such as Lrrc7, Grm1, Gabra4, Kcnc2, Atp2b1, and Atp2a2 place the Med15 effect on differentiated neuronal function rather than on canonical lipid or TGFβ/Nodal readouts.
literature_rationale: Multiple same-direction synaptic and calcium genes support a coherent within-151 program. No MED15-specific perturbation evidence bridges Med15 loss to this signed neuronal program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Med15 loss also reduced adhesion, neurite, and cytoskeletal regulators in the same 151 thalamic population.
finding_consequence: Downregulation of Ntng1, Adgrb1, Nell1, Trim9, Nin, Hook1, Ptpn3, Plekhg1, and Fhdc1 shows that the thalamic signature extends beyond ion channels to structural neuronal programs.
literature_rationale: The coordinated decreases in adhesion, neurite, and cytoskeletal regulators form a defensible program in 151, but no target-specific MED15-to-program bridge is supplied.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Several TH Prkcd subtype-patterning genes were coordinately lower after Med15 perturbation.
finding_consequence: Loss of Prkcd, Pcp4, Lef1, Zic1, Vangl1, and Adarb2 suggests erosion of a cell-state/identity axis in an already postmitotic thalamic glutamatergic class rather than a fate-specification defect.
literature_rationale: The coordinated marker/regulator decreases support erosion of a postmitotic 151 cell-state program, without implying lineage conversion. No MED15-specific bridge predicts this signed identity subset.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The Med15 restricted signature converged most strongly with Psmb4, Psmc5, Psmc1, Ctnnb1, Supt16, and Slc7a6os, while Ptcd3, Setd5, Abcd3, Max, and Bbip1 lay on the opposite side.
finding_consequence: The screen nominates a thalamic synaptic-down state shared with Psmb/Psmc, Ctnnb1, Supt16, and Slc7a6os perturbations; the negative neighbors show that the comparison is not simply a generic direction across all essential genes.
literature_rationale: The six positive comparators have active response surfaces and extensive same-direction overlap, supporting the already-stated positive convergence. Flat Ptcd3, Abcd3, and Bbip1 cannot support opposition and are excluded; the isolated cortical Med15 hit is not part of the focal program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Usp48 was the only significant L4-5 IT CTX Glut response and was upregulated.
finding_consequence: A lone deubiquitinase hit could be an early ubiquitin-system compensation marker, but the one-gene, FDR 0.073 signature is hypothesis-generating rather than a pathway-level call.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Med15 was a sharply thalamus-biased, mostly negative responder: 26 downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and a single Usp48 hit in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, with zero FDR<0.10 genes in the other 20 tested neuronal groups.
finding_consequence: This pattern argues against a universal acute transcriptional collapse after partial postnatal Med15 loss and focuses the biology on a susceptible TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Mediator relatives did not phenocopy uniformly: Med13 and Med23 partially matched the 151 Med15 signature, whereas Med12 and Cdk8 were flat in the same class.
finding_consequence: This separates a Med15-like thalamic output from the CDK8 kinase-module perturbations that might have been expected to behave similarly simply because they are in the same holo-complex.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Med15 loss in postnatal neurons did not recover either the SREBP/lipid program or the TGFβ-Nodal/SMAD program expected from classic ARC105/MED15 studies.
finding_consequence: Because Srebf2 perturbation did downregulate sterol genes in the same screen, the Med15 negative is not just a failure of snRNA-seq to see lipid targets; it refines MED15 biology to an activated, context-dependent coactivator role rather than a basal requirement in these juvenile neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Nf1 loss induced a sparse Vgf-centered neuropeptide response in seven neuronal classes rather than a pan-neuronal transcriptome.
finding_consequence: Vgf marks the dominant recovered neurotrophin/Ras-output gene and localizes the acute Nf1 transcriptional effect to selected postmitotic neurons.
literature_rationale: Recurrent signed Vgf induction is the defensible focal effect. The exact seven-class distribution is descriptive rather than validated selectivity, and the supplied Ras and neurotrophin edges do not complete a target-specific Nf1-to-Vgf chain.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 052 Pvalb Gaba; 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Nf1 loss produced a 151 TH neuronal response containing Vgf and the Ras-feedback genes Ptpn5 and Etv5 together with neuronal-remodeling transcripts.
finding_consequence: This thalamic class is the only place where the acute Nf1 perturbation moved beyond a single gene into a multi-gene Ras-output and neuronal-remodeling signature.
literature_rationale: The 13-gene positive response survives independently of selectivity; neuronal literature supports increased Ras activity after neurofibromin loss, although it does not fully predict the reported transcript set.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: 191 MB P MY GABA coupled Vgf to Scg2, Unc13a, Etv4 and Tnfrsf12a, a compact neurosecretory/MAPK-ETS module distinct from the thalamic response.
finding_consequence: Nf1 can engage the same Vgf axis with different accessory genes in a hindbrain GABAergic population, arguing that Vgf is shared but the secondary remodeling program is cell-type-specific.
literature_rationale: The five-gene, same-direction neurosecretory/MAPK-ETS module is a coherent local program, but its placement in group 191 is descriptive and does not prove selective sensitivity. The sources do not predict the accessory-gene composition.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Positive TrkB-RAF-MEK pathway perturbations opposed Nf1 in the matched thalamic Vgf module.
finding_consequence: The fact that Ntrk2, Braf, Map2k1 and Shoc2 loss decrease the same Vgf/Ptpn5/Atp2a2/Etv5/Unc13a module that Nf1 loss increases anchors the Nf1 signature in a Ras/MAPK-like direction rather than in a generic perturbation-stress axis.
literature_rationale: Each comparator actively decreases overlapping members of the thalamic module that Nf1 loss increases. The supplied NF1, Trk, RAF-MEK, SHOC2, and Vgf evidence completes the qualitative chain predicting this opposite-direction pathway relationship.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Nf1 did not trigger a Tsc1/Tsc2-like PI3K/mTOR transcriptional program in neurons even where Tsc perturbations were strongly detectable.
finding_consequence: This separates the acute neuronal Nf1 output from the astrocyte/glioma NF1-mTOR branch and argues that absence of ribosome, lysosome or proteostasis programs is biological rather than a failure of the snRNA-seq readout.
literature_rationale: Strong matched Tsc1/Tsc2 responses make the absence of a TSC-like Nf1 program an informative divergence, and the direct source supports coarse Nf1-versus-Tsc1 non-equivalence. The corrected claim is narrowed to Tsc1/Tsc2 rather than generalized across less-documented Pten and Mtor comparators.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut showed an isolated decrease in Pten without the Vgf/MAPK-output genes seen in other Nf1-responsive classes.
finding_consequence: The single-gene Pten response separates a PI3K-brake feedback event from the canonical Vgf transcriptional branch and nominates this hypothalamic glutamatergic class for focused follow-up.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: The top positive restricted-signature neighbor, Lztr1, only partially converged with Nf1, while Lrp1 shared same-direction Vgf/Unc13a in midbrain groups.
finding_consequence: Lztr1 supports a RASopathy-like convergence, but the small FDR overlap shows that acute neuronal Lztr1 loss is not a full Nf1 phenocopy; Lrp1 is a data-nominated, noncanonical Vgf partner.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut showed an isolated Lrrc7 increase instead of the recurrent Vgf response.
finding_consequence: This preserves a real cortical Nf1 effect that would be hidden by a Vgf-only summary and nominates Lrrc7 as an exploratory postsynaptic marker of Nf1 perturbation in upper-layer IT neurons.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: SPRED and alternative RasGAP relatives did not phenocopy Nf1.
finding_consequence: SPRED1/SPRED2 can recruit neurofibromin and RASA2/SYNGAP1 are RasGAP-family brakes, but their flat surfaces show that Nf1 is the limiting Ras-to-transcriptome brake in the Vgf-responsive cells of this assay.

finding_summary: Nsd1 loss induced a narrow, mostly up-regulated thalamic program containing ectopic metabolic, extracellular, membrane, and cytoskeletal genes.
finding_consequence: NSD1 is a chromatin writer with developmental brain functions, but the acute mouse-brain Perturb-seq effect was concentrated in one thalamic glutamatergic class rather than being pan-neuronal.
literature_rationale: The cited neuronal Nsd1-loss study directly reports ectopic non-neural expression and identity disruption, matching the observed predominantly up-regulated ectopic metabolic, extracellular, membrane, and cytoskeletal program. Exact markers and neuronal subclass need not match.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The strong thalamic Nsd1-loss program was not reproduced by engaged Ash1l loss, arguing against a generic acute H3K36-writer response.
finding_consequence: A related perturbation, Ash1l, gave significant self-knockdown with no non-self FDR hits, while Nsd2 and Setd2 did not phenocopy Nsd1 and genome-wide correlations to Nsd1 were near zero; Nsd1 therefore marks a more specific state than simple loss of any H3K36-associated methyltransferase in this assay.
literature_rationale: The references support shared H3K36-related biology but not perturbational equivalence. The engaged Ash1l comparison makes the experimental non-convergence informative, while weaker Nsd2 and Setd2 tests limit broader conclusions.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The strongest same-direction Nsd1 neighbor was Zmynd8, with 11/11 shared FDR<0.10 rows in the same direction; Kdm5c was a smaller all-same neighbor with 5/5 overlaps.
finding_consequence: This makes the data-driven chromatin-reader/demethylase neighborhood, not the canonical NSD paralogs, the closest measured approximation to the acute Nsd1 signature.
literature_rationale: The fully same-direction Nsd1–Zmynd8 overlap is supported by the complete writer-to-H3K36me2-reader chain and an informative Zmynd8 response surface. The smaller Kdm5c relationship lacks a specific bridge and is excluded from the corrected focal claim.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Myo5c was the only recurrent Nsd1 downstream gene across responder glutamatergic classes: it was induced in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and again in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The recurrence nominates Myo5c as a compact marker of the Nsd1/Zmynd8-compatible de-repression module even though most other Nsd1 genes were TH-specific.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Nsd1 loss produced a real but narrow transcriptional response concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with 24 downstream FDR<0.10 genes dominated by ectopic metabolic, extracellular-matrix, immune-like, actin-motor, and membrane/Ca2+ genes.
finding_consequence: The main acute P16 neuronal effect is not a global chromatin-collapse or canonical cortical-layer program; it is a sparse thalamic de-repression state anchored by Ddo, Pygm, Capn3, Ptgds, Myo5c, Col9a3, Zap70, Kcnk4, Ano6 and Sil1.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Srsf1 was the strongest inverse Nsd1 neighbor, reversing 14 of 15 shared FDR rows; Sin3a was also mostly inverse, reversing 8 of 10.
finding_consequence: Related genes in the Nsd1 TH module can be driven bidirectionally by other perturbations, arguing that the module is a regulated axis rather than an artifact of one noisy gene list.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The literature-obvious H3K36 writers did not converge with Nsd1: Nsd2 had no FDR genes in the matched responder groups, Ash1l had no downstream FDR genes despite a significant Ash1l self-row in 151, and Setd2 produced only Septin5.
finding_consequence: The acute Nsd1 TH/Pvalb/L4-5 outputs should not be read as a generic consequence of losing any H3K36 methyltransferase; Nsd1 was separated from its most obvious paralog and pathway neighbors in the measured screen.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Zmym2 loss produced a 24-gene response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut in which 22 genes increased, consistent with loss of transcriptional repression.
finding_consequence: This is the main positive biology of the perturbation: Zmym2 behaves as a context-restricted chromatin corepressor in a specific mature thalamic glutamatergic state, not as a pan-neuronal dependency.
