literature_rationale: Removing the unsupported thalamic selectivity and pan-neuronal-negation clauses leaves a literature-compatible, empirically supported de-repression phenotype.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Zbtb7a and Chd4 were the strongest positive data-driven signature neighbors of Zmym2; the BHC-associated target Gtf2i gave a smaller same-direction overlap.
finding_consequence: Cross-perturbation convergence elevates the thalamic Rasgrp2/Notum/Plppr3/Stxbp2 module above a one-target observation and shows that selected chromatin regulators can drive the same loci.
literature_rationale: The active comparators provide repeated same-direction thalamic overlaps, although Zbtb7a is broad and Gtf2i is small. BHC evidence specifically bridges ZMYM2 to GTF2I, while convergence with Zbtb7a and Chd4 remains mechanistically unsupported.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Kmt2b, Srsf1, and Kansl1 formed the top negative Zmym2 signature neighbors by reversing multiple Zmym2-up thalamic loci.
finding_consequence: The anti-signature suggests that the Zmym2-de-repressed genes need other chromatin or RNA-processing activities to stay active; loss of those activities drives the same cell type away from the Zmym2 state.
literature_rationale: The corrected relationship is narrowed to the active, bounded Kmt2b comparator, which reverses seven Zmym2 loci. Broad Srsf1 and the two-gene Kansl1 overlap do not support a generalized three-comparator anti-module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: 155 MB Glut showed a tiny two-gene Zmym2 response with Nfe2l2 and Rom1 at FDR 0.0937.
finding_consequence: Nfe2l2 is a plausible candidate marker of a midbrain Zmym2-sensitive stress/redox locus, but the absence of a larger NRF2 target set means this is not a full oxidative-stress program.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: 217 P MY Pineal Glut contained a single Rnf26 up-regulation after Zmym2 perturbation.
finding_consequence: The result flags one pineal/hindbrain ER-ubiquitin-associated locus as Zmym2-sensitive, but it is a single-gene, n=21 observation.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: The thalamic up-state centers on membrane signaling, adhesion, and calcium/Wnt-associated genes rather than a generic stress program.
finding_consequence: Genes such as F11r, Npr1, Notum, Rasgrp2, Epha10, Kcnh3, Atp2a3, and Ebf4 define a specific de-repressed thalamic regulon and explain why the response cannot be summarized as generic damage or UPR.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: A second 151 TH component up-regulated cytoskeletal, lipid, and synaptic-membrane genes including Marcksl1, Plppr3, Smtn, Ugt8a, Whrn, Efr3a, and Stxbp2.
finding_consequence: This preserves a distinct remodeling branch of the measured Zmym2 signature that is separate from Npr1/Notum/Rasgrp2 signaling and is cross-supported by Zbtb7a, Chd4, Kmt2b, Srsf1, or Kansl1 overlaps.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Measured BHC/REST-associated relatives did not uniformly phenocopy Zmym2: Gtf2i partially converged, Phf21a was different, and Rest was flat in the same thalamic group.
finding_consequence: This tests and rejects the simple expectation that all measured members or recruiters of an LSD1/CoREST/BHC repression axis are interchangeable in postnatal thalamic neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Hnrnpa2b1 perturbation recurrently induced its paralog Hnrnpa1 in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic responders.
finding_consequence: HNRNPA1 and HNRNPA2B1 are related hnRNP proteins and are co-implicated in prion-like-domain neurodegeneration, so Hnrnpa1 up-regulation is a plausible compensatory or stress marker rather than an incidental singleton gene.
literature_rationale: Co-implication in disease, family relatedness, and network association do not constitute a target-to-transcript induction bridge. The recurrent compensatory edge is therefore not specifically anticipated by the supplied literature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Hnrnpa2b1 perturbation elicited a mixed RNA-processing feedback program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with Rbm25, Tcerg1, Drosha, and Hnrnpa1 up and Hnrnpu down.
finding_consequence: This links an hnRNP target with a cell-class-specific network of splicing and microprocessor-adjacent genes, consistent with known HNRNPA2B1 functions in RNA processing but placing the transcriptomic response in one brain cell class.
literature_rationale: The target-to-RNA-processing bridge is biologically specific and includes nervous-system loss-of-function evidence, but the required directional link to this mixed feedback expression program remains undocumented.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Hnrnpu sits on the Hnrnpa2b1 response surface but is not a phenocopy: Hnrnpa2b1 down-regulated Hnrnpu in thalamic and lower-brain GABAergic responders, whereas direct Hnrnpu perturbation produced 1927 FDR<0.10 genes across the six Hnrnpa2b1 responder groups and more opposite than same Hnrnpa2b1-signature overlaps.
finding_consequence: A high-confidence hnRNP neighbor can move in the Hnrnpa2b1 response without sharing its sign structure, separating Hnrnpa2b1 buffering from the much broader Hnrnpu gene-abundance program.
literature_rationale: Hnrnpu is an active, broad comparator on the matched surface, while the Hnrnpa2b1 signature contains signed events and recurrent Hnrnpu decreases in the thalamic and lower-brain GABA groups. The excess of opposite over same-direction overlaps supports empirical divergence, but no source predicts its sign structure.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Hnrnpa2b1 generated a real but very sparse gene-abundance phenotype: only 6 of 21 measured neuronal groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, with the largest response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and a smaller Hnrnpa1-positive response in 155 MB Glut.
finding_consequence: For a broadly acting hnRNP, the screen does not show a uniform housekeeping collapse; in this P16 postmitotic mosaic setting, Hnrnpa2b1 loss is buffered in most neurons and tips a detectable transcriptional state only in a few thalamic, midbrain, hypothalamic, and lower-brain classes.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Hnrnpa1 was the clearest recurrent induced transcript after Hnrnpa2b1 perturbation, rising in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut; the reciprocal Hnrnpa1 perturbation, however, was flat in both groups.
finding_consequence: The screen nominates a paralog/family buffer rather than a one-to-one paralog equivalence: Hnrnpa2b1 loss can recruit Hnrnpa1 in selected glutamatergic neurons, but Hnrnpa1 loss does not phenocopy the Hnrnpa2b1 signature in the same assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The strongest data-driven positive neighbors were not the A/B paralog itself but broad RNA-processing perturbations: Srsf1 shared 12 same-direction versus 5 opposite Hnrnpa2b1-signature genes, while Snrnp70 and Tnpo3 each shared 6 same-direction and 0 opposite genes.
finding_consequence: Cross-screen structure connects the sparse Hnrnpa2b1 signature to splicing/import perturbations, while also flagging Ppp2r1a as a broad non-RBP neighbor; the result would have been missed if only textbook HNRNPA2B1 paralogs were tested.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Several large perturbation signatures ran counter to Hnrnpa2b1 rather than with it: Zbtb7a, U2af2, Ogt, Hnrnpu, and Matr3 had negative same-minus-opposite overlap balances on the Hnrnpa2b1 FDR signature even though U2af2, Hnrnpu, and Matr3 were broad responders in the same cell groups.
finding_consequence: The Hnrnpa2b1 surface is not a generic RNA-processing stress signature; related or broad nuclear perturbations can drive the same measured genes in the opposite direction.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Simple postmitotic Hnrnpa2b1 LoF did not phenocopy the broad RBP-disease signatures; across the same six responder groups Hnrnpa2b1 had 25 downstream genes, whereas Srsf1, Hnrnpu, Tardbp, Matr3, and Fus produced thousands to hundreds.
finding_consequence: Human HNRNPA2B1 disease is tied to prion-like-domain point mutations and perturbed RNP granules, so an acute gene-disrupting CRISPR perturbation in juvenile neurons is a poor proxy for toxic aggregation or tau-associated gain-of-function states; the screen is more informative for loss-of-function gene-abundance buffering than for whether aggregation biology exists.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: B9d1 perturbation produced a 25-gene synaptic, membrane, adhesion, and cytoskeletal remodeling program in 308 CB GABA.
finding_consequence: The screen places the acute postnatal response in a narrow cerebellar GABA context rather than in the broad cortical, striatal, thalamic, hypothalamic, and midbrain neuronal populations where a generic ciliogenesis stress would have been visible.
literature_rationale: The failed cross-cell-type selectivity clause should not erase the substantial positive program. Narrowing retains the observed CB GABA molecular response without claiming that null groups prove exclusive localization or that unmeasured physiological remodeling occurred.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Ranbp2 was the strongest corrected same-direction neighbor of B9d1 in 308 CB GABA, sharing 11 of the 25 B9d1 FDR genes.
finding_consequence: This nominates a data-driven 308 CB GABA state that was not predicted by the B9/MKS literature and preserves the fact that the nearest positive neighbor was not another textbook ciliary transition-zone perturbation.
literature_rationale: Ranbp2 is locally informative and shares 11 of 25 B9d1 genes in the same direction on the same surface. This supports empirical convergence without implying a prior B9D1–RANBP2 mechanism or treating nearest-neighbor rank itself as biological evidence.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Wdr26 opposed the B9d1 308 CB GABA state, with 22 of 25 B9d1 FDR genes significant in the reverse direction after Wdr26 perturbation.
finding_consequence: The same small cerebellar GABA gene cassette lies on a reproducible regulatory axis rather than being a random list of B9d1-only hits: Wdr26 is broad and antagonistic, while Ranbp2 is narrower and partially convergent.
literature_rationale: Wdr26 is highly active and reverses 22 of 25 B9d1 genes on the same cerebellar surface, providing a coherent and strongly powered opposite-direction relationship. No supplied source provides a target-specific mechanistic bridge.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: The 308 CB GABA B9d1 signature was a synaptic, membrane, adhesion, and cytoskeletal remodeling signature, not a Hedgehog or core ciliary-gene feedback program.
finding_consequence: B9d1 loss did not simply turn on or off the canonical GLI/PTCH/IFT/MKS module expected from embryonic transition-zone failure; the measured response instead implicated neuronal membrane organization genes such as Homer3, Grm7, Dlg2, Doc2b, Scn4b, Lrp8, Cdh2, Col5a1, Col18a1, Arhgap31, Arap1, Strip2, Atl2, and Gas8, with Bend6, Aldoa, and Arl15 decreased.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: ER protein-folding genes were significantly decreased after Rb1cc1 perturbation rather than induced as a canonical stress response.
finding_consequence: The strongest repeated transcript class, Hspa5/Calr/Pdia6/Hyou1, argues against a simple model in which FIP200 loss immediately activates a UPR/ISR mRNA module in the affected neurons.
literature_rationale: The defensible focal result is the repeated signed decrease of ER-folding genes. The absence of a canonical UPR/ISR response is contextual rather than the program itself. Neural FIP200 loss supplies an upstream proteostasis-stress bridge but does not predict the direction of the observed chaperone transcriptional program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Responder neurons down-regulated ion-pump, energy, and synaptic genes, most clearly Atp1a3, Atp1b1, Atp5b, Ckmt1, Eno2, Nrxn1, Glrb, Thy1, Sez6l2, and Tubb4a in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
finding_consequence: This links acute Rb1cc1 loss to neuronal-maintenance transcripts rather than limiting the response to core autophagy genes.
literature_rationale: Coordinated reductions in ion-pump, energetic, cytoskeletal, and synaptic-maintenance transcripts align qualitatively with the neuronal and neurite degeneration directly caused by neural FIP200 deletion. Exact RNA markers and timing are contextual rather than missing mechanistic edges.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Proteasome perturbations Psmc1, Psmb4, Psmc5, and Pomp were the strongest same-direction neighbors of the Rb1cc1 signature, sharing 11-17 of the 23 Rb1cc1 features in matched groups.
finding_consequence: The convergence nominates a generic proteostasis-failure component within the small Rb1cc1 response while making clear that proteasome subunit loss is vastly stronger than Rb1cc1 loss.
literature_rationale: Four highly active proteasome perturbations share predominantly same-direction exact features with Rb1cc1. Target-specific evidence completes both arms of a shared neuronal proteostasis-failure and degeneration chain, supporting restricted convergence without implying transcriptome equivalence.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Rb1cc1 produced only 23 downstream FDR<0.10 gene-by-cell-type features, concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, with a one-gene Dmpk effect in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
finding_consequence: The postmitotic FIP200 loss signature is real but far from a pan-neuronal autophagy transcriptome, so cell-type selectivity is the primary phenotype to interpret.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Rb1cc1 reduced the lysosomal cargo genes Psap and Ctsb in 155 MB Glut but did not induce Sqstm1, Lamp1/2, LC3, or GABARAP transcripts in any responder group.
finding_consequence: The lysosomal arm is selective and repressive, separating the measured RNA state from textbook p62-positive autophagy blockade.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Becn1 and Atg5 partially overlapped Rb1cc1 in 155 MB Glut through Calr, and Becn1 also through Ctsb, whereas Atg16l1 and Sqstm1 did not reproduce the Rb1cc1 responder signature.
finding_consequence: The directly measured autophagy relatives were not interchangeable in this assay, preserving a partial Becn1/Atg5 convergence and a negative Atg16l1/Sqstm1 contrast.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Tsc1 and Tsc2 loss generated broad mTOR/lysosomal signatures in the same Rb1cc1 responder groups, but Mtor, Rptor, Depdc5, Fnip1, and Tbk1 did not phenocopy Rb1cc1.
finding_consequence: Autophagy regulation through TSC-mTOR is transcriptionally separable from acute FIP200 loss in postmitotic neurons.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: U2af2, an RNA-processing perturbation, unexpectedly shared 15 of 23 Rb1cc1 significant features with 14 in the same direction.
finding_consequence: This data-driven neighbor was not a prior autophagy comparator and suggests that the Rb1cc1 state can be embedded in broader RNP/splicing stress responses.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Snap25 perturbation in Pvalb interneurons paired Septin4 down-regulation with Syt7 up-regulation, defining a narrow presynaptic scaffold and calcium-sensor adjustment.
finding_consequence: The directionally split Septin4/Syt7 response nominates a Pvalb-specific presynaptic scaffold/calcium-sensor adjustment after SNAP25 loss rather than a pan-neuronal exocytosis program.
literature_rationale: Functional compatibility within the presynaptic compartment is insufficient to establish a target-specific directional bridge.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: Stxbp1 perturbation produced a substantially broader downstream transcriptome than Snap25 perturbation in matched cortical, Pvalb, and midbrain glutamatergic groups.
finding_consequence: SNAP25 and Munc18-1/STXBP1 should not be treated as interchangeable nodes of one transcriptional response, even though they collaborate during vesicle fusion.
literature_rationale: Shared machinery and physical or functional association do not establish transcriptional interchangeability or a directional breadth comparison.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 052 Pvalb Gaba; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Two non-cortical responder groups showed single-gene feedbacks: Insig1 was induced in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and Ypel4 was induced in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The data do not show a full unfolded-protein or activity program, but they nominate a sterol/ER feedback node and an undercharacterized Ypel4 node as cell-type-restricted outputs of Snap25 loss.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Pvalb interneurons paired Septin4 repression with Syt7 induction after Snap25 perturbation.
finding_consequence: Syt7 encodes a slow Ca2+ sensor for facilitation/asynchronous release and Sept4 has presynaptic-scaffold biology; the two-gene Pvalb response is therefore compatible with a narrow presynaptic compensatory state rather than a generic stress program.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: Snap25 perturbation decreased Atp1a3 and Ldhb in 191 MB P MY GABA neurons.
finding_consequence: ATP1A3 is the neuronal α3 Na+/K+-ATPase and Ldhb reports energy metabolism; their paired down-regulation suggests reduced excitation/ion-pumping demand in this hindbrain GABA group.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The strongest data-driven Snap25 neighbors were V-ATPase/proteasome/endocytic perturbations rather than the textbook SNARE-cycle targets tested in the screen.
finding_consequence: Atp6v0c, Psmc5, and Psmb4 partially converged with Snap25 on Septin4, Ypel4, Atp1a3, and Ldhb, whereas Stx1b, Vamp1, Cplx1, Cplx2, Syp, Syt2, and Syt14 did not reproduce the Snap25 signature.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Ylpm1 perturbation recurrently decreased Inha in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA neurons.
finding_consequence: Inha was the only non-target FDR hit in 191 MB P MY GABA and was also significant in 155 MB Glut, making it a compact marker candidate for Ylpm1 response strength.
literature_rationale: Nuclear localization, binding partners, and downstream-gene annotation do not predict the recurrent decrease in Inha.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Ylpm1 perturbation failed to derepress Tert in the transcriptionally responsive 155 MB Glut surface.
finding_consequence: This cautions against transferring the ES-cell telomerase model directly into post-mitotic brain neurons.
literature_rationale: This is a target-specific directional bridge. The embryonic-stem-cell context limits transportability and therefore confidence, but does not make the bridge incomplete.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The 155 MB Glut response contains a nuclear RNA-processing module: Srsf6 and Srsf5 were down-regulated while Atxn2l was up-regulated, and the weaker 046 CTX-CGE GABA response down-regulated Fam98a.
finding_consequence: This is the part of the screen that best matches YLPM1's nuclear-speckle and RNA-binding/PP1-complex priors, but it appears as a cell-restricted adaptive gene-abundance response rather than a global splicing catastrophe.
literature_rationale: The co-occurring Srsf5/Srsf6/Atxn2l changes support an RNA-processing response in 155 MB Glut, but YLPM1 complex membership does not fully predict the loss-induced transcriptional program. The isolated Fam98a observation in 046 is insufficient for placement of the program there.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: 155 MB Glut up-regulated several ubiquitin/DNA-repair or cullin-adaptor genes after Ylpm1 perturbation: Shprh, Dcaf11, and Ube2o, with Fbxl17 also up in the small 046 response.
finding_consequence: The dominant positive genes are not the canonical Tert target, suggesting a compensatory E3-ligase/protein-quality-control arm in the Ylpm1-sensitive midbrain state.
literature_rationale: Three signed ubiquitin or repair-associated genes form a coherent secondary response in engaged 155 MB Glut, but no YLPM1-specific bridge exists. The singleton Fbxl17 result does not establish the program in 046.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: A structural-scaffold submodule was increased in 155 MB Glut, including Crocc, Jakmip2, and Plec.
finding_consequence: Ylpm1 perturbation also altered large cytoskeletal or scaffold transcripts, broadening the midbrain response beyond nuclear functions and E3-ligase compensation.
literature_rationale: The three concordantly increased scaffold or cytoskeletal-associated transcripts define a small but distinct within-group module. It remains an atlas-derived interpretation because no YLPM1-specific literature bridge was supplied.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: 155 MB Glut showed opposing mitochondrial outer-membrane/MICOS-related changes, with Samm50 up and Chchd7 down.
finding_consequence: This separates the midbrain response from a single RNA-processing story and nominates mitochondrial membrane organization as a secondary Ylpm1-sensitive output.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Ylpm1 loss produced a narrow corrected response: only 4 of 20 measured neuronal groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, with the only multi-gene program in 155 MB Glut.
finding_consequence: The phenotype is not a pan-neuronal collapse of a ubiquitous nuclear-speckle protein; it is a sparse postnatal response concentrated in midbrain glutamatergic neurons plus singletons or doublets in 027, 046, and 191.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut; 046 CTX-CGE GABA; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The canonical Zap3/Ylpm1 embryonic Tert-repression program was absent: Tert had FDR 1.0 in every Ylpm1-tested neuronal group.
finding_consequence: Loss of Ylpm1 at P16 did not derepress the embryonic-stem-cell promoter target that defined Zap3, showing that this postmitotic neuronal assay reads a different biology from the ESC differentiation system.

finding_summary: Literature- or STRING-nominated Ylpm1 neighbors failed to phenocopy: Myc and Cacna1a were flat, Gphn had one cortical hit, Gigyf2 and Smarcc2 responded in other groups, and none shared a corrected Ylpm1 signature row.
finding_consequence: The result rejects a simple model in which postnatal Ylpm1 loss follows Myc/Tert logic or behaves like a generic perturbation of connected nuclear/chromatin network genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Zfx perturbation recurrently reduced Inha and Begain across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, and reduced Arhgef25 across 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
finding_consequence: These markers compress a sparse Zfx phenotype into a candidate panel for validating whether future perturbations engage the same posterior neuronal state.
literature_rationale: General transcription-factor function, stem-cell phenotypes, and unrelated documented ZFX targets do not supply a target-to-observed-effect bridge for this neuronal marker panel.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The only Zfx hit in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA was Cyp46a1 down-regulation, nominating neuronal cholesterol 24-hydroxylase as a fragile hypothalamic biomarker of the perturbation.
finding_consequence: Cyp46a1 makes the hypothalamic GABA response biologically distinct from the Inha/Begain/Arhgef25 caudal core and warns against treating all four effect groups as one uniform state.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Zfx loss produced a real but highly restricted neuronal transcriptomic response: only 4 of 22 measured cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, with 25 total downstream calls and 19 of them in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The screen turns a broadly expressed, stem-cell-essential transcription factor into a postnatal neuronal result: Zfx is not a pan-neuronal transcriptional dependency after P16, but four caudal neuron groups retain a small Zfx-sensitive program.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Within 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Zfx loss coupled neuronal signaling genes to cilium/centrosome and trafficking/metabolic genes: Prrg3, Npr2, Nalcn, Cibar1, Cep250, Cenpv, Mvb12b, Tmem147, Flvcr1, Apoo, Pcca, and Zmynd11 were down, while Cdh18 and Ift80 were up.
finding_consequence: This finding keeps the 151 response from being flattened into a generic transcription-factor story; the actual postmitotic signature is a small, mixed architecture/trafficking program rather than wholesale activation of apoptosis or unfolded-protein stress.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The data-driven Zfx neighbors were not canonical stem-cell cofactors: Naa20 was the top positive neighbor with 13 same-direction overlaps, and Tpr, Xpo1, and the broad splicing perturbation Srsf1 converged on subsets of the same down-regulated Zfx genes.
finding_consequence: The cross-perturbation result reframes the Zfx signature as lying near a general RNA-processing/nuclear-transport/Naa20 vulnerability axis in caudal neurons, not just in a ZFX-specific transcriptional circuit.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The strongest robust negative neighbors, Yy1 and Naa15, reversed several 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Zfx-down genes, whereas E2F/MYC/SOX2/ESRRB comparators from the literature network failed to reproduce the 25-gene Zfx signature.
finding_consequence: This contrast prevents an incorrect shortcut from Zfx to the textbook MYC/E2F/stemness network and shows that the nearest postnatal neuronal signatures were screen-nominated, not the obvious stem-cell partners.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Hspa5 perturbation induced an ER chaperone and ERAD program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, including Hsp90b1, Pdia4, Derl3, Creld2, Sel1l, and Herpud1.
finding_consequence: The dataset response lands on the expected BiP/UPR biology, but the corrected signal is sharply concentrated in one thalamic glutamatergic population rather than uniformly present wherever Hspa5 was sampled.
literature_rationale: A neuronal Hspa5 deletion study directly reported induction of GRP94, PDI, CHOP, and GADD34, while mechanistic references place BiP upstream of UPR activation. This directly predicts the observed Hsp90b1, Pdia4, Derl3, Creld2, Sel1l, and Herpud1 program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Hspa5 perturbation induced a mild adaptive amino-acid/ISR program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, anchored by FDR-supported Asns, Slc38a2, and Vars, without establishing a robust terminal Ddit3-Chac1 response.
finding_consequence: This suggests that Hspa5-axis stress in this neuronal context is read out not only as a compensatory chaperone/ERAD program but also as nutrient-redox and ATF4-linked stress that could become maladaptive if sustained.
literature_rationale: The supplied references support the chain from BiP impairment through UPR activation to an ATF4/CHOP-associated stress response. This agrees with induction of the adaptive amino-acid/ISR program and does not require a robust terminal Ddit3-Chac1 response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The strongest full-surface convergences came from glycoprotein-biogenesis and ER-translocation perturbations rather than from ATF6 itself.
finding_consequence: Gfpt1 and Dhdds, which sit in hexosamine and dolichol-dependent glycoprotein biogenesis, and Sec63, a BiP-linked translocation factor, re-induced the same thalamic Hspa5 ER/ISR genes. The convergence ties Hspa5 to nascent ER client load in neurons.
literature_rationale: Gfpt1, Dhdds, and Sec63 are informative in 151 and reproduce coherent ER/ISR components of the Hspa5 response. Their established roles in glycosylation, ER client handling, and BiP-coupled translocation complete the mechanistic chains. No supported overlap places the focal convergence in 145, and weak ancillary comparators are excluded.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Hspa5 loss activated an ER chaperone/ERAD module selectively in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: BiP/HSPA5 is expected to buffer unfolded proteins; the measured induction of Hsp90b1, Pdia4, Derl3, Herpud1, Sel1l and Creld2 shows that the screen recovered the canonical transcriptional consequence of insufficient ER folding capacity, but only in one thalamic glutamatergic population.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Hspa5 perturbation also recruited an ER/endomembrane redox-trafficking adaptation in 151 TH cells.
finding_consequence: Cyb5r1, Gosr2, Pi4k2a, Lrrc59 and Ankrd13c up-regulation extends the response beyond textbook chaperones toward ER membrane redox balance, vesicular traffic and ubiquitin-linked membrane sorting, consistent with homeostatic remodeling of a stressed ER.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Small negative neuronal-gene responses occurred outside the main ER-program group.
finding_consequence: Erc1 was the strongest down-regulated gene in 151 TH, Gnao1 and Nmnat2 were down in 145 MH-LH TH, and Ptprs was the sole significant 308 CB GABA gene, suggesting that ER-chaperone stress can be accompanied by local synaptic or axonal transcriptional weakening without a pan-neuronal shutdown.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Hspa5 was not a pan-neuronal transcriptional trigger under basal P16-to-P37/44 perturbation.
finding_consequence: Only 3 of 19 measured cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and the one broad response was in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut. This confines acute Hspa5 LoF sensitivity to a minority of captured neuronal states in this assay.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: ATF6 and MANF did not phenocopy Hspa5, and Hsp-family perturbations split by compartment.
finding_consequence: Atf6 had no significant matched-group response, Manf mostly induced only Hspa5/Pdia6, Hspa8 and Hsp90ab1 did not share the Hspa5 ER signature, and Hspa9 produced a much broader mitochondrial-stress/ISR surface. Hspa5’s neuronal program is therefore a BiP/ER-client-load response, not a generic Hsp70-family or ATF6-loss signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Pcyt2 perturbation decreased the neurosecretory peptide-processing genes Cpe and Pcsk2 in the same thalamic neurons that induced the sterol program.
finding_consequence: Human PCYT2 disease affects the brain, but prior lipidomic studies emphasize etherlipids; this dataset nominates a neuron-specific Cpe/Pcsk2 decrease as a possible downstream consequence of PCYT2-pathway stress.
literature_rationale: The lipid-function and peptide-processing annotations describe the two ends separately; they do not supply a target-specific bridge between them.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Pcyt2 loss induced a coordinated Srebf2-centered cholesterol synthesis and uptake transcriptional program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, including Insig1, Srebf2, Ldlr, Hmgcr, Hmgcs1, Sqle, Cyp51, Fdft1, and multiple terminal sterol enzymes.
finding_consequence: The screen does not mainly report the canonical PE enzyme genes; it reports a cholesterol-supply rescue in one thalamic glutamatergic state, with Insig1, Cyp51, Nsdhl, Msmo1, Fdft1, Ldlr, Hmgcr, Idi1, Hmgcs1, Sqle, Dhcr24, Dhcr7, and Srebf2 up at FDR<0.10.
literature_rationale: The coherent local sterol program is load-bearing transcriptomic biology. The unsupported near-exclusive thalamic clause is removed because cross-group engagement and power do not establish selectivity; literature links PCYT2 to membrane-lipid homeostasis but does not complete the signed PCYT2-loss-to-SREBF2 activation chain.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The sterol module was accompanied by a smaller fatty-acyl remodeling arm in the same thalamic cells.
finding_consequence: Fads2, Scd2, and Acsl3 up-regulation is consistent with a membrane lipid-remodeling interpretation rather than a cholesterol-only effect, and follows lipidomic literature showing that PCYT2 deficiency remodels phospholipid acyl chains.
literature_rationale: The coordinated fatty-acyl remodeling arm occurs within the powered group-151 response and directly matches qualitative remodeling after PCYT2 deficiency. Exact transcript signs and cellular restriction are contextual details.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Selenoi, the downstream ethanolamine phosphotransferase screened in this panel, recapitulated the Pcyt2 direction weakly but specifically in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: This same-pathway convergence links the Pcyt2 sterol pulse to the CDP-ethanolamine-to-PE branch rather than to an unrelated guide effect.
literature_rationale: Although Selenoi has only four local hits, three form a coherent same-direction sterol overlap. Consecutive positions of PCYT2 and SELENOI in PE synthesis provide a complete pathway-level convergence chain.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The largest same-direction neighbors were not Kennedy-pathway enzymes but endomembrane and trafficking regulators that re-induced the same sterol module.
finding_consequence: Dctn1, Chp1, Rab7, Mib1, Marchf6, Tsc1, and Tsc2 convergence makes the Pcyt2 output look like a shared endomembrane lipid-homeostasis state in thalamic neurons rather than an isolated Pcyt2 fingerprint.
literature_rationale: The principal group-151 comparators have active response surfaces and substantial coherent sterol overlap, so convergence remains interpretable. Group 145 lacks the focal program, Tsc2 is supported mainly by geometry, and target-specific bridges are unavailable for several generalized members.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Srebf2 loss inverted the Pcyt2 sterol response in the same cell group, whereas the two most negative restricted-cosine neighbors did not.
finding_consequence: The opposite signed Dhcr24/Insig1/Hmgcs1/Msmo1/Cyp51/Sqle response turns Srebf2 into a genetic sign check for the Pcyt2-induced cholesterol program and prevents over-reading Eif4g1 or Auts2 anti-correlations that vanish at the FDR-overlap layer.
literature_rationale: The claim survives after narrowing to the coherent Pcyt2–Srebf2 inversion in group 151. The Eif4g1 and Auts2 cosine anti-neighbors and group 145 placement are excluded because they lack an informative FDR-level relationship; literature establishes only the Srebf2 side of the inversion.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Pcyt2 did not induce a transcriptional Kennedy-pathway replacement program or a canonical ISR/UPR/autophagy program.
finding_consequence: The data point away from transcriptional up-regulation of Etnk/Cept/Selenoi/Pisd/Pcyt1 genes as the acute neuronal compensation and toward SREBF2 output plus off-transcriptome lipid remodeling.
literature_rationale: Group 151 is locally informative and directly supports absence of a transcriptional Kennedy-pathway replacement program, consistent with compensation through remodeling and reduced turnover. The underpowered groups and broader unsupported ISR/UPR generalization are excluded.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Other screened lipid relatives did not phenocopy Pcyt2 in the responding thalamic cells.
finding_consequence: Agps and Far1 from ether-lipid synthesis and Hmgcr, Srebf1, and Acsl4 from sterol/fatty-acid biology were flat or nearly flat, indicating that the Pcyt2 response is not a generic consequence of perturbing any lipid enzyme in these neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Depdc5 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut recovers an mTORC1-disinhibition module shared with Tsc1 and Tsc2.
finding_consequence: Tsc1 and Tsc2 were the top two unbiased positive neighbors and shared 13/23 and 11/23 Depdc5 FDR<0.10 genes in the same direction, anchoring the weak Depdc5 signature to the expected mTORC1 axis.
literature_rationale: Active Tsc1 and Tsc2 responses share substantial, concordant FDR-level programs with Depdc5 in the same group. The complete convergence of GATOR1 and TSC regulatory arms on mTORC1 supports the coarse same-direction relationship.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: A compact sterol/SREBP-like transcript set marks Depdc5-active 151 neurons.
finding_consequence: Induction of Ldlr, Insig1, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, Dhcr7, and Cyp51 supplies a nuclear RNA biomarker candidate for mTORC1 activation in a single-nucleus assay where the canonical readout, S6/4E-BP phosphorylation, was unmeasured.
literature_rationale: Six concordantly induced sterol genes form a coherent RNA program and recur under informative Tsc1/Tsc2 perturbations. DEPDC5 loss-to-mTORC1 disinhibition and neuronal mTORC1-to-sterol transcription provide a complete supporting chain.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Depdc5 also reduces a small RNA-processing/nuclear RNA module in 151.
finding_consequence: Down-regulated Rnpc3, Srrm2, Zcchc7, and Snhg11 show that the responder is not a pure lipid signature; RNA-processing genes are part of the measured secondary state.
literature_rationale: Four compatibly decreased nuclear RNA-processing transcripts support a compact secondary program rather than isolated markers. General mTORC1-dependent splicing regulation does not predict this signed mammalian neuronal transcript set, leaving a consequential specific edge incomplete.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Structural and synaptic-adhesion transcripts increase after Depdc5 loss in 151 neurons.
finding_consequence: Tubb3, Tubb4b, Clstn3, Sparcl1, and Adgrb1 provide a transcriptional bridge to published Depdc5 knockdown phenotypes affecting dendrites, soma size, and excitatory synapses, but in a thalamic class rather than the usual cortical models.
literature_rationale: The concordantly increased structural and synaptic-support set is a distinct secondary program. Direct Depdc5 knockdown produces enhanced neuronal growth and excitatory synaptic phenotypes in the same qualitative direction; exact transcripts and thalamic placement are contextual details.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The strongest negative neighbors are stress and organelle perturbations, not GATOR1 relatives.
finding_consequence: Got1, Mdh1, Dnm1l, and Atp6v0c oppose the Depdc5 151 signature and often flip structural genes such as Tubb3/Tubb4b, separating mTORC1-disinhibition from ISR-like mitochondrial or V-ATPase loss states in the same neuronal class.
literature_rationale: The load-bearing relationship is narrowed to the active Atp6v0c comparator: V-ATPase activity promotes Rag–mTORC1 signaling, whereas Depdc5 loss disinhibits it, completing an inverse mechanistic chain. Got1 is weak and the broader GOT1/MDH1/DNM1L generalization lacks equivalent target-specific support.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Pik3r1 and Pik3r3 are the strongest Depdc5-induced genes and recur in Tsc1/Tsc2 signatures.
finding_consequence: Up-regulation of PI3K regulatory subunits is a candidate feedback or buffering response to mTORC1 disinhibition, not merely a generic stress response, because it appears in Depdc5 and the TSC comparators.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The Depdc5 transcriptional response is sharply concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: Only 1 of 20 measured Depdc5 cell groups exceeded FDR<0.10, despite measurable Depdc5 transcript in all 20; this makes the thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c class the screen-defined locus of postnatal transcriptional sensitivity.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Depdc5 resembles loss of mTORC1 inhibitors more than loss of adjacent PI3K/Akt or core mTORC1 genes.
finding_consequence: Tsc1/Tsc2 converge, Pten is partial, Mtor is one of the top negative neighbors, and Rptor, Pik3ca, Pik3r1, Pik3r2, Akt3, Fnip1, and Atg5 do not phenocopy Depdc5 in 151; the screen therefore resolves direction and branch position within a broad mTOR pathway.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Ptpa LoF produced its clearest transcriptional response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with a 15-gene signature enriched for RNA/RNP factors such as Ccnl2, Dusp11, Rbm39, Son, Snrnp70, and R3hdm1.
finding_consequence: This names the only multi-gene Ptpa response and shows that the postnatal neuronal output is a small compensatory RNA-processing signature, not a pan-neuronal PP2A-collapse program.
literature_rationale: The small but multi-gene RNA/RNP response can be retained as a local program, while its apparent 151 selectivity is not interpretable because 151 is highly response-prone and the signature is low-range. No specific literature bridge supports the program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Ptpa did not phenocopy the PP2A scaffold Ppp2r1a, while PP2A B-subunit perturbations Ppp2r2b and Ppp2r5d were flat in the Ptpa-responsive cell groups.
finding_consequence: This directly rejects a simple same-complex equivalence model and shows that the assay can detect PP2A-complex disruption after P16 when the core scaffold is hit.
literature_rationale: The corrected claim is the informative breadth divergence between engaged Ptpa and the highly active Ppp2r1a scaffold perturbation in 151. Flat Ppp2r2b and Ppp2r5d arms cannot support non-phenocopy and are excluded.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Outside 151 TH, Ptpa yielded only ultrafocal FDR-supported effects: Agrn down in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Leng8 and Ece2 down with Ifrd1 up in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and Mbd6 up in 155 MB Glut.
finding_consequence: The one- to three-gene calls preserve real cell-class restriction without inflating them into full pathways.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The top data-driven Ptpa neighbors were non-PP2A targets: Kmt2e, Tbx21, and Usp48 were same-sign, and Serpinb6a, Traf3, and Ift88 were opposite-sign on the restricted Ptpa top-100 signature.
finding_consequence: It records the unbiased comparator result while showing that the Ptpa signature is too small for an FDR-level shared module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The 151 response combined RNP remodeling with reduced neuronal membrane/synaptic genes, including Atp1b2, Wls, and Nrxn1, plus metabolic transporter/lipid genes Slc25a3, Slc29a1, and Tecr.
finding_consequence: The significant genes point to a weak secondary after-state of thalamic neurons rather than a direct phosphatase substrate list.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Ptpa failed to recover PI3K-TSC-mTOR, Gsk3b, Akt3, or Mapt transcriptomes in its responder groups, even though Pten, Tsc1, and Tsc2 were strong in matched thalamic or midbrain glutamatergic cells.
finding_consequence: The expected PP2A signaling neighborhood was measurable in the screen but did not appear after Ptpa loss, supporting a phosphorylation-first or thresholded model for PTPA rather than a canonical kinase-pathway RNA state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut

finding_summary: The strongest 151 and 155 responses were a uniformly up-regulated junction, polarity, and vesicle-trafficking module marked by Ap1m2, Stxbp2, F11r, Patj, Spint2, Cdc42bpg, Hook2, St3gal4, Kdf1, and Epha1.
finding_consequence: Loss of a transcriptional repressor derepressed an epithelial-like trafficking/junction program in mature neurons rather than generating a broad neuronal injury signature.
literature_rationale: Direct Zeb1 loss or down-regulation studies document same-direction derepression of polarity and epithelial genes, including in neuronal progenitors. The recurrent Stxbp2 edge is experiment-specific, but exact marker overlap is unnecessary for the directly supported coarse program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Ctbp1, a known ZEB1 corepressor partner, was the only robust data-driven phenocopy: it was the top positive neighbor and reproduced same-direction Stxbp2, F11r, Ap1m2, St3gal4, Hook2, and Usp43 induction in the matched 151 or 145 groups.
finding_consequence: The strongest cross-perturbation result connects the postnatal TH signature to the ZEB1-CTBP repression axis rather than to an unrelated guide artifact.
literature_rationale: Ctbp1 is active on the relevant surface and reproduces multiple exact same-direction program features. Its established role as a direct ZEB1 corepressor completes the coarse loss-convergence chain.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Stxbp2 was the most recurrent Zeb1-responsive transcript, significant in 145, 151, 155, and 191, with Patj and Ap1m2 recurring in smaller subsets.
finding_consequence: Stxbp2 provides a compact readout of the TH/MB Zeb1 state and separates the effect groups from the many flat groups better than the Zeb1 transcript itself.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Zeb1 loss produced a real but highly restricted P16 neuronal response: 23 significant downstream gene-cell pairs were confined to five thalamic, hypothalamic, midbrain, and pineal-adjacent groups, while every cortical, hippocampal, striatal, and cerebellar group had zero FDR<0.10 genes.
finding_consequence: The screen does not recover the textbook embryonic cortical phenotype broadly; it nominates a postmitotic TH/MB-biased competence state instead.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: The expected paralog/EMT/Wnt/developmental relatives did not phenocopy Zeb1: Zeb2, Smad3, Smarca4, Cdh2, Twist1, Snai2, Twist2, Tcf3, Tcf4, Pak3, and Neurod1 had zero exact FDR<0.10 overlaps with the Zeb1 23-feature signature, and Ctnnb1 was broad but mostly orthogonal.
finding_consequence: Zeb1's TH/MB module is not a generic ZEB-family, TGFβ/EMT, Wnt, or neuronal-differentiation response; the CTBP1 match is selective.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: Flnb down-regulation distinguished Adarb1 perturbation from engaged Adar and Gria2 perturbations in matched neuronal contexts.
finding_consequence: Even with target engagement of Adar or Gria2 in comparator classes, Flnb did not fall, separating the Adarb1 signature from ADAR1 loss and from loss of a central ADAR2-edited receptor transcript.
literature_rationale: The literature makes the selected targets and comparators biologically specific, but it does not establish the directional abundance contrast.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Adarb1 perturbation did not change the abundance of canonical edited receptor and channel transcripts, despite producing a detectable recurrent Flnb response.
finding_consequence: The absence of Gria2, Grik2, Htr2c, Gabra3 and Kcna1 abundance changes argues that the dataset is not reading out loss of receptor editing as receptor transcript loss; edited-site sequencing would be required for that canonical mechanism.
literature_rationale: An editing-centered mechanism is compatible with unchanged transcript abundance, but compatibility alone does not decisively predict the tested absence.

finding_summary: Adarb1 loss produced a sparse but recurrent Flnb-down response in 13 neuronal cell groups, with the largest Flnb effects in thalamic/midbrain/posterior classes.
finding_consequence: The postmitotic snRNA phenotype was not a generic seizure or stress transcriptome; it nominated Filamin B abundance as the dominant cell-autonomous output of Adarb1 perturbation in this screen.
literature_rationale: There is a direct target-to-Flnb molecular bridge, but its documented endpoint is editing rather than the signed abundance program measured here.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut; 052 Pvalb Gaba; 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 217 P MY Pineal Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: The closest positive Adarb1 neighbors over its 19 significant feature rows were Naa20, Uba5 and Xpo1, driven mainly by same-direction Flnb down-regulation.
finding_consequence: This empirical module is not the textbook ADAR pathway; it shows that several perturbations outside RNA editing converge on the same Flnb/filamin expression state in matched neuronal cell groups.

finding_summary: Naa15 and Wdr26 inverted robust parts of the Adarb1 filamin/Zfp941 signature, whereas Zfp804a was inverse only by the restricted score and had no robust shared feature.
finding_consequence: The same sparse Adarb1 feature set is bidirectional across the screen: Naa15 increased Flnb and Flna in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while Wdr26 increased Flnb and Zfp941 in 191 MB P MY GABA.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Literature-obvious comparators did not phenocopy Adarb1: Adar, Flnb, and eight edited receptor-subunit targets had zero robust overlaps with the 19 Adarb1 feature rows.
finding_consequence: The Adarb1 transcriptional signature is separable from general ADAR-family loss, direct Flnb perturbation, and knockout of individual known edited receptor transcripts; it is therefore a specific post-perturbation state rather than a simple receptor-subunit LoF signature.

finding_summary: Creb1 loss induced Crem where matched perturbations of several upstream cAMP, NMDA-receptor, and CaMK inputs did not.
finding_consequence: Although PKA, Ca2+/CaMK, and glutamatergic signaling converge on CREB phosphorylation, efficient Prkaca, Camk2b, Grin2b, Grin2a, and Adcy3 perturbations did not recreate the Creb1-to-Crem signature in the same classes, arguing that the signal is a CREB-family identity or compensation response rather than simple loss of upstream drive.
literature_rationale: The ledger supports direct Creb1-to-Crem compensation and separately documents upstream signaling into CREB. It does not decisively predict the negative comparator arm that distinguishes Creb1 identity loss from reduced upstream drive.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Creb1 loss did not induce or suppress the canonical basal activity-dependent CREB target program despite recurrent detection of Crem compensation.
finding_consequence: The absence of Arc, Bdnf, Fos/Jun, Egr, Npas4, Nr4a1, Per1, and Vgf responses separates this perturbation state from the canonical stimulated pCREB immediate-early program.
literature_rationale: The references establish activity- and calcium-dependent CREB signaling, not that chronic Creb1 perturbation must alter this panel at baseline. The observed tested absence therefore refines the context without constituting disagreement.

finding_summary: Creb1 loss induces Crem in 155 MB Glut, reproducing the established compensatory CREM response to neuronal CREB1 deletion.
finding_consequence: The midbrain glutamatergic response preserves the CREM-feedback axis but adds a different, smaller calcium-kinase/metabolic trace rather than the 151 TH organelle module.
literature_rationale: Creb disruption directly caused CREM overexpression across tissues, and conditional neuronal Creb1 deletion directly induced Crem in dopaminergic midbrain neurons. This predicts the recurrent Crem increase after Creb1 perturbation; broader neuronal-group recurrence affects transportability, not the target-to-effect bridge.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Creb1 loss induces Crem as the most recurrent robust transcriptional response, but only in five hypothalamic, thalamic, midbrain, and brainstem-enriched groups.
finding_consequence: The dominant product of this sparse postnatal LoF is not a global collapse of CREB target genes; it is a lineage-restricted rise of a paralogous CRE-family transcription factor that can buffer CREB biology.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut population is the only broad Creb1 responder, coupling Crem induction to down-regulation of ER, lipid, lysosomal, heme, and vesicle genes.
finding_consequence: This cell class converts CREB1 loss into a small but coherent organelle-homeostasis signature, showing that the Creb1 effect surface is not just one-gene CREM feedback everywhere.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Directly measured CBP/p300 and NMDA/TrkB/PKA/CaMK/ERK comparators do not phenocopy Creb1 in its responder groups.
finding_consequence: The Creb1 signature is not a simple readout of every canonical CREB coactivator or upstream kinase perturbation: Crebbp overlaps only on Stxbp2 in the opposite direction, Ep300 is flat, and Grin1/Ntrk2/Prkaca/Camk4/Mapk1 do not induce Crem.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The unsupervised whole-screen neighbors of Creb1 are very weak and fail the FDR-overlap test.
finding_consequence: A full-screen correlation nominated Mff, Sucla2, Serpinb6a, Cckar, Lgi1, and Ndufs8 rather than textbook CREB relatives, but all lacked exact shared responder-gene hits; Creb1 therefore has a small idiosyncratic signature rather than belonging to a broad recurrent module.

finding_summary: Fto loss did not produce an FDR-supported Bdnf/Ntrk transcriptional program in the assayed mature neuronal response surface.
finding_consequence: Prior Fto-loss studies in adult neurogenesis reported altered BDNF-pathway components, so this negative result confines that mechanism by assay and cell state rather than identifying it as a universal mature-neuron transcriptional output.
literature_rationale: The dataset recovered a distinct Fto-associated RNA-processing response, making the targeted absence informative rather than attributable solely to failed perturbation. The conflict is transportability-limited because the prior study involved adult neurogenesis contexts.

finding_summary: Fto repeatedly repressed the RNA-processing gene Rsrp1 and perturbed a small spliceosomal/RNA-binding module including Rnpc3, Zcchc7, Dazap1, Ccnl2, and Ddx24.
finding_consequence: The recurrence of Rsrp1 across three cell groups and the presence of several RNA-processing genes connect the sparse neuronal phenotype to FTO's methylated-RNA biology rather than to an isolated one-gene artifact.
literature_rationale: FTO deficiency directly alters snRNA methylation, snRNA abundance, and alternative splicing, completing the chain to the recurrent RNA-processing response. Exact markers, signs, and neuronal distribution are not required for program agreement.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: On the restricted 22-entry Fto signature, Snrnp70 was the top same-direction neighbor and Fus the strongest opposing neighbor.
finding_consequence: The data-driven comparison shows that Fto is embedded in an RNA-processing response surface but also that the signature is directional: it is not generic to every RNA-binding or splicing perturbation.
literature_rationale: Both comparators are active on the measured surface: Snrnp70 supplies supported positive convergence, while Fus supplies a coherent opposite-direction relationship. The focal directional discrimination is informative, but no Fto-specific source predicts either comparator relationship.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Slirp was the sole FDR<0.10 response in CNU-HYa/HY GABA neurons, rising 0.79 logFC.
finding_consequence: This isolates a candidate mitochondrial RNA/chaperone compensation marker for a hypothalamic GABA Fto response that would be missed by averaging only the stronger thalamic and midbrain-glutamate groups.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Fto produced a sparse, region-selective response after P16 neuronal CRISPR: 22 FDR<0.10 downstream gene×cell calls across five measured responder groups and no signal in most cortical, hippocampal, and forebrain GABAergic groups.
finding_consequence: This is the central phenotype. FTO is a broadly expressed RNA demethylase, but its acute postmitotic LoF effect in this screen was not broad; the real signal concentrated in thalamic and midbrain-associated cell groups.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Fto up-regulated Rnpc3 in 155 MB Glut, but direct Rnpc3 perturbation caused a much broader matched-cell response, consistent with compensatory Rnpc3 induction rather than an Rnpc3-loss phenocopy.
finding_consequence: This prevents a misleading same-pathway interpretation: Fto may be nudging minor-spliceosome capacity as a response to RNA methylation stress, not copying the state caused by knocking down a core minor-spliceosome factor.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The screened m6A readers Hnrnpc and Hnrnpa2b1 and the AlkB-family enzyme Alkbh8 did not reproduce the Fto signature in matched responder groups.
finding_consequence: Fto's neuronal response is not interchangeable with the available methylated-RNA reader or AlkB-family perturbations; this narrows the phenotype to a selective FTO-linked RNA-processing branch.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: A small TH Prkcd proteostasis/ER-phagy sliver accompanied the RNA-processing response: Ccpg1 and Vbp1 were induced while Ppib and Wsb1 were repressed.
finding_consequence: The responder surface is not purely canonical m6A biology; it contains a weak secondary stress/turnover signature that could mark adaptive proteostasis after disturbed RNA processing.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The TH Prkcd responder included a small neuronal signaling/trafficking component, including Kcnj3 down and Camk2d and Trim46 up.
finding_consequence: Kcnj3 encodes a GIRK-channel subunit in the same general channel family implicated by FTO loss in dopaminergic D2-like receptor physiology, raising a cautious candidate link to neuronal excitability outside dopamine neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: P16 neuronal Fto LoF did not recover the adipocyte-browning, BDNF/neurogenesis, or dopamine-marker programs that dominate major FTO organismal priors.
finding_consequence: The result warns against treating this perturbation as a mouse-brain proxy for the common human FTO obesity allele or for systemic Fto-null phenotypes; those effects are displaced to other alleles, lineages, or modalities.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 215 MB Dopa

finding_summary: In Pvalb interneurons, Scn1b perturbation selectively up-regulated Slc4a10, a Na+-coupled bicarbonate exchanger that can tune neuronal pH and excitability.
finding_consequence: A sodium-coupled pH transporter is a plausible compensatory sentinel for a Nav beta-subunit perturbation, but the single-gene signature argues for a narrow ion-homeostasis response rather than a full fast-spiking interneuron state change.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: The only thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c Scn1b downstream hit was Jun up-regulation, and Grin1 perturbation independently up-regulated Jun in the same class.
finding_consequence: Among the otherwise weak whole-screen neighbors, Jun is the one robust shared responder, nominating an AP-1 immediate-early/excitability-stress node that can be reached from both Nav beta-1 and NMDA-receptor perturbation in this thalamic population.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Scn1b loss up-regulated the adhesion/axon-wiring receptor Celsr3 in MB P MY GABA neurons.
finding_consequence: Celsr3 provides a single-gene bridge between beta-1 cell-adhesion biology and developmental wiring genes, suggesting a possible adult survivor compensation marker in a brainstem/midbrain inhibitory population.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The CNU-HYa/HY GABA response was a Cd2bp2 decrease with no FDR-supported ion-channel, AP-1, or adhesion cohort.
finding_consequence: This preserves a real but noncanonical responder instead of forcing every Scn1b effect into sodium-channel biology; it may mark a local spliceosome/RNA-processing vulnerability or a single-gene false-context signal that needs validation.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: The all-transcriptome nearest neighbors of Scn1b were extremely weak and mostly non-Nav targets; Grin1 was the only top positive neighbor with a robust shared Scn1b feature.
finding_consequence: The neighbor analysis argues that the four-gene Scn1b surface is idiosyncratic rather than a missed member of a large recurrent stress, mitochondrial, or synaptic-downregulation module.

finding_summary: Canonical sodium-channel partners did not phenocopy Scn1b: Scn1a, Scn2a, Scn3a, Scn8a, Scn9a, Fgf13, and Fgf14 were flat or near-flat, while Ank3 caused a broad thalamic program that regulated Jun in the opposite direction.
finding_consequence: Direct cross-perturbation measurement separates biochemical Nav-channel relatedness from transcriptomic equivalence in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, engaged Atp9a loss remained downstream-transcriptionally quiet while Rab7 and Vps35 perturbations produced multi-gene endolysosomal responses.
finding_consequence: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut population can mount a strong endolysosomal RNA response after other trafficking perturbations, but Atp9a loss did not phenocopy those neighbors.
literature_rationale: The references provide a specific ATP9A-to-endosomal-trafficking bridge, but not the transcriptional consequence needed to predict whether engaged Atp9a loss should remain quiet or resemble the comparator perturbations.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Atp9a perturbation in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut selectively up-regulated Rnf41, an E3 ubiquitin ligase involved in receptor and innate-signaling protein turnover.
finding_consequence: The only corrected hippocampal-family DEG points to ubiquitin-dependent receptor/signaling remodeling rather than to direct induction of the canonical RAB5/RAB11 or Wntless machinery.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut

finding_summary: Atp9a perturbation in 053 Sst Gaba selectively down-regulated Sc5d, the lathosterol oxidase step of cholesterol biosynthesis.
finding_consequence: This is a cell-type-restricted hint that a membrane-trafficking flippase lesion can feed back onto neuronal sterol synthesis in Sst interneurons, but the assay recovered only Sc5d rather than a complete cholesterol pathway.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba

finding_summary: The expected flippase/retromer relatives did not phenocopy Atp9a: Atp8a2 and Vps35 responded in different cell classes, while Atp11c and Dip2b were transcriptionally flat.
finding_consequence: The one-gene CA3 and Sst Atp9a hits are therefore not a generic P4-ATPase or retromer signature in this screen, and Vps35 demonstrates that endosomal pathway genes could produce corrected DE when the assayed cell context was permissive.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut; 053 Sst Gaba; 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: In TH Prkcd/Grin2c neurons, Med13 and Med15 partially reproduced the Med23-downregulated neuronal module, whereas Med12 and Cdk8 did not.
finding_consequence: The result argues that physical membership in Mediator is not sufficient to predict an interchangeable Perturb-seq phenotype in this neuronal state.
literature_rationale: Mediator membership alone is insufficient to predict transcriptomic convergence. The comparative Med23-versus-Med15 neural-differentiation result concerns a different phenotype and does not bridge the specific thalamic module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The responsive Med23 thalamic surface lacked the JUN/FOS immediate-early program associated with MED23 R617Q models and instead showed a synaptic-receptor and adhesion program.
finding_consequence: The dataset points to synaptic-receptor and adhesion genes as a mature-neuron consequence of Med23 perturbation while leaving the canonical R617Q immediate-early-gene mechanism context-dependent.
literature_rationale: The literature provides a specific MED23-to-IEG mechanism, but its relevant signed readout is impaired induction after stimulation. An acute loss perturbation without such a challenge is not informative for failure to recapitulate that response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Med23 loss produced a predominantly downward molecular program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut involving synaptic receptors, adhesion, ion channels, and calcium-handling transcripts.
finding_consequence: Only one glutamatergic class carried a multi-gene response, and 19 of 20 significant genes moved downward, arguing for a selective postmitotic thalamic state rather than global collapse of RNAPII transcription after an acute Mediator perturbation.
literature_rationale: The positive program changes biological interpretation beyond DEG breadth and survives removal of the unsupported selective-state claim. Literature supplies only an incomplete bridge to broader neuronal-program withdrawal.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The strongest non-Mediator neighbors of Med23 were proteasome and v-ATPase perturbations that were far broader yet drove the same TH/Pvalb coordinates in the same direction.
finding_consequence: The Med23 endpoint shares a vulnerable neuronal-state module with Atp6v0c, Psmb4 and Psmc5 rather than looking like an isolated ELK1 immediate-early signature.
