literature_rationale: Direct UFSP2-deficiency evidence supports increased mitochondrial machinery and respiration, matching the mitochondrial adaptation. The coordinated vesicle and trafficking decreases lack a supplied target-specific bridge and are excluded from the focal literature-linked claim.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Ufsp2 did not induce the broad Ddit3/Sqstm1-containing stress program that appeared after upstream Uba5 or Ufc1 perturbation.
finding_consequence: The same snRNA assay detected UFM1-cycle transcription when the E1/E2 conjugation machinery was hit, so the weak Ufsp2 phenotype reflects pathway-position buffering rather than absence of assay sensitivity to UFM1 biology.
literature_rationale: The two engaged Ufsp2 responder groups informatively lack the RNA UPR program predicted by direct UFSP2-knockout neuronal evidence, while active Uba5 and Ufc1 comparators demonstrate assay detection of pathway stress. Group 145 is comparator context, not an Ufsp2 positive placement.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Pink1 was selectively up-regulated in the smaller 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response together with Tmsb4x up-regulation and Sema6b/C1qtnf4 down-regulation.
finding_consequence: Pink1 gives the thalamic glutamatergic response a mitochondrial-quality-control marker that is not part of a broad Ddit3/Hspa5 ER-stress state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Ufsp2 produced a narrow two-cell-type response, with 16 FDR<0.10 genes in 155 MB Glut and 4 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while 19 measured groups had zero robust downstream genes.
finding_consequence: The primary phenotype is a restricted postnatal neuronal effect rather than a ubiquitous ER-stress response, and the numerous flat groups are part of the biology rather than a failed target-transcript knockdown call.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The 151 signature was predominantly de-repressive but noncanonical: 17 of 18 FDR<0.10 genes increased, including Ptgds, Capn3, Col9a3, Usp11, Zmynd8, Hexim2, Kcnk4, Slc12a8, Spag5, and Ache, while only Zfp2 decreased.
finding_consequence: The sign pattern fits loss of an H3K4-demethylating repressor, whereas the gene identities point to a local thalamic program mixing chromatin/transcriptional feedback with extracellular/lipid and excitability-linked genes rather than a global REST-target burst.
literature_rationale: The strong internal bias toward increased expression is the same derepressive effect directly documented after KDM5C loss. Exact thalamic genes and occupancy are experiment-specific details, while the single responding cell group is descriptive placement.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The Kdm5c 19-gene restricted signature nominated Zmynd8, not Kdm5b or Rest, as its top same-direction neighbor; Zmynd8 perturbation reproduced 13 Kdm5c FDR genes in the same direction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: This converts a nominal list of thalamic Kdm5c DE genes into a cross-perturbation module and elevates Zmynd8, Usp11, Hexim2, and the Ptgds/Capn3/Spag5/Kcnk4 cluster as a reproducible chromatin-linked output.
literature_rationale: Zmynd8 is an active comparator reproducing 13 genes in the same direction, and direct perturbation evidence identifies a ZMYND8–KDM5C complex whose loss yields concordant enhancer overactivation and derepression. The 151 placement does not require separate literature support.

finding_summary: The same 151 genes driven up by Kdm5c loss were driven down by several chromatin perturbations: Brd4 was the strongest negative neighbor, Kmt2d was second, and Smarcb1 also showed consistent opposite-direction overlap.
finding_consequence: The thalamic Kdm5c response sits on an enhancer/promoter chromatin axis with measurable polarity: losing the eraser exposes a program that is suppressed by losing selected writer/reader/remodeler functions.
literature_rationale: Brd4, Kmt2d, and Smarcb1 have active local surfaces and coherent opposite signed overlap with Kdm5c. Writer–eraser antagonism is supported for KMT2A, but the supplied source does not complete the relationship for the observed comparators.

finding_summary: Prrt1 down-regulation was the entire measurable 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut Kdm5c response.
finding_consequence: It marks a possible second, weaker Kdm5c-sensitive neuronal state distinct from the 151 thalamic program, but by itself should be treated as a hypothesis-generating biomarker rather than a pathway.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: Acute postmitotic Kdm5c loss produced a sharply restricted neuronal mRNA response: 18 downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and a single Prrt1 hit in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, but none in 20 other measured groups.
finding_consequence: The screen refines Kdm5c from a broadly expressed intellectual-disability chromatin regulator to a sparse acute transcriptomic dependency in two diencephalic glutamatergic contexts under this P16 mosaic loss-of-function design.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: The literature-obvious KDM5-family and REST comparators were rejected in this acute assay: Kdm5b had 0 FDR genes across 22 groups and Rest had 0 across 23, while Kmt2a/Kmt2b/Kmt2c showed little overlap with the Kdm5c 151 signature.
finding_consequence: The positive thalamic module is not a generic consequence of removing any H3K4 demethylase or REST-like repressor; Kdm5c specificity and the Kmt2d/Zmynd8 cross-screen relationships are the load-bearing dataset biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Broadly engaged neuronal Pld3 knockdown did not induce the expected APP/TLR/interferon transcriptional program.
finding_consequence: Published PLD3/PLD4 biology predicts lysosomal nucleic-acid handling and, in stressed contexts, TLR or cytosolic DNA-sensor signaling; the Perturb-seq readout shows that reducing Pld3 alone did not measurably turn on App, Sorl1, Tlr7, Tlr9, Ifit1, Ifnb1, Irf7, or Isg15 mRNA in normal brain cell types.
literature_rationale: The references provide an explicit chain from PLD3 loss to defective nucleic-acid clearance, sensor activation, and inflammatory signaling. The absence of the predicted RNA program therefore runs opposite to the documented mechanism, although differences in perturbation strength and requirements for PLD4 loss or substrate accumulation warrant moderate confidence.

finding_summary: The only FDR-supported downstream Pld3 response was Ncapd2 induction in 308 CB GABA, where Pld3 ranked first among 2023 targets on the Ncapd2 coordinate.
finding_consequence: The single-gene signal is too narrow to name a pathway, but it is not a generic screen artifact on that coordinate and nominates Ncapd2 as an exploratory marker of the one recovered Pld3-responsive neuronal state.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: The screen-wide Pld3 signature had no meaningful global positive or negative neighbor; top correlations were near zero and the leading neighbors did not reproduce the CB GABA Ncapd2 effect.
finding_consequence: This rejects the possibility that Pld3 belongs to an obvious recurrent transcriptomic module in this assay; its only robust call is more idiosyncratic than module-like.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Literature-obvious AD, TLR, and lysosome comparators were rejected as Pld3 phenocopies in the matched neuronal cell groups.
finding_consequence: The screen directly tests several genes that bracket the expected biology, including App, Psen1, Sorl1, Sort1, Tmem106b, Grn, cathepsin/lysosome genes, V-ATPase genes, Tlr9, and Trem2. They either were flat or produced different signatures, and none co-induced Ncapd2 in CB GABA, so acute neuronal Pld3 loss is uncoupled from those textbook pathways at the snRNA layer.

finding_summary: The main 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response was a mostly down-regulated neuronal adhesion, Rap-family, calcium and synaptic-scaffold signature.
finding_consequence: This names the biology actually present in the strongest Polr3b cell group instead of forcing the significant genes into a canonical Pol III small-RNA model.
literature_rationale: The 15-gene signed adhesion, Rap, calcium, and synaptic-scaffold response is sufficiently resolved as an atlas program without a selectivity claim. No supplied Polr3b-specific source bridges to that program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Bdp1 induced Ddit3 and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Polr3b did not, despite both lying in Pol III transcription biology.
finding_consequence: This rejects the simple expectation that any Pol III-machinery perturbation in the screen will share a single ISR-like mRNA phenotype and proves that the assay could detect such a secondary program when it was triggered.
literature_rationale: Both Bdp1 and Polr3b produce coherent local responses, making their distinct programs an informative matched divergence. Their shared Pol III role is specific, but the source does not predict Bdp1-selective ISR-like induction or Polr3b non-phenocopy.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA carried two-gene, cell-restricted Polr3b signatures rather than pathway-scale programs.
finding_consequence: The sparse FDR calls are worth preserving as reporter hypotheses but should not be inflated into a broad Pol III, ISR, or proteostasis response.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Polr3b generated only 19 downstream FDR<0.10 calls across 3 of 21 recovered neuronal groups, rather than a broad mRNA collapse.
finding_consequence: A core Pol III subunit perturbation was transcriptionally buffered in most postmitotic NeuN+ neurons, focusing interpretation on a narrow thalamic and midbrain surface rather than on assumed global Pol III failure.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Proteasome perturbations Psmb4, Psmc1, and Psmc5 converged with the Polr3b significant readouts, especially the down-regulated 151 TH module.
finding_consequence: The data-driven comparison shows that the Polr3b state is closest to the neuronal-downshift limb of essential proteasome perturbations, not to another Pol III target, and separates exact FDR convergence from weaker continuous-only neighbors such as Hspa5 and Pomp.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Ppp2r1a, Ankrd11, Tardbp, Naa15, and Setd5 opposed subsets of the Polr3b signature at FDR<0.10.
finding_consequence: The negative-neighbor analysis shows that the Polr3b vector is directionally organized, not just weak noise, but it places that organization opposite broad phosphatase, chromatin, and RNA-binding perturbation states.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The 151 signature is dominated by ER chaperone and folding compensation: Hspa5, Canx, Hyou1, Pdia4 and Hsp90b1 were all up-regulated.
finding_consequence: This converts a translocation-factor KO into a readable nuclear UPR-like output, showing that at least one neuronal class senses Sec63 loss as ER folding load.
literature_rationale: Five concordantly induced ER chaperone and folding genes establish the 151 program. Target-specific Sec63-deficiency studies directly document the same XBP1/BiP-linked response; neuronal placement is contextual.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: A smaller integrated-stress/amino-acid branch accompanied the chaperone program in 151, led by strong Chac1 induction with Slc3a2 and Mars1 up-regulation.
finding_consequence: Chac1 is the largest positive Sec63 effect in 151, making ATF4-like redox and amino-acid stress a useful biomarker hypothesis in addition to canonical BiP induction.
literature_rationale: Chac1, Slc3a2, and Mars1 support a coherent secondary stress program, but the supplied Sec63 studies establish selective IRE1/XBP1 activation rather than the signed ATF4/CHAC1 branch.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The 151 Sec63 response also contained a small negative neuronal-structure module, including Nlgn2, Sptbn1, Syne1, Nin and Plekhg1 down-regulation.
finding_consequence: The downstream state is not only ER quality-control rebound; the stressed neurons also repress synaptic or cytoskeletal components.
literature_rationale: Five concordantly decreased neuronal-structure genes support a secondary program, but general ER-homeostasis disruption does not specifically bridge Sec63 loss to signed Nlgn2/cytoskeletal repression.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Gfpt1 and Dhdds were the two strongest positive Sec63 signature neighbors, and Atp2a2 was a further ER-stress neighbor; all three re-induced Chac1/Hspa5-linked stress genes in the same 151/155 groups.
finding_consequence: The unbiased neighbors are glycosylation and ER-calcium hits, not only textbook translocon genes, arguing that vulnerable neurons converge on a shared ER client-load stress state.
literature_rationale: Gfpt1, Dhdds, and Atp2a2 have active matched surfaces and concordant ER-stress overlaps. Their established effects on glycosylation or ER calcium complete target-specific chains predicting convergence with Sec63 loss.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Sec63 loss produced a real but very narrow neuronal response: 18 downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and only Hspa5 in 155 MB Glut, with zero FDR<0.10 downstream genes in the other 16 measured Sec63 groups.
finding_consequence: The effect is not pan-neuronal ER failure; it marks a restricted postnatal vulnerability of two glutamatergic populations, especially the thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Atf6 and Marchf6 did not phenocopy Sec63: Atf6 had zero FDR<0.10 genes in all matched responder groups, whereas Marchf6 produced a sterol-biosynthesis signature instead of Hspa5/Chac1 overlap.
finding_consequence: Sec63 is not reporting generic ER-membrane perturbation; its transcriptome is closer to client-import and glycoprotein load than to ATF6 loss or ERAD E3 loss.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The Sec63 neuronal signature did not enter the polycystin disease axis: Pkd1 perturbation was flat in the Sec63 responder groups and Sec63 induced ER-stress genes rather than a measurable Pkd1-like state.
finding_consequence: Known SEC63 disease biology is liver and kidney epithelial/ciliary; this neuronal LoF response refines the mechanism to a generic ER proteostasis stress in only selected postmitotic neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The recurrent Tbcd output was alpha-tubulin induction rather than Tbcd mRNA loss: Tuba1a was up in all six responding groups and Tuba1b was up in the two strongest responders.
finding_consequence: TBCD is a beta-tubulin-binding cofactor, but the measured compensatory state is transcriptional reinforcement of alpha-tubulin isotypes, suggesting an attempted heterodimer-homeostasis correction rather than a broad stress response.
literature_rationale: Recurrent Tuba1a induction, reinforced by Tuba1b in the strongest responders, is a coherent tubulin-homeostasis output. The biochemical bridge is specific, but the literature does not establish that this signed transcriptional induction is compensatory.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Tbce was the strongest data-driven positive neighbor of Tbcd and phenocopied the alpha-tubulin module in matched deep-brain groups.
finding_consequence: The only directly targeted TBCA-E cofactor besides Tbcd converged on the same Tuba1a-dominated program, making the response pathway-specific rather than an idiosyncratic guide or cell-count artifact.
literature_rationale: Tbce is an active comparator with eight concordant exact overlaps and a highly coherent positive relationship. TBCD and TBCE are direct components of the same core tubulin chaperone, completing the coarse mechanistic chain.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Structural tubulin perturbations did not reproduce the Tbcd/Tbce cofactor state: Tuba1a editing induced other tubulin isotypes only in Pvalb and TH neurons, and Tubb5 was flat in every Tbcd-response group.
finding_consequence: The cofactor signal is not simply the transcriptomic mirror image of losing any tubulin subunit; cofactor imbalance and direct alpha-tubulin knockdown land in different feedback states.
literature_rationale: The corrected relationship is restricted to the active Tuba1a comparison in Pvalb and thalamic neurons, where structural-tubulin editing produced a distinct feedback state. The locally flat Tubb5 comparison is excluded, and literature does not predict the observed transcriptional divergence.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Dnm1l was a strong anti-neighbor of the Tbcd 19-feature signature and drove a broad thalamic injury program with Tuba1a, Tuba1b and Jun changing opposite to Tbcd.
finding_consequence: A broad DE perturbation in the same thalamic class can be detected in this assay, but it does not converge on alpha-tubulin induction; the Tbcd signature is therefore not a generic consequence of any damaged neuron entering an ISR-like state.
literature_rationale: Dnm1l is strongly active on the same thalamic surface and shows coherent opposite changes in Tuba1a, Tuba1b, and Jun, making the data-driven divergence evaluable. No target-specific literature bridge predicts the opposition.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Tbcd loss of function produced a sparse, deep-brain-biased response: only 6 of 22 measured cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and all cortical, hippocampal, and cerebellar groups were null or weak.
finding_consequence: The screen does not show a pan-neuronal transcriptomic collapse after acute postnatal Tbcd editing; it resolves the response to hypothalamic/thalamic/midbrain classes and prevents interpreting the many cortical zeros as unmeasured controls.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response was the only Tbcd state that expanded beyond tubulins, adding Jun, Nfil3, Satb1, Ypel4, Kctd16, Slc25a23 and Mturn up-regulation plus Lrrc7, Ptprn2 and Samd5 down-regulation.
finding_consequence: Thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c neurons are not just another Tuba1a-only responder; they recruit a secondary transcriptional and synaptic-remodeling layer that could mark the cell class in which microtubule-buffering stress becomes coupled to neuronal state changes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: In 155 MB Glut, engaged Ywhag loss failed to reproduce the strong Tsc2-loss sterol–lysosomal transcriptional program.
finding_consequence: Although curated 14-3-3 biology connects YWHAG-containing dimers to phosphorylated TSC2 and TORC1 control, Tsc2 perturbation and Ywhag perturbation are nearly uncorrelated in the cell type where Tsc2 has a large response.
literature_rationale: The YWHAG–TSC2 interaction makes the comparison biologically specific, but interaction and pathway annotation alone do not provide the perturbational direction needed to classify the observed failure to phenocopy Tsc2 as agreement or disagreement.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: A YWHAG neurodevelopmental gene can be transcriptionally buffered after sparse P16 neuronal loss.
finding_consequence: Across the 22 measured nonresponder groups, strong self-transcript depletion usually did not propagate to secondary stress, proteostasis, synaptic, or migration-like RNA programs; together with the paralog and RAF contrasts, the result points the main YWHAG disease biology toward embryonic morphology, phosphoprotein localization, excitability, or astrocyte/NMDA contexts rather than broad cell-autonomous steady-state RNA changes in P16-specified neurons.
literature_rationale: Strong Ywhag depletion in highly response-prone groups 151 and 155 supports the narrower conclusion that acute postnatal loss can be transcriptionally buffered. Developmental and electrophysiological studies do not predict this RNA null, and weak paralog/RAF non-phenocopy plus claims that other mechanisms are exclusive alternatives are excluded.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Ywhag loss produced a one-gene Vgf-positive response confined to 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
finding_consequence: The only FDR<0.10 downstream gene after Ywhag perturbation was Vgf, so the screen supports an acute upper-layer intratelencephalic neuropeptide/activity marker rather than a broad canonical 14-3-3 transcriptional program.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: The data-nominated Eef2 and Grin2b neighbors bracket the Ywhag Vgf response in opposite directions in the same upper-layer IT class.
finding_consequence: Eef2 was the strongest positive whole-screen neighbor and strongly induced Vgf, whereas Grin2b was the strongest biological anti-neighbor and repressed Vgf; this anchors Ywhag's lone signal to a real activity/synaptic axis while showing that the Ywhag signature is much weaker than either comparator.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: The screened 14-3-3 paralogs Ywhae and Ywhaz did not phenocopy Ywhag.
finding_consequence: Ywhag, Ywhae, and Ywhaz are high-confidence family interactors, yet Ywhae had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes and Ywhaz had only a Pfn2 response in a different L2/3 IT class; this argues that the weak Ywhag Vgf response is not a generic single-isoform 14-3-3 knockout program.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

finding_summary: The canonical RAF/MAPK 14-3-3 interaction arm was not recovered as a Ywhag-like neuronal RNA signature.
finding_consequence: Braf and Raf1 are high-confidence Ywhag interactors, but Braf was active only in two non-007 groups and Raf1 was flat; neither altered Vgf in 007, so the residual Ywhag signal should not be read as a RAF-like ERK transcriptional output.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: The Zfhx3 thalamic signature is dominated by loss of adhesion, guidance, GPCR, calcium, and extracellular-matrix markers rather than a broad chromatin or RNA-processing collapse.
finding_consequence: Human ZFHX3 LoF implicates promoter control of nervous-system developmental genes; the mouse postmitotic phenotype narrows that prior to modest remodeling of neuronal connectivity/state markers in one thalamic class.
literature_rationale: The 19-gene signed response contains a coherent adhesion, guidance, GPCR, calcium, and ECM program. ZFHX3 promoter occupancy provides target-specific proximity to neural and axon-development regulation but does not establish loss-induced down-regulation of this program. Placement in the sole responder group is descriptive, not evidence of thalamic selectivity.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Tagln3 and Scg2 are the strongest positive markers of the Zfhx3 thalamic responder state.
finding_consequence: These genes give the otherwise small Zfhx3 signature practical markers for detecting or validating the perturbed state in thalamic glutamatergic neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Zfhx3 loss produced a real but sharply restricted 19-gene response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The screen does not show a generic Zfhx3 transcriptional requirement across postmitotic neurons; it nominates a thalamic glutamatergic state as the only acute responder in this P16-to-P37/44 assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Zfhx4 was induced by Zfhx3 perturbation, but direct Zfhx4 or Zfhx2 perturbation did not phenocopy Zfhx3 in the same thalamic group.
finding_consequence: The most literal same-family signal in the responder signature behaves like a compensatory marker, not like evidence that ZFHX-family paralogs are interchangeable in this acute postmitotic context.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Canonical SCN clock-neuropeptide and Pdgfrb oxidative-stress targets were absent from both the hypothalamic nulls and the thalamic responder signature.
finding_consequence: A Zfhx3 LoF screen in broad P16-postmitotic neuronal groups should not be read as an SCN or oxidative-stress model: the expected prior axes were explicitly tested and not recovered.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: The strongest data-driven positive neighbors of Zfhx3 were Srsf1, Atp6v0c, Ctnnb1, Cic, and Hspa9 rather than ZFHX paralogs or SCN clock genes.
finding_consequence: Cross-screen convergence shows that the small Zfhx3 thalamic state lies on a broader perturbational axis shared with RNA-processing, lysosomal/mitochondrial, Wnt, and transcriptional-repressor perturbations.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: BAF and cleavage/polyadenylation comparators were measurable but failed to align with Zfhx3 despite the reported ZFHX3 interactome.
finding_consequence: The direct perturbation data separate physical association in human LoF studies from functional equivalence in acute mouse thalamic neurons: Smarcb1 and Smarcc2 were strong but mostly distinct responders, whereas Smarca2, Smarca4, and Cstf2 were flat.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Cd81 loss selectively up-regulated L1cam in Pvalb interneurons, creating the strongest downstream event in the entire Cd81 surface.
finding_consequence: L1cam points to a neuronal adhesion/axon-projection axis rather than to the immune and viral-entry programs that dominate CD81 literature.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: Cd81 perturbation induced Grsf1 in the 110 CNU-HYa HY MM glutamatergic group, the only robust effect outside Pvalb interneurons.
finding_consequence: GRSF1 nominates mitochondrial RNA handling as a cell-class sentinel of Cd81 loss, but only as a single-gene response.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: The Cd81 L1cam and Grsf1 responses were not reproduced by screen-measured tetraspanin/integrin relatives Tspan7, Itga4, or Itgb1.
finding_consequence: CD81 sits in tetraspanin webs with integrins, but the neuron response was not a generic tetraspanin-web or β1-integrin transcriptomic signature.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: Cpe loss produced a single downstream DEG, Aff3 up-regulation, restricted to 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
finding_consequence: This is the only FDR<0.10 downstream event; it points to a narrow cortical transcription-factor response rather than broad recovery of CPE peptide-processing biology.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut

finding_summary: The data-driven Cpe neighbors were not true phenocopies: the robust neighbors were broad proteostasis or TSC/mTOR-axis perturbations, whereas dense full-transcriptome similarity was near zero.
finding_consequence: This prevents over-interpreting Cpe as a silent proteotoxic-stress hit; Psmb4, Psmc1, and Tsc1 can secondarily reduce Cpe in some groups, but they generate thousands of DEGs unlike acute Cpe itself.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Measured secretory-pathway relatives Pcsk2, Pcsk5, Sort1, Snap25, and Sv2a failed to phenocopy the Cpe Aff3 response.
finding_consequence: CPE belongs to a regulated-secretory propeptide module, but the directly queryable neighbors either produced no 009 downstream response or mostly self-transcript-only surfaces, arguing that the Cpe phenotype is not a generic dense-core or synaptic vesicle transcriptome.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut

finding_summary: Engaged Gabrb2-loss surfaces did not induce transcriptional replacement by Gabrb1, Gabrb3, or a broader inhibitory-synapse program.
finding_consequence: Although β subunits participate in interchangeable-looking receptor pentamer diagrams, the dataset argues that acute loss of Gabrb2 RNA is not generally countered by a detectable Gabrb1/Gabrb3 or GABA-handling mRNA compensation program.
literature_rationale: Receptor composition, network association, knockout phenotypes, and paralog diversity do not supply a specific perturbation-to-transcriptional-compensation bridge. The dataset's informative absence therefore has no matching literature expectation.

finding_summary: Gabrb2 loss induced an immediate-early neuronal activity-response program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, including Nr4a1, Fos, Npas4, Vgf, and Homer2.
finding_consequence: A postsynaptic GABA_A beta2 perturbation crossed the nuclear activity-response threshold in one thalamic glutamatergic state rather than causing a pan-neuronal stress or synapse-loss program.
literature_rationale: The coherent local program survives removal of the unsupported claim that it is unique to this cell type. Gabrb2 deletion is linked to disrupted thalamic inhibition, and neuronal activation directly induces represented genes such as Fos and Npas4. Unequal power limits distributional inference but does not erase the positive molecular phenotype.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Gabrb2 and Slc12a5 converged in the same 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c group on same-direction induction of Nr4a1, Fos and R3hdm2.
finding_consequence: The receptor subunit and the KCC2 chloride extruder both sit on the mature hyperpolarizing GABA axis; their convergence argues that the Gabrb2 signature is an inhibitory chloride-signaling phenotype, not an arbitrary nine-gene fluctuation.
literature_rationale: Both perturbations have informative local surfaces and share same-direction activity-response genes. The complete chain from impaired GABAA inhibition or chloride extrusion to increased excitability and immediate-early transcription predicts this coarse convergence without requiring the exact three-gene overlap or thalamic subtype.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Several validated negative 151 neighbors drove subsets of the Gabrb2 reporter genes downward, including Grin1, Kmt2d and Nalcn.
finding_consequence: Opposite-direction hits make the readout directional: the Gabrb2 program is not merely a generic thalamic perturbation artifact, because several perturbations invert Homer2, Vgf, Nr4a1, Fos, Npas4, Opn3 or R3hdm2 in the same cell group.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The 151 Gabrb2 response was not reproduced by directly perturbing beta paralogs, common alpha/gamma/delta co-subunits, or inhibitory-synapse organizers.
finding_consequence: The screen separates beta2 loss from a generic GABA_A-complex signature: Gabrd was the closest restricted positive neighbor but had only one FDR<0.10 gene, while Gabrb1, Gabrb3, Gabra1-5, Gabrg2, Gabrg3, Gphn, Nlgn2, Arhgef9, Slc6a1 and Slc32a1 were flat in the matched group.

finding_summary: Postnatal sparse Gabrb2 loss recovered a thalamic immediate-early response but not the broad developmental, glial or seizure-like programs reported in human GABRB2 disorders and germline mouse knockouts.
finding_consequence: The result narrows what this screen can model: it captures a cell-autonomous consequence of losing beta2-containing inhibition after neuronal specification, whereas patient missense alleles can be gain-of-function, loss-of-function, trafficking, or dominant-effect variants acting from early development.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Phf21a targeting recurrently increased Rreb1 across all five Phf21a responder groups.
finding_consequence: The principal Phf21a-associated readout in this brain atlas is not a broad generic neuronal program but a narrow Rreb1-centered module that is consistent with a chromatin-regulatory perturbation and is a practical marker for responsive cells.
literature_rationale: The references provide a strong target-specific derepression mechanism and an unsigned PHF21A–RREB1 association, making the bridge biologically specific but insufficient to predict the recurrent Rreb1 increase decisively.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: In TH Prkcd/Grin2c Glut, Phf21a and Sin3a perturbations drove Rreb1 in opposite directions despite their shared association with HDAC1/2 repressor biology.
finding_consequence: The directionality of Rreb1 is complex-specific: shared access to HDAC1/2 does not predict the same transcriptional state, warning against treating deacetylase-core perturbations as interchangeable.
literature_rationale: Shared HDAC1/2 pathway membership alone does not establish interchangeable transcriptional consequences or a directional Rreb1 expectation, so the observed sign reversal lacks a specific literature bridge.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: TH Prkcd/Grin2c Glut expanded the Phf21a response into an ECM/adhesion/junction-biased module containing Col4a5, Cdh13, Jam2, and Wls/Lats2, with related pieces in MB Glut and MB/P/MY GABA.
finding_consequence: This prevents the non-cortical response from being collapsed into Rreb1 alone and identifies the only responder where Phf21a loss changed more than one or two genes.
literature_rationale: The compatible ECM, adhesion, and junction changes support a local coherent program. Group 151's greater breadth is confounded by its response-prone baseline and is not retained as selectivity; no target-specific literature bridge supports the program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Myt1l and Naa20 were the strongest positive Phf21a neighbors by restricted screen-wide cosine, with Myt1l matching the sign of 17/18 Phf21a FDR hits.
finding_consequence: The best data-driven convergence was outside the canonical BHC complex, indicating that the P16 Phf21a response shares a small Rreb1-centered state with other neuronal perturbations rather than simply tracking known complex membership.
literature_rationale: The finding is narrowed to Myt1l: an active comparator with extensive signed agreement and direct source evidence of same-direction Phf21a/Myt1l DEG overlap. Naa20 convergence is excluded because its exceptionally broad surface and lack of a target-specific bridge make that component weak.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Only 5 of 22 measured Phf21a cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, giving a sparse, mostly up-regulated response rather than a pan-neuronal program.
finding_consequence: The majority-zero surface is a biological feature of acute P16 Phf21a loss: it confines the detectable transcriptional effect to two cortical IT groups and three TH/MB groups.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Rest perturbation did not phenocopy Phf21a: Rest had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across all 23 cell groups, including every Phf21a responder.
finding_consequence: This directly rejects the simplest BHC80-as-REST-effector expectation for acute P16 neurons and forces a developmental or REST-independent interpretation of the Phf21a signature.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The strongest negative neighbor, Yy1, weakly opposed Phf21a and drove Rreb1, Ccdc141, and Wls downward in TH Prkcd/Grin2c Glut, while Ppargc1a and Taf1b were flat in Phf21a responder groups.
finding_consequence: The lack of a strong inverse neighbor shows that Phf21a does not sit on a simple bipolar axis within the screen; even the best negative comparator only partially inverts the Phf21a genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The P16 mosaic neuronal signature is far narrower than PHF21A human haploinsufficiency would suggest, pointing the main disease-relevant deficit toward earlier developmental, craniofacial, or circuit-assembly windows.
finding_consequence: A therapeutic or modifier screen that uses only acute postmitotic neuronal transcriptomics could miss the dominant PHF21A disease biology; Rreb1 is useful as an engagement biomarker but not evidence that the full human syndrome was modeled.

finding_summary: Ptprn2 perturbation produced a single-cell-class, single-gene downstream response: Sh2b1 decreased only in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
finding_consequence: Sh2b1 links the otherwise vesicle-facing Ptprn2 perturbation to a receptor-adaptor transcript in corticofugal neurons, but the evidence is narrow and should be treated as a candidate marker rather than a pathway-scale program.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut

finding_summary: The IA-2 paralog Ptprn and core vesicle-exocytosis perturbations did not phenocopy Ptprn2.
finding_consequence: Dense-core and SNARE biology was recoverable in the same screen, but its signatures were Stxbp1/Snap25-centered rather than Ptprn2-centered; therefore the near-null Ptprn2 result is a specific buffered response, not a global inability of the assay to see vesicle perturbations.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 052 Pvalb Gaba; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The canonical LCN2/SLC22A17 iron-apoptosis and secondary stress readouts were absent from the Slc22a17 DE surface.
finding_consequence: The assay would have seen a Bcl2l11, iron-handling, ISR, or autophagy transcriptional response if receptor loss were intrinsically stressing these postmitotic neurons; their absence makes the nulls mechanistically informative rather than a pure snRNA-seq readout failure.
literature_rationale: Strong local target reduction plus a uniformly null multi-gene stress, iron, ISR, and autophagy sentinel set makes absence of an appreciable program informative in 005. Direct positive evidence comes from neural stem cells, while the source distinguishes mature-neuron phenotypes, leaving transfer to homeostatic cortical neurons incomplete.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Slc22a17 loss produced a single robust downstream DEG: Msmo1 was up-regulated in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, while every other sterol gene queried remained below genome-wide significance.
finding_consequence: The hit nominates L4-5 IT cortical glutamatergic neurons as the only transcriptomic responder and links the response to a cholesterol-biosynthetic enzyme rather than to the canonical LCN2-Bim or iron-handling module.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Lrp2, the measurable LCN2-receptor literature comparator, was also transcriptionally flat in the same 22 neuronal groups.
finding_consequence: A same-ligand receptor did not reveal a hidden LCN2 receptor program in this homeostatic neuronal screen, supporting the idea that the missing axis is ligand and inflammatory tissue context rather than Slc22a17-specific buffering alone.

finding_summary: The screenwide Slc22a17 signature had no strong neighbors; its closest data-driven comparators either had no 005 response or diverged from the Msmo1-up singleton.
finding_consequence: The weak correlation structure argues that Slc22a17 perturbation does not collapse onto a generic cortical stress, endocytosis, or neuronal-activity signature; Ap2s1 even drove Msmo1 in the opposite direction in 005.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Ahdc1 perturbation lowers Wls in its responsive thalamic surface without inducing canonical beta-catenin output genes such as Axin2 or Nkd1 or phenocopying Apc loss.
finding_consequence: AHDC1 can impinge on a WNT-ligand trafficking component while leaving Axin2 and Nkd1 uninduced, so Wls should be treated as a local marker rather than evidence for a complete beta-catenin output program.
literature_rationale: The dossier contains separate AHDC1 and Wnt-pathway annotations but no target-specific bridge joining them; shared transcriptional or pathway context is insufficient.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The Ahdc1 thalamic signature primarily remodels cell-surface and extracellular-matrix genes rather than a generic stress program.
finding_consequence: Down-regulation of Ptprz1, Spock3, Lrp1b, Tro and Cdh18 with opposite up-regulation of Chst1 and Col18a1 points to re-patterning of neuronal adhesion and pericellular matrix in the one vulnerable postmitotic class.
literature_rationale: Seven compatibly interpreted, signed genes support a local adhesion and extracellular-matrix program independently of exclusivity. No target-specific AHDC1 edge connects loss to this program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: A second component of the same 151 response is a mostly negative neuronal communication program.
finding_consequence: Loss of Ahdc1 decreased the AMPA-receptor subunit Gria2, acetylcholinesterase Ache, the calcium/synaptic gene Mctp2, the calcium-binding gene Calb1 and the Wnt secretion factor Wls, linking AHDC1 to synaptic-state genes in mature thalamic neurons.
literature_rationale: Five neuronal-communication genes decrease coherently within the corrected response. AHDC1 disease association supplies relevance but no specific directional bridge to this mature-neuronal program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Neurocutaneous and chromatin disease-family comparators did not phenocopy Ahdc1 in the Ahdc1 responder group.
finding_consequence: MECP2, NIPBL and ADNP can be compared directly in the same thalamic group; their perturbations either had no Ahdc1-signature overlap or mixed same/opposite overlap, and Huwe1, Ctcf, Brd4, Wac and Ctnnb1 were also only partially aligned. AHDC1 therefore should not be collapsed onto a generic postmitotic chromatin-disorder signature.
literature_rationale: The comparator perturbations have active same-group surfaces and do not reproduce the Ahdc1 signature, supporting a coarse non-phenocopy claim. Chromatin-network proximity motivates comparison but does not predict the observed divergence.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Ahdc1 produced a corrected transcriptional response in only one measured cell group, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; all other recovered groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes and 215 MB Dopa had no rows.
finding_consequence: The screen localizes the acute postmitotic Ahdc1 dependency to a posterior thalamic glutamatergic state rather than to a pan-neuronal consequence of losing a broadly expressed nuclear protein.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The strongest positive neighbors of the Ahdc1 151 signature were Srsf1, Uba5 and Trrap, not direct AHDC1 partners.
finding_consequence: These three much broader perturbations recurred on the Ahdc1 down-state genes, especially Snhg11, Lrp1b, Mctp2, Gria2, Ccdc85a, Ache, Calb1, Tro, Ptprz1, Spock3 and Cdh18, nominating the Ahdc1 response as a local version of a broader thalamic vulnerability module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Prox1 and Apc were the strongest measured anti-neighbors of Ahdc1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The same small thalamic gene set can move in the opposite direction under other perturbations: Prox1 reversed Rreb1, Spock3, Calb1 and Ache, while Apc reversed Spock3, Calb1, Rreb1 and Ptprz1. That bidirectionality argues against the Ahdc1 genes being merely stochastic low-count artifacts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The canonical Gibbin/GATA mesoderm pathway was absent from the neuronal Ahdc1 response.
finding_consequence: Gata3 was a biological partner to test because hESC Gibbin and GATA3 co-regulate RA/BMP4 mesoderm genes, yet Gata3, Gata4, Twist1 and Pitx2 perturbations were transcriptionally flat in postnatal neuronal groups, including the Ahdc1 responder. The thalamic signature is therefore an AHDC1-dependent neuronal program, not residual activation of the embryonic mesodermal module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: ER Ca2+-pump loss triggered a UPR/ISR-like module where Atp2b2 did not, separating SERCA2 stress from plasma-membrane PMCA2 loss.
finding_consequence: The screen could detect a secondary Ca2+-pump stress program when ER calcium handling was perturbed, so the absence of Ddit3/Chac1/Xbp1/Hspa5 induction after Atp2b2 is an informative compartment-specific negative.
literature_rationale: The active Atp2a2 comparator produces a strong UPR/ISR program on the matched measured surface, while those markers are absent after Atp2b2 perturbation. This supports compartment-specific non-phenocopy, but the literature does not specifically predict the ATP2B2 negative.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: PMCA-family and related Ca2+-ATPase perturbations were not interchangeable with Atp2b2: Atp2b1 produced a restricted 151 response, Atp2b3 produced one 191 response, and Atp2c1 was flat.
finding_consequence: This keeps the expected paralogs as measured comparators and shows that neuronal PMCA2 has a distinct P16 snRNA loss-of-function footprint rather than a family-wide mRNA state.
literature_rationale: The defensible comparison is with active Atp2b1 in the 151 group, where its substantial response differs from Atp2b2. Atp2b3 and Atp2c1 are too sparse to support generalized family divergence and are excluded from the load-bearing claim.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Atp2b2's strongest data-driven neighbors were dominated by near-zero signatures, while the broad RNA-splicing perturbation Srsf1 diverged rather than converged.
finding_consequence: The full-screen search did not reveal a hidden Atp2b2-like module; it independently supports the interpretation that Atp2b2 is transcriptionally flat in this assay.

finding_summary: Atp2b2 loss did not induce mRNA compensation by other PMCA paralogs, Atp2a2, Atp2c1, or calmodulins in any measured cell group.
finding_consequence: The buffered transcriptome is not explained by a visible replacement module at the level of Ca2+-ATPase or calmodulin transcripts.

finding_summary: Calm3 loss decreased the transcript of its canonical calmodulin-regulated CaV1.2 client Cacna1c in Sst interneurons.
finding_consequence: CACNA1C/CaV1.2 is a direct calmodulin-regulated channel and calmodulin variants cause LQTS through altered CaV1.2 regulation; the dataset nominates Sst GABA neurons as a brain context where Calm3 loss may also depress the channel transcript.
literature_rationale: The cited target–client relationship makes Cacna1c biologically relevant, but direct functional regulation of the CaV1.2 protein does not predict downregulation of its encoding transcript.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba

finding_summary: Calm1 produced a multi-gene response in TH Prkcd/Grin2c neurons whereas similarly depleted Calm3 was transcriptionally silent there, despite the loci encoding identical calmodulin protein.
finding_consequence: Calm1 and Calm3 encode the same calmodulin peptide, so matched target depletion might have been expected to converge; instead Calm1 triggered a many-gene Rasgrp2/Peg3/Resp18-positive signature while Calm3 was downstream-silent in the same cell type.
literature_rationale: Protein identity is specific evidence relevant to the paralog comparison, but it does not provide a decisive directional prediction for transcriptomic breadth after separate gene perturbations. Thus the observed non-equivalence is not a documented contradiction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: In Sst interneurons, Cacna1c/CaV1.2 was the lone downstream Calm3 hit and decreased after Calm3 perturbation.
finding_consequence: Cacna1c is a direct, high-confidence calmodulin-regulated L-type calcium-channel client, so its Sst-specific transcriptional decrease is the clearest canonical CaM-axis signal in the dataset and is consistent with a compensatory attempt to reduce CaV1 calcium entry when CaM-dependent channel feedback is perturbed.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba

finding_summary: Ncdn up-regulation was a private Calm3 response in Pvalb interneurons.
finding_consequence: Because no shared CaM client program accompanied it, Ncdn is best treated as a Pvalb-restricted marker of Calm3 perturbation rather than as evidence for a known calmodulin pathway.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: Slc38a1 down-regulation was a private Calm3 response in CNU-HYa/HY mammillary glutamatergic neurons.
finding_consequence: The significant Slc38a1 decrease nominates amino-acid/neurotransmitter-precursor transport as the only measurable transcriptomic output in this hypothalamic glutamatergic class, separated from the Pvalb Ncdn and Sst Cacna1c responses.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: Postnatal Calm3 loss generated an exceptionally sparse neuronal transcriptome: only 3 of 22 measured cell groups carried any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and each responder had one gene only.
finding_consequence: The primary result is not a broad pan-neuronal calcium-stress program but a narrowly cell-type-restricted, one-gene surface in Pvalb interneurons, Sst interneurons, and CNU-HYa/HY mammillary glutamatergic neurons.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 053 Sst Gaba; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: The exact calmodulin paralogs Calm1 and Calm2 did not phenocopy Calm3 in matched responder groups, and Calm1 instead produced a small TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response where Calm3 was flat.
finding_consequence: The result rejects a simple model in which knocking down any one gene encoding identical CaM protein produces the same neuronal transcriptional state; gene copy, guide/editing context, expression dosage, or cis-regulatory differences dominate the weak transcriptomic output.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 053 Sst Gaba; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Perturbations of Cacna1c, Kcnq2/3/5, Camk2a/b/g, and Ppp3ca failed to converge on the three Calm3 downstream genes in the matched responder groups.
finding_consequence: Although these are direct or core CaM clients and effectors, their own transcriptional DE surfaces do not explain the Calm3 Ncdn, Cacna1c, or Slc38a1 hits; the Calm3 readout is therefore not a generic CaV/Kv7/CaMKII/calcineurin module.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 053 Sst Gaba; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: Acute neuronal Calm3 loss did not recreate a calmodulinopathy-like CaV/Kv7/CaMK transcriptional state.
finding_consequence: Human CALM3 disease is dominated by specific heterozygous missense alleles that poison CaM-dependent channel regulation, whereas this experiment weakened one Calm locus postmitotically in mouse neurons; the mostly flat DE surface argues against treating single-gene CRISPR Calm3 loss as a transcriptomic proxy for dominant CALM3 channelopathy.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 053 Sst Gaba; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: Ctsb perturbation did not induce a lysosomal CLEAR, autophagy, UPR/ISR, or cathepsin-family compensation program.
finding_consequence: A crippling lysosomal proteolysis defect should have generated secondary stress transcripts detectable by snRNA-seq; instead Ctsd, Ctsl, Ctss, Lamp1/2, Tfeb/Tfe3, Sqstm1/Map1lc3 genes and Atf4-Ddit3-Hspa5 stress genes were all FDR-flat, so any buffering is not a recurrent transcriptional bounce-back.
literature_rationale: The source-audit evidence provides a direct, directional Ctsb-loss-to-lysosomal-program bridge opposite to the informative neuronal result. The macrophage-to-neuron context difference limits transportability but does not erase the contradiction.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Neither unbiased signature neighbors nor literature-obvious endolysosomal comparators converged with Ctsb.
finding_consequence: The closest feature-centered neighbors of Ctsb had residual correlations of only about ±0.06 and at most six FDR genes, while App, Psen1, Sorl1, Grn, Lamp2, Psap, Atp6v0a1, Atp6v1a and Atp13a2 failed to form a shared Ctsb-like neuronal module; this prevents a false pathway story from being inferred from textbook proximity alone.

finding_summary: The Alzheimer/inflammasome priors for CTSB are displaced away from this WT juvenile NeuN+ transcriptomic screen rather than contradicted by it.
finding_consequence: CTSB inhibition can alter amyloid peptide production in hAPP models and released cathepsin B can participate in amyloid-β-driven inflammasome activation, but this screen lacked aged amyloid substrate burden, peptide readouts and well-sampled microglia; its null specifically says that deleting Ctsb in young postmitotic neurons does not by itself start an amyloid-, NLRP3-, or Il1b-like transcriptional cascade.

finding_summary: Gtf2i loss induced a compact thalamic membrane, lipid, signaling, and cytoskeletal-modulator program led by Kcnk4, Pnpla6, Rasgrp2, Notum, and Plppr3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The response did not look like a global consequence of reducing a ubiquitous transcription factor; it singled out a specific thalamic glutamatergic state and a compact marker set headed by Kcnk4, Pnpla6, Rasgrp2, and Plppr3.
literature_rationale: General transcription-factor function and other documented GTF2I-dependent neuronal programs are insufficient to bridge to the specific observed program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Engaged Baz1b perturbation did not reproduce the Gtf2i thalamic module, arguing that the response is not a generic output of perturbing a co-deleted Williams-Beuren interval gene.
finding_consequence: The contrast argues that the Gtf2i thalamic module is not a generic transcriptional output of perturbing a co-deleted Williams-Beuren locus gene; it is more consistent with gene-specific dosage biology.
literature_rationale: The literature supports nonredundancy within the disease interval, but the decisive Gtf2i-versus-Baz1b transcriptomic comparison remains undocumented.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The strongest positive data-driven neighbor was Zmym2: in the same thalamic class it up-regulated Plppr3, Notum, and Rasgrp2 in the Gtf2i direction; Kdm5c and Nrg2 converged on Kcnk4/Catsperz/Notum subsets.
finding_consequence: Zmym2 is also a literature-obvious comparator because GTF2I may reside in a BHC chromatin complex containing ZMYM2 and PHF21A, so its unprompted nomination links the tiny Gtf2i module to a measurable chromatin-cofactor perturbation rather than only to the GTF2I paralog family.
literature_rationale: The focal relationship is narrowed to the informative Zmym2 comparison, which shares three same-direction thalamic effects with Gtf2i. Possible membership in the same BHC complex is specific but does not establish an obligate dependency or predict these signs. Sparse Kdm5c and Nrg2 comparisons are ancillary only.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The TFII-I-family comparator Gtf2ird1 did respond weakly in 151 but shared none of Gtf2i's nine thalamic downstream genes; Phf21a, Usf1, and Taf1 likewise did not phenocopy the Gtf2i module.
finding_consequence: GTF2I and GTF2IRD1 are neighboring Williams-syndrome genes with shared embryonic importance, yet the postnatal Perturb-seq surface rejects simple interchangeability in the only robust Gtf2i responder.
literature_rationale: The claim is narrowed to Gtf2ird1: both paralogs respond in 151, yet their local DEG sets do not overlap. Direct comparative brain ChIP-seq demonstrates distinct binding features and predicts coarse downstream divergence. Phf21a is ancillary, while flat Usf1 and Taf1 cannot bear non-phenocopy claims.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Srsf1, Ap2s1, and Ppp2r1a are the leading opposite-direction neighbors, reversing multiple Gtf2i thalamic genes including Notum, Rasgrp2, Plppr3, Celf5, Kcnk4, and Catsperz.
finding_consequence: The Gtf2i module is therefore not a monotonic stress artifact: unrelated RNA-splicing, endocytosis, and phosphatase-complex perturbations can drive the same genes in the opposite direction, giving the module cross-screen polarity.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Gtf2i loss produced a narrow neuronal response: 9 downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and singleton Gas2l1/Erlin2 effects in two hindbrain/midbrain classes, with no FDR-supported downstream genes in 19 other measured classes.
finding_consequence: The result turns the main biological readout from a ubiquitous TFII-I loss into a thalamus-biased postnatal module, while keeping the two singleton midbrain/pons signals as exploratory rather than pathway-scale responses.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The 151 response increases Kcnk4, Rasgrp2, Notum, Pnpla6, Stoml1, Celf5, and Plppr3 while decreasing Carmil3, pointing to a local excitability/Rap-actin/Wnt-modulatory program rather than global transcriptional failure.
finding_consequence: TFII-I is a transcription factor, but the acute postnatal downstream genes are membrane, lipid, Wnt, and cytoskeletal modulators; that sharply limits mechanistic claims to a small secondary module in one thalamic class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The expected mitochondrial/autophagy/ISR secondary program was absent after Gtf2i perturbation even in the three responder groups, whereas Atp2a2 perturbation in the same groups readily induced Ddit3 and Chac1.
finding_consequence: This is an informative negative result: the snRNA-seq readout can detect stress transcriptional programs in these cell classes, so Gtf2i's flat stress surface is better explained by timing, cellular context, and sparse dosage than by a generic inability of the assay to see ISR-like programs.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The only significant L4/5 IT Kcnq2 downstream gene was Bdnf, and two other channel perturbations in the same cell class, Kcnb1 and Gabrg2, also up-regulated Bdnf.
finding_consequence: Bdnf is an activity-regulated trophic transcript, so its recurrent induction is a plausible biomarker of channel-driven excitability rather than a generic CRISPR injury signature; because Kv7 openers are antiseizure, Bdnf up-regulation should be read as a loss-of-channel response, not as a desired direction for therapy.
literature_rationale: Significant Kcnq2 depletion, Bdnf induction, and matched induction after other channel-loss perturbations support the expected activity-response effect. Target-specific channel-loss-to-hyperexcitability evidence plus depolarization-to-BDNF evidence completes the signed chain.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Rogdi down in L2/3 ENT/PPP/RSP IT neurons and Agap2 up in TH Prkcd/Grin2c neurons were singleton, cell-type-restricted Kcnq2 markers rather than members of a recovered pathway.
finding_consequence: The two non-cortical responder groups nominate epilepsy- or synapse-linked transcripts, but the single-gene nature of each response argues for cautious marker follow-up rather than a pathway-level conclusion.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The data-driven negative neighbor Ap2s1 moved Kcnq2 marker genes in the opposite direction, down-regulating Bdnf in L4/5 IT neurons and Agap2 in TH Prkcd/Grin2c neurons while suppressing Egr1, Arc, Npas4, and Vgf.
finding_consequence: This contrast separates a tiny Kcnq2 channel-loss signature from the much broader Ap2s1 perturbation state and shows that the Kcnq2 marker directions are not a universal neuronal-stress artifact.

finding_summary: Postnatal Htt loss induced an SREBF/sterol-feedback transcriptional response in hypothalamic, thalamic, and midbrain neuronal groups, strongest in 155 MB Glut.
finding_consequence: The measured phenotype is not a pan-neuronal Htt collapse; it nominates a subcortical cholesterol-feedback axis that is separable from the many flat cortical and forebrain-inhibitory bins.
literature_rationale: The positive sterol program survives removal of the unsupported claim that it is biologically restricted to these groups. Mutant-HTT literature supplies a target-specific but context- and direction-mismatched bridge, so the relation remains specific_incomplete.

finding_summary: The sterol genes rose after Htt loss, the opposite sign from the cholesterol-biosynthesis deficit reported for mutant HTT models.
finding_consequence: This argues that acute wild-type Htt loss is not simply a transcriptomic miniature of polyQ Huntington disease; the screen is seeing feedback activation of an intact SREBF2 module.
literature_rationale: The recurrent positive sterol module is opposite the directly documented mutant-HTT repression of SREBP/cholesterol transcription. The perturbation difference limits mechanistic interpretation but does not erase the supported sign divergence.

finding_summary: The top positive Htt neighbors were not other HD genes but dynein/dynactin, mTOR-autophagy, and ER sterol-control perturbations that independently induced the same sterol module.

Sources provide HTT transport/autophagy links and direct MARCH6-to-sterol regulation, but do not complete the signed convergence bridge for the full comparator set.

finding_summary: The Kif1a sterol module converged with Dctn1, Mib1, Chp1, Tsc1 and Tsc2 perturbations in matched cell groups.

finding_summary: The screen models partial postmitotic Kif1a loss, not the full spectrum of allele-specific KAND motor-domain mechanisms.
finding_consequence: Human KIF1A disorders include dominant missense variants with distinct motor phenotypes, including rigor microtubule binding; therefore weak sterol/stress biomarkers from CRISPR LoF should not be read as universal KAND markers or as support for inhibiting KIF1A.

finding_summary: Kif1b, Kif5a, Kif5c, Klc1, Klc2 and Tanc2 did not phenocopy Kif1a in the Kif1a-positive cell groups.

finding_summary: Scamp5 loss produced a weak coordinated sterol-biosynthesis response in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c neurons, with Msmo1, Srebf2, Cyp51, Dhcr24, Insig1, and Hmgcs1 trending upward and the module opposing Srebf2 loss.

finding_summary: Scamp5 perturbation decreased the ER-stress effector Ddit3 in CNU-MGE GABA neurons rather than inducing a CHOP response.

literature_rationale: The literature provides a target-specific ER-stress bridge compatible with reduced stress output after SCAMP5 loss, but the decisive link to the observed Ddit3 decrease is not documented.

finding_consequence: Human SCAMP5 disorders are dominated by missense alleles and channel-trafficking phenotypes; a flat Cacna transcript surface is therefore evidence that this mouse LoF screen would miss altered channel surface delivery rather than evidence that the disease axis is absent.
literature_rationale: Strong Scamp5 suppression and adequate power in 110 and especially 151 support the restricted finding that T-type-channel transcripts remained unchanged. The source establishes membrane-trafficking regulation but does not directly establish transcript invariance; 054 lacks a sufficiently documented informative absence test.

finding_summary: Scamp5 loss gave a real but extremely focal neuronal transcriptomic response: only three of 23 recovered cell groups had any downstream gene at FDR<0.10, with the largest response limited to five genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: SCAMP5 is a neuronal membrane-trafficking protein, so its postmitotic loss is not globally silent, but this in vivo snRNA-seq assay mostly captures absence of secondary transcription rather than the canonical presynaptic physiology.

finding_summary: The thalamic Scamp5 signature combines Gabra1, Cx3cl1, and Sparcl1 down-regulation with Msmo1 and Fyttd1 up-regulation rather than induction of a canonical synaptic-vesicle gene set.
finding_consequence: Gabra1 down-regulation is compatible with a postsynaptic inhibitory-receptor adjustment in neurons whose primary SCAMP5 lesion should be presynaptic membrane recycling, while Cx3cl1 and Sparcl1 point to altered extracellular or neuron-glia signaling in the same small responder class.

finding_summary: Scamp5 perturbation suppresses Ddit3/CHOP in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and does not activate an ER-stress/CHOP program.
finding_consequence: Literature places increased SCAMP5 downstream of ER stress in a mutant-huntingtin aggregation model; the measured loss-of-function direction in this screen is therefore not a toxic ER-stress induction and may sit on the opposite side of that stress-endocytosis axis.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA

finding_summary: The only broad cross-perturbation convergence is an exploratory membrane-lipid/endolysosomal module: Scamp5 induces Msmo1 in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c cells, while Chp1, Mib1, Dctn1, Rab7, and Tsc2 induce much larger sterol-associated programs in the same matched responder groups.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The thalamic Smarce1 signature suppresses a postsynaptic DAG/PKC module while allowing a small Dagla increase.
finding_consequence: Concordant decreases of Prkcd, Prkcb, Begain, Lrrc7, Sdk2, Ptpn3, and Rasa4 with Dagla up suggest that the postmitotic BAF lesion is read out through synaptic lipid/PKC signaling rather than through a generic heat-shock, UPR, or proteasome rebound program.

finding_summary: Core BAF perturbations nominate the same 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c module: Smarcb1 and Smarcc2 were the two strongest Smarce1 signature neighbors.
finding_consequence: The same-direction 14/16 and 12/16 overlaps with Smarcb1 and Smarcc2 turn a 16-gene Smarce1 hit into a reproducible local SWI/SNF/BAF module, not an isolated single-target artifact.
literature_rationale: Smarcb1 and Smarcc2 are highly active comparators reproducing most Smarce1 genes concordantly. Their experimentally established membership in the same BAF core predicts coarse transcriptional convergence.

finding_summary: The top data-driven non-BAF neighborhood is asymmetric: Ctnnb1, Ap2s1 and Srsf1 converge with Smarce1, whereas Chd4, Naa15, Celf2, Huwe1 and Zfp423 invert small parts of the same signature.
finding_consequence: The restricted neighbor search preserves both positive and negative axes around the observed module and shows that the Prkcd/Begain/Abhd12b genes are not simply the first genes to move after any large perturbation in 151 TH neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Smarce1 loss produced a real but sharply restricted response: 16 downstream FDR<0.10 genes only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: A canonical chromatin-remodeling subunit did not produce a pan-neuronal acute stress or transcriptional collapse; the dataset localizes its detectable post-P16 neuronal dependency to one thalamic glutamatergic class.

finding_summary: BAF membership was not sufficient for phenocopy: Arid1a and Arid2 were partial, whereas Arid1b, Smarca2, Smarca4 and Smarcc1 did not reproduce the Smarce1 module in 151 TH neurons.

finding_summary: The postnatal neuronal phenotype is narrower than SMARCE1 disease genetics would imply from Coffin-Siris syndrome or clear-cell meningioma alone.
finding_consequence: SMARCE1 haploinsufficiency can be pathogenic, but the screen indicates that after neurons are specified the immediate transcriptional liability is a small thalamic module; embryonic BAFopathy and meningeal tumor-suppressor mechanisms are displaced from this P16 NeuN+ assay.

finding_summary: Atxn2 loss did not induce Atxn2l transcript compensation in the transcriptionally responsive 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut population.
finding_consequence: ATXN2L is an ATXN2-related stress-granule and processing-body factor, so the lack of Atxn2l upregulation argues against a transcriptional paralog buffer in this dataset.

finding_summary: The responder biased upward toward synaptic-vesicle and neurite/cytoskeletal transcripts.
finding_consequence: Up-regulation of Syt7, Sncb, Crmp1, Cspg5, Tln2, Ncdn, Stmn4, and Gprasp1 suggests that loss of an mRNP/translation scaffold is secondarily rebalanced through synaptic and structural mRNAs rather than through a canonical heat-shock or UPR module.

finding_summary: Atxn2 loss also depressed a small nuclear RNA-processing arm in the same responder.
finding_consequence: Down-regulation of Srsf11, Son, and Rsrp1, together with Coro6, Tspoap1, and Peg3, separates the Atxn2 response from a purely synaptic induction and points to a compensatory spliceosomal/nuclear-mRNA-processing component downstream of a cytoplasmic RBP perturbation.
literature_rationale: Target-specific ATXN2 depletion directly supports decreased stability and abundance in an RNA-regulatory network, matching the qualitative downward RNA-processing effect without requiring exact marker replication.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Measurable ataxia, ALS, stress-granule, and translation comparators mostly failed to phenocopy Atxn2.
finding_consequence: Atxn1 and Tardbp were transcriptionally active in 151 TH cells but shared at most a few Atxn2-signature genes, while Fmr1, Pum1, Tia1, Ddx3x, and Eif4g1 contributed no shared robust Atxn2-signature genes; the result is a direct rejection of simple disease-family or RBP-family interchangeability in this assay.

finding_summary: Atxn2 produced a true but extremely restricted transcriptomic response: only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
finding_consequence: This makes the thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c population the only context in this juvenile postmitotic brain screen where acute Atxn2 loss left a robust nuclear mRNA footprint; the many flat groups should be analyzed as informative non-results, not pooled away.

Pharmacologic pan-HSP90 inhibition does not complete the consequential transfer to selective genetic Hsp90ab1 loss, so the heat-shock non-engagement remains inferred; broader ER and adjacent-network claims are excluded.

finding_summary: In the main 151 response, Med13 perturbation down-regulated the cluster-name marker Prkcd together with Pcp4, Lrrtm1, Adgrb1, Plekhg1, Ildr2, Ramp3, and Zmat4.
finding_consequence: The top corrected gene is the marker that names the cell group, so the perturbation is best read as a weakening of a TH Prkcd neuronal identity and adhesion program rather than as a generic transcriptome-wide decrease.

finding_summary: Med13 also down-regulated glutamatergic and excitability genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, including Grin2b, Grm1, Kcnc2, Atp2a2, and Atp2b1.
finding_consequence: Human MED13 variants are linked to neurodevelopmental disease, and this postmitotic assay shows a possible later neuronal effector layer: receptor, potassium-channel, and calcium-handling transcripts rather than only early progenitor fate genes.

finding_summary: The data-driven Med13 signature converged with Ctnnb1, Cic, Atp6v0c, Psmb4, and Hspa9 perturbations, all of which repressed the same 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c genes in the same direction.

finding_summary: The strongest negative restricted-signature neighbors Setd5, Ankrd11, and Kmt2d inverted part of the Med13 thalamic program, up-regulating genes such as Prkcd, Grin2b, Plekhg1, Grm1, Kcnc2, Zmat4, or Atp2b1 that Med13 repressed.

finding_summary: P16 Med13 loss-of-function was sharply cell-type selective: 15 total FDR<0.10 downstream genes were confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, while 19 measured groups had no corrected response.

finding_summary: Slc12a5 loss induced a compact thalamic activity-response signature only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

finding_summary: The Slc12a5 thalamic module converged most strongly with calcium-homeostasis and metabolic perturbations, not with another chloride cotransporter.
finding_consequence: Atp2a2, Gfpt1, and Atp2b1 were the top three positive whole-screen neighbors of the 10-gene Slc12a5 signature and recapitulated the same Dusp1/Fos/IEG direction in 151, placing KCC2 loss in a thalamic activity- and homeostasis-coupled response module.
literature_rationale: Atp2a2, Gfpt1, and Atp2b1 are informative comparators with coherent same-direction recovery of the Slc12a5 activity signature. The relationship is data-supported despite lacking a target-specific literature bridge.

finding_summary: The thalamic signature extended beyond immediate-early genes to a small synaptic and membrane-trafficking tail.

finding_summary: The screen recovers an epilepsy-relevant activity gene only as a restricted secondary signature.

A flat snRNA response in most neuronal groups should therefore not be read as absence of KCC2 electrophysiology.

finding_summary: The three strongest negative whole-screen neighbors inverted the Slc12a5 thalamic signature rather than representing chloride biology.

finding_summary: Gabrb2, but not the other measured GABA-A/GABA-B/glycine receptor subunits, shared a thalamic activity edge with Slc12a5.

The response therefore reads out the consequence of losing the KCC2 chloride extruder rather than a generic CCC regulatory module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

literature_rationale: The 151 assay surface demonstrably detects canonical Wnt feedback under active Apc, Ctnnb1, and Tcf7l2 perturbations, making the absence of those genes after Tbl1xr1 loss an informative expected-program test. The source supports induced Wnt cofactor activity but not basal phenocopy of those comparators.

The recovered Tbl1xr1 module is therefore not a generic chromatin-remodeler signature.

literature_rationale: A target-specific, directional TRIP12-loss-to-p53-activation relationship conflicts with the informative RNA result, although dependence on ARF and oncogenic-stress context limits transportability.

Literature supports non-generic RNP consequences but not these particular signed relationships; sparse singleton placements are not retained.

finding_summary: P16 Zeb2 loss produced a real but narrow neuronal transcriptomic response, with the only multi-gene module in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
finding_consequence: The screen recovered a postnatal Pvalb-cell response rather than a pan-neuronal ZEB2 program, refining the known interneuron biology to a small survivor-state signature three to four weeks after sparse AAV-CRISPR loss of function.
