finding_consequence: The cross-screen match suggests that the Jun/Stmn4/Scg2 response is a generic lysosome/TSC/CAML adaptive module that can be engaged secondarily by Trio loss, rather than a direct readout of Rac1 or RhoA activity.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Postnatal Trio loss produced a very sparse, cell-class-restricted nuclear transcriptional phenotype: only 5 of 23 measured cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and those groups contained only 1, 1, 1, 4 and 2 hits.
finding_consequence: The main result is not a broad Rho-GTPase collapse but a weak survivor signature confined to a few mature neuronal classes; the many zeros must therefore be interpreted as part of the phenotype rather than as failed DE tables.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut; 052 Pvalb Gaba; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Midbrain and hindbrain-lineage responders up-regulated structural and small-GTPase-adjacent genes: Stmn4 in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, plus Dtna and Rapgef6 in 155 MB Glut.
finding_consequence: This is the clearest transcriptomic echo of Trio's cytoskeletal role; loss of a Rac/Rho GEF produced a compensatory module that touches microtubule dynamics, synapse organization and Rap-family GEF signaling rather than the canonical Trio transcript itself.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Measured Rho/Rac-pathway relatives and the paralog Kalrn failed to phenocopy Trio in the matched cell groups.
finding_consequence: Kalrn, Rac1, Cdc42, Tiam1, Dock7, Dock3, Sos1/2, Pak1/2/3 and Slit/Robo perturbations were directly queryable and did not share the Trio FDR signature, so the observed postnatal Trio response is not interchangeable with bulk loss of other Rho-family pathway nodes.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut; 052 Pvalb Gaba; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The human TRIO disease axis is not recapitulated as a broad acute loss-of-function transcriptome in juvenile mouse neurons.
finding_consequence: TRIO neurodevelopmental alleles can produce domain-specific RAC1 loss or hyperactivation and act during circuit formation; the P16 CRISPR screen recovered only a few adaptive genes, warning against interpreting an acute null signature as a complete model of pathogenic missense or gain-of-function TRIO alleles.

finding_summary: Tuba1a perturbation evoked tubulin-isotype bounce-back in Pvalb and thalamic glutamatergic neurons, whereas Tubb3 perturbation did not up-regulate alpha- or beta-tubulin paralogs in any measured group.
finding_consequence: The absence of compensation after Tubb3 is not because the assay cannot see tubulin homeostasis: the same screen detects coordinated Tubb3/Tubb2a/Tuba4a/Tubb4a/Tubb4b/Tubb5 induction after Tuba1a loss.
literature_rationale: Tuba1a provides an active positive control for coordinated tubulin-isotype induction in the matched groups, whereas Tubb3 perturbation lacks that expected program. A direct Tubb3-null study predicts compensation, making the informative absence directionally opposite.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The only cortical responder was 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, where Tubb3 knockdown coincided with borderline FDR decreases of Slc38a1 and Anapc4 but no tubulin-family or MAP transcript compensation.
finding_consequence: This converts a weak two-gene signal into a bounded interpretation: L4/5 IT neurons show a restricted metabolic/ubiquitin-housekeeping response, not a canonical microtubule transcriptional program.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: 191 MB P MY GABA showed a singleton induction of Rnf31 after Tubb3 perturbation.
finding_consequence: RNF31 is the catalytic LUBAC E3 ligase; its isolated up-regulation is a hypothesis-generating marker of ubiquitin/NF-kappa-B or survival buffering rather than evidence for a broad stress response.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Tubb3 had no robust data-driven convergent neighbor: the strongest non-control score correlations were only r≈0.04, and Cacna1g, Ephb1, Trp53, Fbxo11, and Akt3 failed to share Tubb3's three downstream genes.
finding_consequence: The pre-literature neighbor search argues that the Tubb3 signature is not a hidden member of a large recurrent Perturb-seq module; even the closest profiles are weak and cell-type-displaced.

finding_summary: Tubb3 did not phenocopy microtubule-motor perturbations: Dync1h1 and Kif1a produced sterol/SREBP-like responses in midbrain, hypothalamic, and hindbrain cells, while Tubb3 in the same axis produced only Rnf31 or no downstream genes.
finding_consequence: Because human TUBB3 mutations can perturb kinesin interactions, the divergence shows that acute beta-III-tubulin LoF in this assay is not equivalent to a generic axonal-transport or dynein-stress state.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Strongly engaged Atp6ap1 perturbations did not induce the expected lysosomal, autophagy, HIF, or iron-homeostasis transcriptional programs.
finding_consequence: ATP6AP1 biology may be expressed through V-ATPase assembly, organelle pH, vesicle loading, or proteostasis phenotypes that are not necessarily captured as acute cell-type-level mRNA changes.
literature_rationale: The literature provides relevant organelle-level mechanisms, while the informative dataset result concerns absence of compensatory transcription; these are not directly contradictory.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba; 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: The data-driven positive neighbours Atp6v0a1, Atp6v0c and Atp6ap2 replay the Atp6v0a1-low signature, implicating a V0/accessory module rather than a random Atp6v0a1 fluctuation.
finding_consequence: Cross-perturbation convergence makes the one-gene Atp6ap1 output interpretable: Atp6v0c produced stronger Atp6v0a1 loss in both responding groups and Atp6ap2 matched the direction, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
literature_rationale: Structural evidence completes the bridge for coarse V0/accessory-module convergence, but the extension adds a consequential breadth distinction not explained by that shared-complex membership.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Restricted negative-neighbour analysis nominated Rab7 and Cltc, with Rab7 driving the opposite Atp6v0a1 direction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: Late-endosomal disruption appears able to up-regulate, rather than down-regulate, the V-ATPase a1 transcript in the same TH class, a hypothesis-generating sign inversion relative to the Atp6ap1/V0c pattern.
literature_rationale: Narrowed to Rab7, the comparison is an exact-group, active-comparator sign inversion of Atp6v0a1 and remains a distinct powered relationship. Cltc is excluded as uninformative, and no source predicts the Rab7-dependent RNA sign.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Atp6ap1 produced a bona fide downstream transcriptomic effect only in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and the effect was the same V0-sector gene, Atp6v0a1, going down in both groups.
finding_consequence: The result converts an apparently ubiquitous V-ATPase component into a sharply restricted neuronal readout in this screen: most classes tolerated Atp6ap1 perturbation without an FDR-significant secondary state, whereas two classes coupled Ac45 loss to lower Atp6v0a1 mRNA.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: V1-sector perturbations in the screen, Atp6v1a, Atp6v1b2 and Atp6v1e1, did not phenocopy the Atp6ap1 Atp6v0a1 decrease in the two responding groups.
finding_consequence: This rejects a simple model in which any V-ATPase subunit perturbation feeds back onto Atp6v0a1 mRNA; the detectable Atp6ap1 response behaves as a V0/accessory-specific coupling.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The Pvalb downstream genes point to a secretory/synaptic state change rather than to a simple V-ATPase subunit replacement program.
finding_consequence: Scg2, Ptprn, and Slc6a17 were induced while Ntrk2 and Serpini1 were reduced, consistent with remodeling of vesicle/secretory and trophic state in the interneuron class where Atp6v1b2 loss was transcriptionally visible.
literature_rationale: The compatible secretory/transport induction and trophic-support withdrawal constitute a small but coherent Pvalb state program. V-ATPase synaptic-vesicle biology is target-proximal but does not predict the observed signed RNA pattern.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: Atp6v0c was the V-ATPase perturbation that most clearly converged with Atp6v1b2 in Pvalb interneurons.
finding_consequence: The same-complex V0 c-ring target was a top same-direction neighbor and recapitulated 5 of 11 Atp6v1b2 Pvalb genes, supporting that the small Atp6v1b2 signature reflects V-ATPase biology rather than an unrelated guide artifact.
literature_rationale: Both perturbations are informative in Pvalb neurons and share five same-direction FDR genes. ATP6V1B2 and ATP6V0C are obligate components of the coupled V1–V0 machine, providing a complete chain for coarse convergence.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: Canonical TFEB/autophagy, UPR/ISR, and proteasome subunit transcription were expected but absent from the Atp6v1b2 Pvalb response.
finding_consequence: The responder did not mount the usual lysosomal-capacity or protein-folding program that a strong organelle-acidification defect might elicit; the measured effect is therefore a restricted neuronal state change, not a generic acidification catastrophe.
literature_rationale: The references provide a target-specific lysosome/autophagy bridge, but they do not predict the direction of the measured RNA programs; therefore their absence is not a documented opposite result.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: Atp6v1b2 triggered a small Pvalb stress-feedback module led by Dusp1 and Gadd45g.
finding_consequence: The response contains an inducible MAPK/growth-arrest feedback component, indicating that the perturbation was sensed even though it did not escalate into a broad lysosomal or integrated-stress transcriptional program.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: The strongest full-profile neighbors were proteasome targets, but their convergence compressed to the same small Pvalb module rather than to Atp6v1b2 induction of proteasome mRNAs.
finding_consequence: Psmb4, Psmc1, and Psmc5 nominated a proteostasis/stress axis data-first, and Psmb4 shared 7 of the 11 Atp6v1b2 Pvalb genes, yet Atp6v1b2 itself left Psmb4 and Psmc1 at FDR 1.0.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: Atp6v1b2 produced a real but very narrow postnatal neuronal transcriptomic response: among 14 recovered cell groups, only 052 Pvalb Gaba had downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
finding_consequence: A core V-ATPase subunit was not a broad neuronal transcriptional hit under sparse P16 Cas9 loss of function; the response is concentrated in fast-spiking interneurons rather than distributed across the brain taxonomy.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: V-ATPase subunits were not interchangeable in this CRISPR/snRNA assay: Atp6v0c produced broad responses that Atp6v1b2 and the other measured V1/accessory subunits did not.
finding_consequence: This subunit hierarchy rejects a naive same-complex-equals-same-phenotype model and shows that the Atp6v1b2 nulls cannot be generalized to V-ATPase inactivity in those cells.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Endogenous Bscl2 depletion did not induce an ER-stress transcriptional program in the responsive 151 thalamic population, separating acute loss from the stress mechanism associated with dominant misfolding seipin alleles.
finding_consequence: Human BSCL2 disorders include recessive loss-of-function lipodystrophy and dominant neuropathy mutations that can misfold seipin and stress the ER; plain transcript depletion in mouse neurons did not reproduce a strong ER-stress-like RNA response, suggesting that disease-relevant stress may require chronic lipid imbalance, cell-type contexts outside this assay, or mutant protein gain of toxicity.
literature_rationale: The literature supports allele-mechanism separation and specifically ties mutant seipin to ER stress, but it does not provide a directional transcriptomic expectation for acute Bscl2 loss. The absence of an ER-stress RNA program therefore refines rather than contradicts the documented mutant-protein mechanism.

finding_summary: Hpf1 down-regulation is a single-gene Bscl2-responsive marker in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons.
finding_consequence: HPF1 connects the only robust transcriptomic effect of Bscl2 loss to PARP-dependent serine ADP-ribosylation and chromatin/DNA-repair regulation, a noncanonical branch relative to lipid-droplet seipin biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Acute Bscl2 loss was almost completely buffered transcriptionally, with real downstream signal confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The perturbation down-shifted the Bscl2 transcript in many neuronal classes, but only one thalamic class crossed downstream FDR, so the screen refines seipin biology to a sparse postmitotic neuronal response rather than a pan-neuronal ER/lipid program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The Bscl2 signature did not recover a lipid-droplet, PPARgamma/adipogenic, UPR, or integrated-stress program.
finding_consequence: Seipin's canonical biology is ER lipid-droplet assembly and toxic BSCL2 alleles can activate ER stress, yet none of the measured marker genes from those programs was FDR-significant even in the 151 responder group.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Neither data-driven signature neighbors nor literature-obvious ER/lipid and HSP comparators phenocopied Bscl2 in the 151 responder class.
finding_consequence: The nearest whole-screen neighbors had near-zero cosine similarity, and perturbations of Rab18, Reep1, Atl1, Spast, Kif5a, Pparg, Atf6, or Hspa5 did not reproduce Hpf1 down-regulation, arguing that the Bscl2 hit is not a generic ER-stress, motor-neuron-disease, or lipid-droplet-module signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Nr1d2 perturbation reciprocally induced Nr1d1 in the informative thalamic response, opposite the loss of Nr1d2 output after Clock perturbation.
finding_consequence: This places the strongest Clock-responsive gene, Nr1d2, inside feedback control: suppressing Clock lowers Nr1d2, whereas suppressing Nr1d2 releases Nr1d1 and some Dbp expression.
literature_rationale: The references explicitly place CLOCK upstream of NR1D/DBP transcription and REV-ERBs in the repressive feedback branch, forming a complete directional chain consistent with the observed reciprocal Clock and Nr1d2 perturbation responses.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Clock loss recurrently lowered Nr1d2 across six neuronal groups, including four groups in which Nr1d2 was the sole downstream FDR-supported readout.
finding_consequence: A REV-ERB paralog is the most sensitive measured readout of acute neuronal Clock-Bmal1 inhibition; Dbp and Tef joined only in the larger 151/155 multi-gene signatures.
literature_rationale: This is not an arbitrary biomarker: it is a canonical, directionally predicted Clock-to-output edge replicated in six cell groups. The claim is narrowed to the observed recurrent decrease and does not assert universal sensitivity or cell-type selectivity.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Only the 151 thalamic and 155 midbrain glutamatergic groups resolved a multi-gene circadian-output module, with Dbp and Tef down in both and Per3 additionally down in 155; Hhatl was the lone noncanonical FDR hit.
finding_consequence: The significant DE surface in Clock responders is narrow and almost entirely canonical clock output, leaving little evidence for secondary ISR, proteostasis, lysosomal or synaptic homeostatic programs after 3-4 weeks of postmitotic Clock disruption.
literature_rationale: Repeated decreases in canonical CLOCK-BMAL1 outputs define a coherent circadian-output program in the two multi-gene responders. Direct CLOCK control and positive-limb regulation fully predict the qualitative direction without requiring exact cell-group replication.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The same-complex comparator Bmal1 was the strongest data-driven positive neighbor of Clock but was broader and stronger, sharing 8 same-direction Clock hits and adding FDR-significant Nr1d2/Nr1d1/Dbp responses in Clock-weak groups.
finding_consequence: The paired perturbations separate a nonredundant ARNTL/BMAL1 node from a partially buffered CLOCK node: the screen detects the circadian circuit when the obligate partner is hit, but Clock single loss is visibly buffered in several matched neuronal groups.
literature_rationale: The active Bmal1 perturbation shares same-coordinate circadian effects with Clock and is broader, as predicted by BMAL1 nonredundancy and CLOCK compensation by NPAS2. Groups listed only for additional Bmal1 responses are excluded from Clock's focal program placement.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The top data-driven opposing overlaps came from broad pleiotropic perturbations, not from a dedicated circadian antagonist: Srsf1 overlapped seven Clock hits but with mixed signs, and Uba5 opposed only Dbp in two groups.
finding_consequence: A gene-level clock-output overlap is not automatically a clock mechanism; the exact-overlap screen prioritizes Bmal1 as the specific positive neighbor and flags Srsf1/Uba5 as broad, low-specificity contrasts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Clock loss produced a real but sharply restricted transcriptional response: 6 of 22 tested neuronal groups had downstream FDR<0.10 genes, whereas cortical, hippocampal, striatal and cerebellar groups were weak or null.
finding_consequence: The dominant phenotype is not a pan-neuronal stress or synaptic response; it is a sparse recovery of a circadian-output program in selected subcortical and pineal-enriched neuronal groups during the P37-44 postmitotic window.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Other measurable circadian-loop genes did not phenocopy Clock: Cry1, Cry2, Nr1d1, Nr1d2, Rora/Rorb/Rorc and Tef produced sparse or different FDR surfaces rather than the Clock Nr1d2-Dbp-Tef program.
finding_consequence: Membership in the clock network is directional. Loss of a repressor, nuclear receptor, or output factor cannot be assumed to mimic loss of the Clock positive limb in postmitotic neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: The canonical CPT1C-GluA1/SAC1/AMPAR axis was not recovered as an RNA program.
finding_consequence: Cpt1c loss did not change Gria1-4, TARP, Dlg4, or Sacm1l transcripts at FDR<0.10, and direct Gria/Cacng/Dlg4 perturbations were themselves almost flat; this converts an apparent absence of AMPAR genes into a readout-boundary result rather than a missed textbook hit.
literature_rationale: Direct Cpt1c evidence shows unchanged AMPAR mRNA despite altered protein trafficking and function, supporting the qualified RNA non-recovery claim. The nearly silent receptor and scaffold perturbations are weak comparator context and cannot independently establish divergence.

finding_summary: The strongest positive Cpt1c responder was an isolated increase of Mfn2 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
finding_consequence: Mfn2 provides a focused ER-mitochondrial stress/mitochondrial-dynamics hypothesis for a Cpt1c-sensitive cortical population, but no other mitochondrial or UPR transcript crossed FDR, so this is a single-gene candidate rather than a pathway activation call.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Cpt1c perturbation produced an isolated Cnnm2 decrease in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
finding_consequence: The result nominates magnesium/divalent-cation handling as a hypothalamic glutamatergic RNA marker of Cpt1c loss, distinct from the AMPAR genes expected from the trafficking literature.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: Restricted Cpt1c signature neighbors were nominal and failed the FDR-level feature test, whereas inverse Tsc1 produced a broad 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut response.
finding_consequence: The leading top-200 cosine neighbors, Calm1, Grm1, Gria4, and Ppargc1a, and the inverse neighbor Chrna6 look similar only in a restricted low-amplitude signature; none reproduced Cpt1c Mfn2 or Cnnm2 at FDR<0.10. Tsc1 shows that the same cell group can produce hundreds of DE genes when a perturbation engages a transcriptional pathway.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: SPG73/HSP biology did not appear as an acute L5 ET or ATL1/SPAST-like transcriptomic phenotype.
finding_consequence: Human CPT1C disease is tied to a heterozygous ER/lipid-droplet-altering variant and motor-neuron axonopathy; the flat L5 ET, Atl1, and Spast surfaces argue that this Perturb-seq design does not model that adult long-axon, allele-specific disease mechanism.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut

finding_summary: Hsf1 perturbation recurrently decreased Rsrp1 in Pvalb, thalamic, and midbrain neuronal responders.
finding_consequence: Rsrp1 was FDR-significant in the three strongest multi-gene Hsf1 signatures and was down in every Hsf1 cell type, making it a useful transcriptomic sentinel even though its mechanistic placement downstream of HSF1 is unknown.
literature_rationale: General HSF1 transcription-factor biology cannot support the specific recurrent decrease of Rsrp1. The relationship remains a screen-defined candidate edge.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Hsf1 loss decreased a compact Hsph1/HSP90/cochaperone transcript program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
finding_consequence: The direct phenotype matches the sign expected for losing a heat-shock transcription factor, but shows a narrow basal requirement in unstressed postmitotic neurons rather than pan-neuronal heat-shock collapse.
literature_rationale: The literature directly supports the target-specific transcriptional mechanism and predicts the observed decrease in the canonical chaperone module. Restriction or relative strength across neuronal groups affects transportability, not the completeness of this core directional bridge.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 052 Pvalb Gaba; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: Proteasome subunit perturbations are the major opposite neighbors of Hsf1.
finding_consequence: Psmc5, Psmb4 and Psmc1 up-regulated the same Hsph1/HSP90 genes that Hsf1 loss lowered, providing an in-assay stress positive control and showing that snRNA-seq would detect secondary HSP transcription when proteotoxic stress is generated.
literature_rationale: Three strongly active proteasome comparators repeatedly induce the same chaperone genes lowered by Hsf1 loss. Proteasome-stress activation of HSF1-dependent transcription completes the mechanistic chain predicting this opposition.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The Hsf1 phenotype is not a generic heat-shock-factor or chaperone-family loss signature.
finding_consequence: Hsf4 was completely flat and Hsp90ab1 had robust self-knockdown without downstream DE; Hspa5, Hspa8, Hspa9 and Hspd1 were null or different. This rejects simple paralog or single-HSP phenocopy in this assay.
literature_rationale: The family-wide claim must be narrowed to engaged or active comparators such as Hsp90ab1 and Hspa9. Flat Hsf4 and Hspd1 cannot establish non-phenocopy, while the specialization source does not predict the entire acute neuronal comparator pattern.

finding_summary: TH Prkcd/Grin2c and midbrain glutamatergic neurons carried the strongest Hsf1-dependent chaperone signal.
finding_consequence: Most of the resolved basal HSF1 output came from posterior glutamatergic classes: TH Prkcd/Grin2c cells lost six transcripts and MB Glut cells lost Hsph1, Stip1, and Rsrp1.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Ppp2r1a, Sin3a, U2af2 and spliceosome-associated perturbations converge on Hsf1 through a restricted Rsrp1/TH-chaperone module.
finding_consequence: The strongest same-direction neighbors were not HSF-family genes, nominating Rsrp1 and a small RNA-processing-adjacent branch of the basal neuronal stress network.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Hsf1 loss did not trigger a broad secondary UPR, ISR, autophagy, lysosomal or proteasome-bounce-back program.
finding_consequence: Canonical stress transcripts were measured but not significant, so acute basal Hsf1 loss mostly subtracts chaperone transcription rather than creating a transcriptomically visible proteostasis crisis over 3-4 weeks.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Kifbp decreased Srebf2 but did not activate the broad sterol-response module that Pcyt2 and Dctn1 perturbations triggered in the same cell group.
finding_consequence: Srebf2 is interpretable as a point depression of a cholesterol transcription factor, not as a full SREBP2 target-gene wave downstream of Kifbp.
literature_rationale: The strong Srebf2 decrease without accompanying sterol targets is an informative program-level uncoupling test because active Pcyt2 and Dctn1 controls produced the canonical program in the same group. No target-specific Kifbp-to-SREBP2 or sterol-program bridge is supplied.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The only cortical excitatory responder, 001 L5-6 IT Glut, uniquely induced Exosc10 and Plekhm2 after Kifbp perturbation.
finding_consequence: Exosc10 points to RNA-exosome surveillance and Plekhm2 to kinesin-linked lysosome motility, so the L5-6 response is more consistent with a small RNA-quality/endolysosomal compensation than with a canonical axon-growth program.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut

finding_summary: Kifbp and the data-driven neighbor Srsf1 converged on Dazap1 up-regulation in 046 CTX-CGE GABA and on Srebf2 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The sparse Kifbp signature connects most reproducibly to an RNA-processing perturbation rather than to the literature-obvious kinesin targets.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Literature-obvious kinesin and KBP-neighbor perturbations did not phenocopy Kifbp in the matched responder cell types.
finding_consequence: The lack of shared Exosc10, Plekhm2, Dazap1, or Srebf2 regulation separates the acute P16 Kifbp signature from direct perturbation of Kif1a, Kif1b, Stmn2, Cit, Ret, and neuronal Kif5 motors in the same screen.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut; 046 CTX-CGE GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Klc1 loss produced a single robust Pvalb response: Agtpbp1/CCP1 decreased in 052 Pvalb Gaba and was not FDR-significant for any other target in that same cell group.
finding_consequence: Agtpbp1 encodes a tubulin deglutamylase implicated in neuronal microtubule health, so its selective reduction is the only transcriptomic bridge from KLC1 to the microtubule post-translational code in this acute screen.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: Anapc4 was induced by Klc1 in 191 MB P MY GABA, converged in the same direction with Snrnp70, and split from the broad Kansl1 signature in the opposite direction.
finding_consequence: The APC/C subunit is not a canonical kinesin cargo, but its recurrent, sign-sensitive behavior nominates an ubiquitin-ligase/proteostasis node as the main midbrain/hindbrain GABAergic readout of Klc1 rather than a generic neuronal-stress wave.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Klc1 did not induce APP/CB1R/neurotrophin-cargo transcripts or JNK/tau/UPR/autophagy stress markers despite literature linking KLC1 loss to APP transport, CB1R axon guidance, aged tau stress, and RPE phagosome pathology.
finding_consequence: For KLC1, the expected biology is cargo localization and chronic axonal integrity, not an immediate juvenile nucleus-wide stress transcriptome; a lack of App, Cnr1, Mapt, Jun, Hspa5, Ddit3, or Sqstm1 DE is therefore informative rather than an assay failure.

finding_summary: Acute partial Snrpn targeting did not converge with the assayed Prader-Willi-region perturbations, supporting separation of isolated SmN reduction from a multi-transcript imprinted-locus lesion.
finding_consequence: PWS genetics implicate a paternally expressed locus rather than an isolated acute fall in Snrpn coding RNA; the dataset supports separating SNRPN as a locus marker from the immediate transcriptomic consequences of partial SmN reduction.
literature_rationale: The literature defines PWS as an imprinted-locus disorder and reports severe effects from a larger paternal deletion while an Snrpn exon deletion alone lacked an obvious phenotype. This completes a target-to-locus-mechanism chain supporting the observed nonconvergence, with weak engagement of some comparators limiting confidence in its breadth rather than breaking the bridge.

finding_summary: Nr4a1 RNA induction was not a robust or universal response to partial Snrpn loss across the assayed neuronal groups.
finding_consequence: NR4A1 antagonism has been proposed from embryonic cortical culture phenotypes; these mouse-brain Perturb-seq cell classes do not support Nr4a1 mRNA as a universal pharmacodynamic marker of partial Snrpn loss.
literature_rationale: The cited study supplies a direct, directional SNRPN-knockdown-to-NR4A1-increase relationship. Thus, the absence of canonical NF-kappaB transcripts in a transcriptionally responsive neuronal surface is informative but not a decisive directional disagreement.

finding_summary: Msrb2 and Galk2 were part of the FDR<0.10 Usp48 signature in 151, pointing to a small mitochondrial redox and carbohydrate-metabolism arm.

finding_summary: Camk2b depletion did not induce transcriptional replacement by measured CaMKII paralogs or CaMKII inhibitor genes.

finding_summary: Camk2b depletion did not phenocopy the broad transcriptional programs produced by Grin1, Grin2a, or Grin2b perturbation in matched neuronal classes.
finding_consequence: CaMKII is a postsynaptic NMDA-receptor effector, but the same broad neuronal classes that showed target-only Camk2b signatures could mount large GRIN-dependent RNA programs. CAMK2B depletion therefore should not be treated as a transcriptomic surrogate for upstream receptor loss.
literature_rationale: The references provide a specific NMDAR-to-CaMKII pathway bridge, but pathway adjacency alone does not decide whether upstream receptor loss and downstream effector loss should yield equivalent RNA states.

finding_summary: Partial postnatal Camk2b transcript loss is not a transcriptomic surrogate for regulatory CAMK2B disease alleles that alter kinase control and development.

The mouse Perturb-seq result shows that partial Camk2b mRNA reduction in broad neuronal classes is not sufficient to trigger a broad RNA phenotype, warning that variant-specific kinase regulation, developmental timing, and cellular physiology may be more informative therapeutic readouts.
literature_rationale: Variant-specific kinase and developmental mechanisms support the proposed distinction, but the decisive bridge to the observed sparse loss-of-transcript program is missing.

finding_summary: Chchd10 did not engage the OMA1/DELE1-like integrated-stress program that the same screen readily detected after Opa1 or Dnm1l perturbation.

The physical CHCHD10–TDP-43 connection does not itself predict this transcriptomic divergence, and no positive Chchd10 program warrants cell placement.

finding_summary: Gbf1 perturbation failed to induce the expected UPR/ER-stress transcriptional program despite producing a detectable neuronal-state response.
finding_consequence: GBF1 depletion or inhibition can provoke ER stress, XBP1/UPR activation, autophagy, and death in other cellular contexts; the absence of FDR-significant Hspa5, Ddit3, Atf4, Xbp1, Herpud1, or related induction in the mouse-brain screen suggests this perturbation was not equivalent to acute Golgi blockade.
literature_rationale: The references directly connect GBF1 depletion to UPR activation. The dataset showed an alternative neuronal-state response but no canonical UPR induction, making the result directionally opposite. Differences in cell context and weak Gbf1 RNA engagement reduce confidence but do not remove the direct bridge.

finding_summary: The 151 Gbf1 signature was dominated by loss of neuronal-state and neurite-associated transcripts rather than by Golgi or ER-stress genes.
finding_consequence: Cck, Nsg1, Stmn2, Tuba1a, Thy1, and Slc25a12 falling together points to a neuronal homeostatic-state change in thalamic neurons, while the canonical secretory-stress program remained absent.
literature_rationale: The coordinated six-gene neuronal-state withdrawal is a defensible positive program. The underpowered absence of UPR and purported contradiction are excluded because target engagement and stress-marker estimates are uncertain; literature supplies no bridge to the surviving neuronal program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Gbf1's sparse signature converged most strongly with proteasome and organellar-stress perturbations, especially Psmb4, Psmc5, Gfpt1, Atp6v0c, Atp2a2, and Sec31a.

literature_rationale: The comparators are strongly active in 151 and reproduce most of the small but coherent Gbf1 neuronal-withdrawal signature with matching signs. Literature supports a GBF1-to-organelle-stress edge but not the specific neuronal program or convergence with each comparator.

finding_summary: Klf7 perturbation produced an eight-gene, predominantly down-regulated cytoskeletal and membrane-associated molecular response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons.
finding_consequence: Klf7 has strong developmental neurobiology, but this screen localizes an acute P16 loss-of-function transcriptomic response to one thalamic glutamatergic class rather than to cortex, hippocampus, midbrain, or inhibitory neurons.
literature_rationale: The literature directly supports a KLF7-to-neuronal-structural-program bridge, consistent with the observed cytoskeletal response, but it does not provide a decisive directional expectation for replay of the nominated developmental targets in this surface.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Trrap was the strongest same-direction screen neighbor of Klf7 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The nearest neighbor was data-derived rather than a KLF paralog: Trrap shared significant same-direction down-regulation of Tuba1a, Sptan1, Rgs11, Ahnak2 and Pgm2l1 within a much larger 626-gene thalamic response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The AP-2 clathrin-adaptor subunit Ap2s1 was the strongest anti-neighbor of Klf7 and reversed most of the Klf7 eight-gene module in 151.
finding_consequence: Ap2s1 produced a large 1498-gene thalamic response and significantly changed six of eight Klf7 genes in the opposite sign, converting the tiny Klf7 module into a directional axis rather than isolated one-off DEGs.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The thalamic Klf7 signature was a small cytoskeletal/membrane-associated program rather than the canonical embryonic olfactory KLF7 target program.
finding_consequence: Tuba1a, Coro1a, Flot1, Ahnak2, Pgm2l1, Rgs11 and Sptan1 fell in 151, whereas Cdkn1a, Cdkn1b, L1cam, Omp and generic axon-growth markers did not pass FDR<0.10 anywhere; the screen therefore refined Klf7 biology away from its best-known olfactory neuroblast targets.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Screened KLF-family perturbations did not phenocopy Klf7 in the Klf7 responder class.
finding_consequence: Klf9, an axon-growth suppressive KLF in retinal-ganglion literature, was the second strongest negative 151 neighbor but had a distinct 19-gene up-biased response; Klf1, Klf11, Klf12 and Klf13 were flat or nearly flat. The family is therefore not interchangeable in this P16 thalamic context.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Lonp1 induced its Ddit3-centered stress program where Clpp, Clpx, Afg3l2, Hspd1, and Yme1l1 did not reproduce it.
finding_consequence: The response was not a generic readout of perturbing any mitochondrial proteostasis gene; in these cells Lonp1 was a more effective trigger of the Ddit3/Shmt2/Aldh1l2 module than the assayed CLPXP and inner-membrane protease neighbors.
literature_rationale: The Lonp1-to-ISR arm is strongly target-specific, but the focal finding is a cross-perturbation boundary. Functional relatedness alone cannot establish the observed ranking or non-phenocopy of the comparator perturbations.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Lonp1 induced a compact ISR-like mitochondrial stress module in 155 MB Glut and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, centered on Ddit3 with Shmt2, Aldh1l2, and Slc7a1.
finding_consequence: The positive signal is biologically interpretable despite only seven FDR-supported downstream genes: it points to ATF4/CHOP-linked one-carbon and amino-acid stress rather than nonspecific transcriptomic collapse.
literature_rationale: Despite few DEGs, recurrent Ddit3 and compatible one-carbon and amino-acid stress genes define a compact coherent ISR-like program. Direct LONP1-depletion evidence establishes mitochondrial proteostasis failure and ISR activation in the same direction.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Lonp1 perturbation increased the ER unfolded-protein-response transcript Herpud1 in P MY Pineal glutamatergic neurons.
finding_consequence: These FDR-supported non-mitochondrial genes show that the sparse response contains a secondary quality-control arm, not only canonical mitochondrial one-carbon genes.
literature_rationale: The original three-gene ER/membrane arm was over-grouped because Emc3, Herpud1, and Rtn3 did not co-occur and had mixed directions. The Herpud1 increase nevertheless survives independently as a specifically supported expected readout; no comparable claim is made for Emc3 or Rtn3.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Opa1 and Hspa9 were the accepted positive signature neighbors of Lonp1 and reproduced the Ddit3, amino-acid transport, and one-carbon module more broadly than Lonp1 itself.
finding_consequence: Same-screen convergence shows that the Lonp1 signature is a mitochondrial proteostasis signature even though Lonp1 alone has few significant genes.
literature_rationale: The corrected load-bearing relationship is the informative Opa1–Lonp1 convergence on an ISR program: loss of each target is independently linked to that same signed effect. HSPA9 remains useful empirical context but is excluded from the literature-agreement claim because the supplied shared-machine edge does not establish its signed ISR response.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: The literature-obvious mitochondrial protease comparators Afg3l2, Yme1l1, Clpp, Clpx, and Hspd1 did not phenocopy Lonp1 in this assay.
finding_consequence: The negative comparator test prevents collapsing all mitochondrial protein-quality-control genes into one transcriptional module; Lonp1 aligned with Opa1/Hspa9 stress, not with the CLPXP/YME1L/AFG3L2 set.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 155 MB Glut; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Postnatal neuronal Lonp1 loss-of-function did not phenocopy the breadth of congenital LONP1 disease; only 3 of 23 measured neuronal groups had any FDR-supported downstream response.
finding_consequence: The result argues that CODAS and classical mitochondrial-disease mechanisms are likely displaced to developmental lineages, stronger alleles, or contexts outside sparse P16 neuronal editing, rather than a uniform mature-neuron transcriptional syndrome.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 155 MB Glut; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Map2k1 loss selectively depressed a narrow ERK-output, neuropeptide/synaptic module in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons.
finding_consequence: This is the clearest positive biology in the screen: it localizes basal MEK1-dependent transcription to a thalamic neuronal class and identifies Vgf, Ptpn5, Etv5, and Unc13a as its measured output genes.
literature_rationale: Direct neural genetic evidence links Map2k1/Map2k2 loss to disappearance of ERK-response transcripts, and neuronal studies place Etv5 and Vgf downstream of MEK–ERK signaling. The observed decreases therefore match the documented pathway direction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: 191 MB P MY GABA carried a real but two-gene response, Uso1 up and Las1l down, that was separate from the thalamic ERK-output module.
finding_consequence: This keeps the caudal GABAergic signal as a measured response without over-merging it into the canonical Vgf/Etv5/Ptpn5 thalamic program.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The Map2k1 thalamic module is pathway-selective: Braf converges, Nf1 inverts, but Map2k2 and most receptor/Ras/ERK neighbors do not phenocopy it.
finding_consequence: Testing directly measured relatives prevents a generic RAS-MAPK interpretation; the result points to a BRAF/SHOC2/MEK1-biased basal branch in this cell group rather than pathway-wide interchangeability.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The screen recovered Etv5/Vgf/Ptpn5 but not a full Fos/Egr/Dusp/Spry immediate-early or feedback program after postnatal Map2k1 loss.
finding_consequence: It distinguishes a basal transcriptional dependency from the broad activity- or growth-factor-evoked ERK program that the snRNA assay might have missed in unstimulated juvenile neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Across six FDR-engaged neuronal groups, Ndufb8 depletion failed to produce a coordinated oxidative-phosphorylation transcriptional shutdown; the only downstream call was Puf60 in 308 CB GABA.
finding_consequence: For an inner-membrane complex-I subunit, a sparse scRNA response implies that the acute phenotype is not a large transcriptional OXPHOS shutdown and is more likely to reside at protein-complex, activity, or metabolic-output levels.
literature_rationale: The references provide a specific NDUFB8-to-complex-I functional bridge, but primarily at the protein-complex, assembly, and respiratory-function levels. They do not decisively predict the tested RNA program, so its absence is a refinement rather than agreement or disagreement.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Prkag2 was selectively up-regulated after Ndufb8 perturbation in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
finding_consequence: PRKAG2 is an AMPK nucleotide-binding subunit, so the result nominates a cortical L2/3 energy-sensor compensation marker without a full ISR or autophagy program.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

finding_summary: Puf60 was selectively up-regulated after Ndufb8 perturbation in 308 CB GABA.
finding_consequence: The only cerebellar-GABA hit is an RNA-binding splicing factor rather than an OXPHOS transcript, nominating a noncanonical, cell-class-restricted response marker.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Complex-I and complex-I-biogenesis comparators were also nearly flat: 25 targets produced 21 downstream FDR<0.10 calls in 550 target-by-cell-group tests, and none reproduced the two exact Ndufb8 responder genes.
finding_consequence: A same-complex prior predicted that at least some NDUF genes might phenocopy one another; instead the screen shows module-level transcriptomic buffering under this assay design.

finding_summary: Ppib loss did not induce the collagen-PCP, ER-chaperone, or UPR/ISR genes that would be expected if collagen clients were retained in the ER.
finding_consequence: UPR genes are detectable in this screen after other perturbations, so the absence of Hspa5/Ddit3/Atf4/Xbp1 and ER-chaperone remodeling reads as a biologically informative absence in neurons rather than a generic limitation of single-nucleus RNA-seq.
literature_rationale: The cited PPIB-deficient patient fibroblasts directly connect PPIB-complex impairment to collagen retention and PERK-UPR activation. Differences between matrix-producing fibroblasts and neurons affect transportability but do not erase this signed target-specific bridge.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut; 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The brain-neuron null localizes PPIB loss-of-function biology away from a broad postmitotic neuronal transcriptional requirement and toward unsampled collagen-rich matrix lineages.
finding_consequence: PPIB's best-established Mendelian disease is osteogenesis imperfecta type 9; the screen shows that the same gene can be broadly expressed and knocked down in neurons without producing the collagen/UPR transcriptome that drives matrix-cell pathology.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut; 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut; 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut; 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut; 022 L5 ET CTX Glut; 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut; 046 CTX-CGE GABA; 052 Pvalb Gaba; 053 Sst Gaba; 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 217 P MY Pineal Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Neither restricted-signature neighbors nor the assayed immunophilin/chaperone comparators revealed a robust Ppib-convergent downstream surface.
finding_consequence: Cross-perturbation comparison prevents overinterpreting nominal Ppib genes: the top data-driven correlations were small, Kremen1/Tomm40/Npy1r were downstream-null in matched groups, and the only assayed PPIase-family comparator Fkbp1a was also downstream-null.

finding_summary: Prnp LoF did not evoke UPR/ISR, autophagy-lysosome, oxidative-stress, apoptosis, or immediate-early synaptic transcriptional programs.
finding_consequence: Prion diseases are proteopathic and neurodegenerative, so these secondary programs were the obvious transcriptional outputs to look for; their absence, despite strong Prnp self-depletion in several groups and despite recovery of a UPR-like Hspa5 response in the same assay, refines the result to 'acute PrPC lowering is transcriptionally buffered' rather than 'the assay missed all stress biology'.
literature_rationale: Target depletion and the active Hspa5 positive control make the broad stress-program absence informative. A closely matched Prnp disruption study nevertheless reported a subtle oxidative-stress response, directly opposing the categorical oxidative-program null while not contradicting every other tested program.

finding_summary: Prnp loss produced a single significant DnaJ/Hsp40-family co-chaperone signal, Dnajc27 up-regulation, only in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
finding_consequence: The strongest Prnp downstream transcript is not a pan-neuronal prion transcriptome; it is a cell-restricted, one-gene candidate for an Hsp70/co-chaperone compensation that can be followed up only in CNU-MGE-lineage neurons.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA

finding_summary: Prnp loss lowered Setd1b only in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
finding_consequence: The hypothalamic/hypothalamic-mammillary glutamatergic arm of the Prnp signature is chromatin-regulator-like rather than synaptic or UPR-like, and it reached only FDR 0.056, making it a restricted biomarker hypothesis rather than a pathway claim.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: The unbiased Prnp signature neighbors had near-zero global correlations and did not share the two FDR genes.
finding_consequence: The actual screen nominates a sparse, nearly singleton Prnp signature; even the top positive neighbors Htr2a, Kif21a, Foxc2, Coa8, and Smc1a and the top negative neighbors Kcnb1, Dstyk, Sin3a, Sh3kbp1, and Nhs are correlation neighbors only, not phenocopies.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: PRNP-network perturbations in APP/Fyn/mGluR5/NCAM/LRP1/CaV/HSPA5/SNCA/CSNK2B space did not phenocopy Prnp.
finding_consequence: PrPC is embedded in synaptic and amyloid-beta receptor networks, but in this postnatal LoF assay those neighbours either were flat or fired different FDR genes; the Dnajc27/Setd1b signature is therefore not a generic readout of APP-PrPC-Fyn or PrPC adhesion/calcium signaling.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: Timp2 loss produced a single robust downstream neuronal transcript: Dab2ip was up-regulated in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, while every other significant row in the Timp2 surface was the Timp2 transcript itself.
finding_consequence: This makes Dab2ip a narrow, hypothesis-generating marker of Timp2-sensitive hippocampal/amygdalar-lineage glutamatergic neurons rather than evidence for a broad MMP or injury-stress transcriptome.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut

finding_summary: The assayed TIMP paralog Timp3 did not phenocopy Timp2: it failed to up-regulate Dab2ip in 012 and produced only Syp down-regulation in 046 CTX-CGE GABA.
finding_consequence: This rejects simple interchangeability between TIMP inhibitors in the postnatal neuronal CRISPR readout and shows that family membership did not predict the one Timp2-responsive gene or cell class.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut; 046 CTX-CGE GABA

finding_summary: Atad1 did not induce the mitochondrial integrated-stress program that was readily detected after Dnm1l and Opa1 perturbation in the same 151 TH class.
finding_consequence: The null is informative for the organelle-stress hypothesis: if Atad1 loss had generated a large DDIT3/ASNS/CHAC1 amino-acid stress response, this screen and this cell class could have detected it.
literature_rationale: Dnm1l and Opa1 provide active matched positive controls showing that the 151 group can detect a mitochondrial ISR, making its absence after engaged Atad1 perturbation informative. ATAD1 quality-control biology does not itself supply a specific signed ISR prediction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Atad1 produced exactly one downstream FDR<0.10 hit in the entire measured screen: Smarcd1 was mildly induced in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: This preserves the only positive Atad1 transcriptomic signal without inflating it into a pathway; it is at most an exploratory marker of a thalamic/habenular glutamatergic response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The ATAD1-AMPAR axis did not convert into a nuclear RNA phenotype: Gria1, Gria2, Gria3, Gria4, and Grip1 perturbations were also essentially flat in the matched 151 TH class and across the Atad1-measured groups.
finding_consequence: This separates the literature's receptor-surface trafficking phenotype from the snRNA-seq axis used here; failure to recover an AMPAR module should not be read as evidence that ATAD1 cannot affect synapses.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Atad1 did not converge with screened peroxisomal target perturbations Pex1, Pex13, Pex14, or Abcd3; those comparators were sparse and non-overlapping, and Pex13's Insig1 signal in 151 TH was absent after Atad1 perturbation.
finding_consequence: Although ATAD1 also localizes to the peroxisomal membrane, its postnatal neuronal LoF signature is not a generic peroxisome-biogenesis or peroxisomal transport signature in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: The P5B ATPase paralog-family comparator Atp13a3 was also flat, with 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 22 measured groups.
finding_consequence: The screen did not reveal an acute neuronal transcriptional module shared simply by losing type V P-type ATPases.

finding_summary: Atp13a2 failed to converge with screened Parkinson/endolysosomal network genes: most were flat and Vps35 produced a small 151 TH-skewed response rather than an Atp13a2-like program.
finding_consequence: Disease-network proximity did not imply a shared acute loss-of-function transcriptome in juvenile neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Caly loss did not phenocopy the substantially broader transcriptional responses caused by core clathrin/AP2 perturbations, including in 191 MB P MY GABA.
finding_consequence: Although CALY is a clathrin light-chain interactor, the small score-vector correlations argue that its acute transcriptional consequences are adapter-specific and not a proxy for disabling clathrin-mediated endocytosis globally.
literature_rationale: A specific CALY-to-clathrin/endocytosis bridge is documented, including selective neuronal trafficking phenotypes, but the decisive link to transcriptomic non-equivalence with core coat machinery is absent.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Caly produced a single robust downstream transcriptome hit, down-regulation of the Polycomb transcript Phc2, and only in 191 MB P MY GABA neurons.
finding_consequence: This is the only positive Caly response in the whole measured surface; the solitary Phc2 hit is therefore a hypothesis-generating marker of a hindbrain/midbrain GABA state rather than a recovered clathrin, AMPAR, or dopamine-receptor program.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Unbiased whole-screen neighbors were essentially absent; the strongest positive and negative Caly score-cosines were near zero.
finding_consequence: The sparse Caly signature is not a hidden member of a broad module nominated by unrelated targets: top positive neighbors Syncrip, Pfkm, and Trp53 had cosines only 0.031 to 0.029, and top negative neighbors Atp6ap1, Ntrk2, and Glmn were only -0.016 to -0.013.

finding_summary: Caly did not phenocopy core clathrin/AP2 perturbations even in the only Caly-responsive class.
finding_consequence: Cltc and Ap2s1 perturbations produced multi-gene 191 MB P MY GABA signatures, and Ap2s1/Ap2m1/Cltc each had broad responses elsewhere, showing that the screen can detect transcriptional consequences of damaging endocytic-coat perturbations; the one-gene Caly response is therefore a selective peripheral phenotype, not a generic endocytosis signature.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Cdh2 did not activate a β-catenin/Wnt transcriptional program in the thalamic group where Apc, Ctnnb1, and Tcf7l2 produced large FDR-backed signatures.
finding_consequence: A simple model in which acute N-cadherin loss releases β-catenin to drive nuclear Wnt output is rejected in this P16 sparse neuronal context; the Wnt arm was detectable in the same screen and cell group when perturbed directly.
literature_rationale: Cdh2 perturbation was engaged and the canonical Wnt output was detectable through active matched comparators, making non-activation informative. Target-specific neural Cdh2 loss directly produced reduced rather than released Wnt signaling.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Cdh2 uncoupled from the actin-compensation response observed after Actb perturbation.
finding_consequence: Although cadherin-catenin complexes mechanically connect to actin, removing Cdh2 did not trigger the multi-group Actg1/Flna/Vcl/Myh10/Tpm1 response seen after Actb loss, arguing that the N-cadherin perturbation was not perceived as a global actin cytoskeletal insult by these nuclei.
literature_rationale: Actb supplies an active recurrent compensation surface, while the broadly measured and target-engaged Cdh2 perturbation lacks that response. Cadherin–actin coupling motivates the test but does not predict the specific transcriptional divergence.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Cdh2 did not converge with the β-catenin destruction/TCF axis despite Ctnnb1, Apc, Tcf7l2, Lrp6, and Gsk3b perturbations being measured in the same matched neuronal groups.
finding_consequence: Same-pathway and same-complex membership did not predict a shared Perturb-seq state; Wnt-core perturbations were concentrated in thalamic neurons, but Cdh2 remained downstream-null there.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Several individual adhesion and catenin-family perturbations phenocopied Cdh2's transcriptional buffering rather than producing strong signatures.
finding_consequence: Ctnna2, Ctnna3, Ctnnd2, Ncam1, Nectin1, Pcdh15, and Pcdh19 were flat or near-flat, suggesting that acute loss of one neuronal adhesion component is often not enough to force a cell-body transcriptomic state in this assay.
cell_types: matched Cdh2-measured neuronal groups

finding_summary: In matched thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic strata, Pten loss produced broad downstream transcriptional responses whereas engaged Cntnap2 loss produced none.
finding_consequence: This internal positive contrast argues that the Cntnap2-negative downstream result is target-specific, not simply a failure to detect responses in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut or 155 MB Glut.
literature_rationale: The references establish Cntnap2 functions and loss phenotypes, but none addresses Pten or supplies a target-specific expectation for this cross-perturbation breadth asymmetry.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Rbfox2 down-regulation is the best L5-6 IT transcriptional sentinel of Cntnap2 loss in this assay.
finding_consequence: Rbfox2 is not an obvious CASPR2-complex component, so its isolated decrease is a data-nominated marker of the limited mature deep-layer response rather than a curated pathway hit.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut

finding_summary: Abcc8 down-regulation is a weak but corrected L4-5 IT ion-channel-associated sentinel of Cntnap2 perturbation.
finding_consequence: The K-channel-related response points to an ATP-sensitive potassium-channel subunit rather than to the expected Kv1.1/Kv1.2/CNTN2 machinery, refining where any transcriptional compensation lies.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Acute Cntnap2 perturbation was almost flat transcriptomically; the only downstream FDR<0.10 genes were Rbfox2 in L5-6 IT neurons and Abcc8 in L4-5 IT CTX neurons.
finding_consequence: The dataset nominates a sparse postnatal cortical IT response rather than a broad replay of germline Cntnap2 neurodevelopmental phenotypes.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: The canonical CNTNAP2/CNTN2/Kv1 and neurexin-family synaptic programs were transcriptionally uncoupled from acute Cntnap2 loss.
finding_consequence: A structural adhesion/channel-localization pathway can fail to produce mRNA changes even when perturbed; Cntnap1, Cntn1, Kcna1, Kcna2, Kcnab1, and Kcnab2 also failed to phenocopy the Cntnap2 cortical IT signature.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Cntnap2 differed sharply from transcriptional and mTOR ASD-risk regulators that responded broadly in the same postnatal screen.
finding_consequence: Mef2c, Chd8, Tsc1, Tsc2, Pten, and Rbfox1 generated multi-cell-type transcriptional responses, so the weak Cntnap2 surface is a gene-specific mismatch rather than a universal inability to detect ASD-gene biology at P16-P44.

finding_summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Eif4e perturbation generated a broad RNA response whereas Eif4a2 and Eif4g1 were nearly self-only, showing strong response-breadth asymmetry within the eIF4F-associated machinery.
finding_consequence: Functional partners in cap-dependent initiation were not interchangeable in this neuronal transcriptome, so the Eif4a2 phenotype cannot be inferred from generic eIF4F disruption.
literature_rationale: The dossier provides target-specific EIF4A2 mechanisms and evidence that translation-initiation components can have distinct biological outputs, but it does not decisively predict the observed matched-cell breadth asymmetry.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Eif4a2 loss produced only two robust downstream mRNA changes in the screen: Cadm4 down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Dbn1 down in 191 MB P MY GABA.
finding_consequence: The real Eif4a2 response is cell-type-restricted and singleton-like rather than a broad neuronal translation-stress program; these two genes should be treated as isolated markers, not as a recovered pathway.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The unbiased signature-neighbor search did not find a high-cosine Eif4a2 module.
finding_consequence: The top nonself positive cosine was only 0.0327 and the top negative was -0.0172; Ufc1 recurred with Cadm4 down and was the only robust top-positive responder, whereas Sacs and Alkbh8 were transcriptionally flat. Eif4a2 therefore sits at the edge of detectable screen structure, not in a strong recurrent perturbation class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The eIF4F cap-binding node Eif4e responded far more strongly than Eif4a2, while Eif4h and Eif4g1 did not phenocopy Eif4a2.
finding_consequence: Same-complex comparisons show that a postmitotic neuronal mRNA response is not a generic property of perturbing any eIF4F-linked target: Eif4e drove 234 FDR<0.10 genes in the same 151 group and shared Cadm4 down-regulation, Eif4h produced only two singletons across the screen, and Eif4g1 was flat.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 155 MB Glut; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: The sparse postnatal Eif4a2 loss-of-function surface does not resemble a cell-autonomous neurodevelopmental mRNA-collapse phenotype.
finding_consequence: Human EIF4A2 disease is global, developmental, and variant-dependent; the P16 mosaic loss-of-function experiment shows that knocking out Eif4a2 after neuronal specification is largely buffered at the nuclear RNA level, so this assay should not be used as a negative genetic model of the embryonic human syndrome.

finding_summary: Two translation-linked measurable neighbors, Ddx3x and Mtor, failed to recover the Eif4a2 singleton genes despite modest responses of their own.
finding_consequence: The Cadm4/Dbn1 surface is not a linear consequence of perturbing any translation-initiation-associated regulator: Ddx3x and Mtor responses were concentrated in 151/155 and missed both Eif4a2 FDR genes in the matched groups.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: In responding 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, Glmn loss failed to induce the expected GLMN–SCF/FBXW7–MYC/Cyclin E transcriptional program or an Fbxw7-like response.
finding_consequence: GLMN is a protein-level inhibitor of RBX1-containing cullin-RING ligases; the screen did not show induction of the Fbxw7/Myc/Ccne1 axis or a strong Fbxw7 perturbation phenocopy at mRNA level.
literature_rationale: The target-specific GLMN–RBX1–FBXW7 mechanism is direct and directional, but its documented readout is post-translational. The absent RNA program therefore cannot be called disagreement without a protein-to-transcriptome link.

finding_summary: Among Arid1b comparators, 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c neurons contained a recurrent BAF response with Ptpn3, Reep2, Begain, Prkcd and Lrrc7 down-regulation after Smarcb1, Smarcc2 and Smarce1 perturbation, but that module was not recruited by Arid1b.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: In Pvalb neurons, Atp6v1a perturbation was largely self-only whereas Atp6v0c, and more modestly Atp6v1b2, produced substantially stronger V-ATPase-associated transcriptional responses.
finding_consequence: Complex membership is not equivalent to equal Perturb-seq phenotypic strength: the V0 c-ring subunit drove a broad synaptic and stress program, the V1 B2 subunit drove a smaller module, and Atp6v1a was mostly self-only.
literature_rationale: Sector-specific biology provides a concrete basis for possible non-equivalence, but the required directional bridge to a stronger Atp6v0c-associated transcriptional program is not documented.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: Atp6v1a perturbation induced the canonical stress transcript Ddit3 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
finding_consequence: Ddit3 shows that a V-ATPase perturbation can cross into the integrated-stress axis in this assay, but that crossing was anatomically narrow rather than a pan-neuronal consequence of Atp6v1a targeting.
literature_rationale: The positive Ddit3 readout survives removal of the unsupported anatomical-restriction claim. Confidence is moderated by marginal FDR, 33 perturbed cells, and the source's amyloid-treated human-neuron context rather than a direct ATP6V1A-to-DDIT3 demonstration.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: The other Atp6v1a hits were isolated, non-canonical up-regulations of Golga4 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Lta4h in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, and Chd2 in 191 MB P MY GABA.
finding_consequence: These single-gene hits keep the measured cell-type specificity visible without inflating them into Golgi, eicosanoid, or chromatin programs that the FDR surface does not support.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Across the full screen, the closest Atp6v1a neighbors were proteasome and proteostasis perturbations, especially Psmb4, Psmc5, and Psmc1, with weaker convergence to Cltc, Pomp, Vps37a, Atp6v0c, Atp2a2, Gfpt1, and Hspa9.
finding_consequence: The data nominated a stress-control module rather than simply grouping Atp6v1a with every V-ATPase subunit; Ddit3 in 066 was shared by Atp6v1a, Cltc, Gfpt1, Psmb4, and Psmc1.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: The V-ATPase complex was not transcriptionally interchangeable: Atp6v0c was much broader than Atp6v1a, Atp6v1e1 and Atp6v1b2 were weak, and Atp6v0a1 was flat across matched groups.
finding_consequence: Same-complex annotations alone would have predicted closer phenocopy. The measured split says that subunit position, isoform stoichiometry, or editing tolerance dominates the acute transcriptional outcome.

finding_summary: The screen did not phenocopy dominant ATP6V1A encephalopathy or recessive cutis laxa programs; it instead reports the acute postmitotic LoF response of surviving mouse neurons.
finding_consequence: Human ATP6V1A disease is driven largely by missense developmental alleles or systemic recessive loss, so a flat P16 neuronal LoF signature should not be read as absence of ATP6V1A disease biology.

finding_summary: Acute Brd1 loss decreased Gabbr2 and Rgs11 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, narrowing the measured neurotransmission phenotype to a small thalamic GABA-B/GPCR-signaling module.
finding_consequence: Prior Brd1+/- mouse work implicated neurotransmission and cortical excitation-inhibition balance; this dataset narrows the reproducible single-cell signal to a small thalamic GABA-B/GPCR module and does not reproduce broad Pvalb/Sst involvement at FDR thresholds.
literature_rationale: Prior Brd1-deficiency studies specifically connect the target to neurotransmission and GPCR-associated programs, making the bridge biologically relevant. However, the supplied descriptions do not provide the direction needed to classify the observed Gabbr2/Rgs11 decrease as agreement or disagreement.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c response was dominated by signal-transduction genes: Brd1 perturbation decreased Gabbr2, Rgs11 and Ptpn3 and increased Wdr26.
finding_consequence: The strongest Brd1 responder carried a GABA_B/RGS/tyrosine-phosphatase signaling signature rather than the broad calcium, cAMP or glutamate program expected from germline forebrain Brd1 studies.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Ndufa13 was a significant Brd1-down gene in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: This supplies a single mitochondrial complex-I and cell-death-associated marker within the thalamic response and connects weakly to prior Brd1+/- proteomic evidence for mitochondrial perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: In 308 CB GABA, Brd1 loss induced a single robust gene, the Hsp40 co-chaperone Dnajb2.
finding_consequence: The cerebellar GABA response points to a sharply delimited proteostasis marker rather than a broad neuronal remodeling program.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Esrra perturbation was the top significant-overlap negative neighbor and up-regulated Ptpn3 and Rgs11 where Brd1 down-regulated them in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The opposing data-driven comparator makes the Ptpn3/Rgs11 part of the thalamic signature bidirectional across the screen.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Acute Brd1 loss produced a very narrow neuronal transcriptional response: only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 308 CB GABA had any downstream genes at FDR<0.10, with five and one genes respectively.
finding_consequence: This converts a mostly flat surface into a biological statement: after P16, Brd1 is not a pan-neuronal transcriptional dependency, even though its transcript was tested in 22 neuronal groups.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: The best same-direction data-driven Brd1 neighbors were proteasome perturbations: Psmc5 shared four of the six Brd1 FDR gene-by-cell features and Psmb4 shared three, all in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The overlap argues that the thalamic Brd1 genes are a stress-sensitive downstream module also engaged by proteasome loss, not necessarily direct BRD1 chromatin targets.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The two measurable MOZ/MORF acetyltransferase relatives, Kat6a and Kat6b, did not phenocopy Brd1: both were flat in every matched cell group and flat on the Brd1 response genes in 151 and 308.
finding_consequence: Canonical H3 acetyltransferase-complex membership did not predict acute postmitotic transcriptomic convergence; any active Brd1 biology in this dataset is therefore Brd1- or context-specific rather than a generic Kat6a/Kat6b HAT-loss signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Acute Brd1 loss did not recover the broad schizophrenia- and affective-disorder transcriptional programs described in chronic Brd1+/- brains.
finding_consequence: The result warns against reading the P16 sparse CRISPR signature as a germline Brd1 haploinsufficiency model: sentinel calcium, dopaminergic, glutamatergic and Tcf4 genes were absent, and only six downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 across the whole measured surface.
cell_types: all measured Brd1 groups

finding_summary: The measured thrombospondin/integrin-side relatives Cd36, Itgb1, and Itgb2 were also downstream-null, while the most direct CD47 receptor and thrombospondin ligands, Sirpa and Thbs1-4, were not perturbation targets.
finding_consequence: The absence of a Cd47 phenotype was not hiding in an obvious same-axis phenocopy among measured CD47-adjacent receptors; the library mostly missed the transcellular SIRPα/thrombospondin ligands that would be needed to make a receptor-ligand epistasis claim.

finding_summary: Unbiased screenwide matching placed Cd47 in a no-signature neighborhood: the strongest standardized cosine similarities were only +0.034 and -0.033, with top positive neighbors that were completely FDR-flat.
finding_consequence: A hidden recurrent Cd47 module should have produced non-trivial convergence with another perturbation. Instead, the data-driven neighbors look safe-target-like or weak, reinforcing that the Cd47 profile is dominated by residual noise rather than a coherent biological state.

finding_summary: Cisd2 loss induced Mcfd2 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, consistent with a stress-responsive ER-to-Golgi cargo-receptor readout.
finding_consequence: The only positive signal points to a narrow ER/ERGIC cargo-receptor compensation rather than to global mitochondrial or autophagy collapse.
literature_rationale: The evidence supports Mcfd2 induction as a narrow ER/ERGIC-associated readout, but not a compensatory program, successful cargo-traffic adaptation, exclusion of mitochondrial or autophagic defects, or proven cell-type selectivity.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Cisd2 did not activate the amino-acid, one-carbon, UPR, or mitochondrial integrated-stress genes that Opa1 and Hspa9 activated in the same screen.
finding_consequence: This gates the null interpretation: a severe ER/mitochondrial secondary stress response was detectable by snRNA-seq here, but Cisd2 did not induce it.
literature_rationale: Cisd2 was engaged and the Opa1 and Hspa9 surfaces demonstrate local detectability of the tested stress programs. Target-specific Cisd2 loss directly activated UPR/ER stress in prior work, opposite to the informative acute neuronal absence.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Nominal data-driven signature neighbors of Cisd2 were exploratory and failed the 066 Mcfd2 replication test.
finding_consequence: The top score-vector neighbors came from a weak nominal surface and should not be over-interpreted as pathway convergence.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: The WFS2/Cisd2 loss phenotype is not reproduced as an immediate autonomous neuronal ISR after sparse P16 CRISPR loss.
finding_consequence: The screen refines CISD2 disease expectations toward chronic, high-penetrance organelle failure, stress exposure, or unsampled tissues rather than an acute transcriptomic program in most juvenile neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Becn1, Atg5, and Atg16l1 did not phenocopy Cisd2, despite the known NAF-1/BCL-2/Beclin-1 autophagy relationship.
finding_consequence: A same-pathway prior was directly testable in the parquet and was rejected: the small Becn1/Atg5 midbrain signature was absent after Cisd2 perturbation, and none produced the 066 Mcfd2 response.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Whole-screen signature neighbors of Cntnap1 were essentially residual noise, with absolute signed-score Pearson correlations no larger than 0.0365 and safe-target controls interleaving among the top anti-neighbors.
finding_consequence: The data-driven analysis did not nominate a hidden Cntnap1-like transcriptional module; this supports treating the target as flat in this modality rather than pursuing nominal genes as a pathway.

finding_summary: Cyfip2 depletion did not transcriptionally engage the nominated WRC/Arp2/3, FMR1–Rac1, SHANK3/TMEM108, or BDNF–NTRK2 neighborhood in six target-engaged neuronal groups.
finding_consequence: Canonical CYFIP2 biology centers on protein complexes and actin/endocytic signaling; this result prevents over-reading the Perturb-seq data as a transcriptional activation or repression of the WRC pathway.
literature_rationale: The references specifically nominate the tested biological neighborhood, but do not predict transcriptional feedback among its components; the observed RNA-level absence is therefore a refinement rather than agreement or disagreement.

finding_summary: Partial postnatal Cyfip2 loss produced a sparse RNA phenotype that should not be treated as equivalent to recurrent WRC-disrupting CYFIP2 Arg87 missense disease alleles.
finding_consequence: The sparse knockdown transcriptome is a poor standalone reversal signature for DEE65 programs driven by mutant CYFIP2 protein.
literature_rationale: The references directly document an allele-specific mutant-protein mechanism, supporting the distinction between Arg87 disease variants and the experiment's partial loss-of-expression perturbation.

finding_summary: A direct Eif4e perturbation was strongly transcriptional in thalamic/midbrain groups while Cyfip2 was flat, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut where Cyfip2 self logFC was -0.489 with FDR 4.39e-11 but Eif4e had 234 downstream genes.
finding_consequence: The assay could detect a transcriptional consequence of perturbing a translation-initiation node in a matched cell group; upstream Cyfip2 loss therefore does not simply collapse onto eIF4E loss in juvenile neurons.
literature_rationale: Cyfip2 provides a target-engaged tested absence while Eif4e supplies an active matched response surface. Their opposite roles within an eIF4E-restraining complex predict coarse divergence rather than phenocopy.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The measurable WAVE/FMRP/Rac neighborhood did not reconstitute a shared Cyfip2-like transcriptome: Cyfip1 had no downstream hits, and Fmr1, Fxr1, Rac1, Pak1, and Pak2 had zero or one hit each across their measured groups.
finding_consequence: A member of the same paralog family and nearby Rac/FMRP pathway nodes were directly tested and rejected as phenocopies, so the Cyfip2 flatness is pathway-local rather than an isolated target anomaly.

finding_summary: Data-driven score-surface neighbors exposed no robust positive or negative Dgke module; the five best positive and five best negative non-control neighbors all had |r|≤0.026.
finding_consequence: This prevents over-annotation of Dgke by weak nearest neighbors: the apparent neighbors are numerical extrema around zero rather than biologically convergent perturbations.

finding_summary: Measured lipid-signaling relatives did not converge with Dgke: Dgkd, Plcb1, Prkca, Pik3ca, Pik3cb, Pik3r1, Pik3r2, and Inpp5k were flat, Prkcg had only three singleton responses, while Pten and Pitpna generated restricted signatures that were near-orthogonal to Dgke.
finding_consequence: The contrast shows that the screen could detect transcriptomic consequences at some phosphoinositide nodes, so Dgke's silence is specific to the DGKE/DAG-to-PA branch rather than a universal blindness to lipid signaling perturbations.

finding_summary: The canonical DGKE renal/thrombotic and challenge-induced programs were absent from the neuronal Dgke surface: Ptgs2, Th, Trp53, Cdkn1a, Gk, and Pecam1 each had FDR=1.0 in every measured group.
finding_consequence: The negative result localizes the disease-relevant DGKE biology away from basal postmitotic neuronal transcription and toward unsampled podocyte, endothelial, platelet, fibroblast, renal-stress, or epileptogenic challenge contexts.
