finding_summary: Epha4 loss produced a one-gene Sst GABA response: Tmsb10 was up-regulated, nominating an actin-monomer cytoskeletal marker rather than a broad collapse of Sst identity.
finding_consequence: EPHA4 is a contact-dependent receptor that signals through cytoskeletal GTPase pathways, so the only FDR-supported downstream RNA change landing on an actin-sequestering protein is biologically coherent but still a restricted biomarker hypothesis.

finding_summary: The unbiased full-screen nearest neighbors of Epha4 were not robust biological mimics: Sh3kbp1 and Musk were the top positive neighbors only at cosines 0.036 and 0.032, while Chrna6 and Cux1 were the strongest negatives at about -0.019.
finding_consequence: Epha4 sits close to the origin of the perturbation-signature space; its top empirical neighbors are too weak to support a convergent module.

finding_summary: Other EphA/EphB receptor perturbations did not phenocopy Epha4: their score-vector cosines to Epha4 were all near zero and none reproduced the Sst Tmsb10 hit.
finding_consequence: The result argues against a shared juvenile brain nuclear-RNA signature for the Eph receptor family and makes the weak Sst actin marker Epha4-specific within the receptors actually tested.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba

finding_summary: Measured EPHA4 cytoskeletal-pathway neighbors, including Fyn, Chn1, Trio, Rac1, and Pak1/2/3, failed to converge on the Epha4 Sst signature.
finding_consequence: The absence of convergence separates receptor loss from knockdown of downstream Rac/PAK machinery in this fixed-dose, postmitotic screen: where Trio or Rac1 had hits, they were different genes and cell groups.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba

finding_summary: Frrs1l produced a real but extremely small adjusted response only in 308 CB GABA: Med20 was up-regulated and no other downstream gene in any measured group reached FDR<0.10.
finding_consequence: The only nuclear echo of acute Frrs1l loss falls in a cerebellar GABA class, the broad anatomical domain emphasized by motor and Purkinje-cell studies, but the one-gene signature is too small to read as an AMPAR or cerebellar disease program.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Whole-screen score-vector neighbors of Frrs1l were numerically Wdr26 and Fbxo11, not AMPAR genes, and the absolute correlations were tiny with no FDR-level Med20 overlap.
finding_consequence: This rejects the apparent global ranked-signature neighbors as mechanistic convergence and keeps the Frrs1l interpretation anchored to its single adjusted cerebellar hit plus the explicitly measured AMPAR-complex contrasts.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: The literature-obvious AMPAR biogenesis and auxiliary-subunit comparators did not phenocopy Frrs1l: Cpt1c had only two isolated downstream hits, Gria1-3 had one each, Gria4 had none, and Cacng2/Cacng3/Cacng8 were completely downstream-null.
finding_consequence: FRRS1L, CPT1C, GluA pore-forming subunits and TARPs are physically and functionally linked at the AMPAR assembly/trafficking level, yet acute postnatal CRISPR of these same targets does not create a shared snRNA-seq program; same-complex membership therefore does not predict transcriptomic convergence in this assay.

finding_summary: Thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c neurons were capable of an activity/immediate-early-like GABA-receptor response, because Gabrb2 knockdown robustly induced Nr4a1, Vgf, Fos, Npas4 and Homer2, whereas matched Gabbr1 cells did not.
finding_consequence: This contrast argues that the absent Fos/Npas4/Nr4a1 response after Gabbr1 is biologically specific to metabotropic GABA-B loss rather than a blanket inability of this cell group or the Wilcoxon readout to detect activity-coupled transcription.
literature_rationale: Gabrb2 supplies an active, coherent immediate-early response on the same well-engaged cell-group surface, making the matched Gabbr1 absence informative. The supplied source establishes a target-specific Gabrb2 phenotype but does not predict this precise transcriptional divergence.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Gabbr1 produced only a single accepted downstream change: Eif4e was up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the same group with the strongest thalamic on-target Gabbr1 mRNA decrease.
finding_consequence: The result localizes the whole positive Gabbr1 transcriptomic surface to one thalamic singleton rather than a broad GABA-B, stress, proteostasis, or synaptic-depression program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Gabbr1 had no strong whole-screen signature neighbor: after Gabbr1 itself, the best non-control positive cosine was Fbxo11 at 0.0688 and the most negative biological cosine was Wdr26 at -0.0244.
finding_consequence: The data-driven comparison rejects a hidden robust program shared with an unrelated perturbation and shows that apparent neighbors are weak restricted-signature correlations, not stable FDR-level phenocopies.

finding_summary: The same-complex and proximal GABA-B pathway perturbations were also nearly silent: Gabbr2, Kctd8, Kctd16, Kcnj6, Gnao1, Gnb1/Gnb5 and Adcy1/3/5 produced zero to two isolated downstream hits and did not reproduce the Gabbr1 thalamic Eif4e signal.
finding_consequence: The flat Gabbr1 profile is not an orphan anomaly; it is the screen-level behavior of a metabotropic receptor module whose primary outputs are G-protein, GIRK, voltage-gated Ca2+ channel and adenylyl-cyclase physiology rather than basal mRNA abundance.

finding_summary: Postmitotic partial Gnb1 transcript loss produced a muted RNA response and therefore does not model the altered effector coupling of all GNB1 encephalopathy missense alleles.
finding_consequence: The muted mRNA response after Gnb1 depletion cautions that direct suppression of GNB1 or pan-Gβγ signaling would be a blunt strategy, while GIRK-channel findings from K78R models are mechanistically informative but not a universal signature of simple Gnb1 knockdown.
literature_rationale: The references independently establish GNB1 haploinsufficiency and missense-specific altered-effector mechanisms, completing the bridge from perturbation class to expected nonequivalence. The muted transcriptomic response to partial depletion is compatible with, though not a direct assay of, the missense GIRK phenotypes.

finding_summary: The only robust CNU-LGE/LSX GABAergic responder was Ola1 up-regulation after Gnb1 perturbation.
finding_consequence: Ola1 links the singleton Gnb1 response in striatal/extended-amygdala GABAergic neurons to a translation and integrated-stress-response ATPase, but the evidence is a one-gene signature rather than a full ISR module.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA

finding_summary: Gnb1 perturbation weakly but significantly increased Ankrd13d in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons.
finding_consequence: Ankrd13d nominates ubiquitin-dependent receptor trafficking as a possible local compensation in a thalamic class, rather than the expected direct cAMP, PLC, GIRK, or immediate-early GPCR program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Ankrd13d was not a generic thalamic stress marker: broad RNA-processing, export, UBA5, and lysosomal perturbations usually drove Ankrd13d down, opposite to the weak Gnb1-driven increase.
finding_consequence: Opposite sign in much stronger thalamic signatures makes the Gnb1-Ankrd13d edge more specific, but also shows that its direction is context-sensitive and not a universal injury response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Screened GPCR-pathway relatives did not phenocopy Gnb1: Gnb5, Gnas, Gnao1, Gnal, adenylyl cyclases, Plcb1, Kcnj6, and Rgs6 were all flat or one-gene responders and none reproduced the Ola1 or Ankrd13d calls in matched cell groups.
finding_consequence: The expected heterotrimeric-G-protein neighborhood converged on the same conclusion as Gnb1 itself: this acute screen is poor at converting GPCR effector biochemistry into stable nuclear DE signatures.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The screen separates human GNB1 encephalopathy biology from simple postmitotic Gnb1 loss: neither Gnb1 nor Kcnj6 loss evoked activity-regulated transcripts, and Gnb1 did not resemble GPCR effectors transcriptionally.
finding_consequence: GNB1 disease alleles can alter GIRK regulation, including gain-of-function behavior in K78R models, so a flat LoF snRNA-seq surface should not be read as evidence that disease-relevant Gβ1 channel biology is absent from neurons.
cell_types: all 22 measured Gnb1 cell groups

finding_summary: Assayed malate-aspartate shuttle neighbors did not phenocopy the Got2 response.
finding_consequence: The same biochemical pathway did not collapse to one transcriptomic module: Got1 and Mdh1 had distinct TH Prkcd/Grin2c signatures, Mdh2 had a single Pvalb hit, and Slc25a12, Slc25a13, Glud1, and Mpc1 were flat.
literature_rationale: The claim is narrowed to Got1 and Mdh1, which are informative in the matched thalamic surface and show distinct active programs from Got2. Mdh2 and the flat transporter or metabolic perturbations cannot support independent non-phenocopy claims and are excluded. Literature supports MAS modular divergence but not the exact signed transcriptional relationship.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Got2 loss produced one FDR<0.10 downstream event, Snap25 up-regulation, confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The only robust Got2 transcriptional phenotype was a narrow synaptic-gene change, not a broad mitochondrial or amino-acid stress program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The empirical Got2 neighbor landscape was low-amplitude; Rrn3 was the only positive neighbor that robustly shared the 151 Snap25 increase.
finding_consequence: This preserves the pre-literature result that the nearest restricted signatures were not the textbook MAS enzymes and that most nominal neighbors failed full-surface FDR validation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Gprc5b produced a real but very small mixed-sign L4/5 intratelencephalic cortical signature and no other cell group crossed the downstream FDR threshold.

finding_summary: The whole-screen nearest neighbors of Pdha1 were statistically weak and biologically unconvincing.

finding_consequence: Because Pdhb, Dlat, Dld, Pdhx, and Mpc1 were directly searchable in the same parquet, their failure to converge turns the Pdha1 Vps4a/Slc4a3 hits into local, Pdha1-biased events rather than a shared transcriptional PDH-complex state.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Pex14 loss produces a low-amplitude, directionally coordinated SREBF2/cholesterol-homeostasis program, strongest in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with Cyp51, Dhcr24, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, Insig1, Fdft1, Nsdhl, and Dhcr7 biased upward.
finding_consequence: The ranking of Cyp51, Dhcr24, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, Insig1, Fdft1, and related genes suggests a sterol-homeostatic compensation to impaired peroxisome biogenesis rather than a generic stress response; Srebf2 knockdown drives the same panel in the opposite direction in this dataset.
literature_rationale: The references explicitly support both links: PEX14 is required for peroxisomal import and PEX14 deficiency causes a biogenesis defect, while genetic peroxisome deficiency activates SREBP2 and Pex14-deficient cerebellum shows altered cholesterol homeostasis. This complete chain predicts the upward sterol-homeostasis program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The data-driven Pex14 signature neighbors were numerical rather than biological: the largest positive cosine was 0.0352 and the strongest negative cosine was -0.0336 after target-transcript exclusion.
finding_consequence: This formally rejects a hidden whole-transcriptome module nominated by the screen itself; Pex14 sits inside the null cloud rather than with a coherent stress, synaptic, or peroxisomal cluster.

finding_summary: The Pex14 null is not a shared PEX-module signature: Pex1 and Pex13 import-complex perturbations and Abcd3, Acox1, Hsd17b4, Agps, and Far1 peroxisomal-metabolism perturbations were themselves mostly flat and did not converge with Pex14.
finding_consequence: Even the literature-obvious neighbors in peroxisomal matrix import and ether-lipid or fatty-acid metabolism failed to form a recurrent neuronal transcriptional module, arguing that the missing Pex14 response is pathway-level buffering rather than a one-gene anomaly.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 217 P MY Pineal Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Pi4ka perturbation in 217 P MY Pineal Glut produced Abca2 down-regulation with Dgkd up-regulation, forming a sparse endolysosomal lipid-transport and DAG-turnover response.
finding_consequence: The Abca2 hit connects the strongest rare-cell response to brain lipid handling, and the Dgkd signal suggests a candidate phospholipid-remodeling compensation after Pi4ka perturbation.
literature_rationale: PI4KA is directly tied to PI4P synthesis and the PI cycle, DGKD to DAG-to-phosphatidic-acid conversion, and ABCA2 to endolysosomal sterol and sphingolipid handling. This is a specific mechanistic bridge, but the observed transcriptional directions remain undocumented.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Pi4ka perturbation down-regulated Slc12a5/Kcc2 in 191 MB P MY GABA.
finding_consequence: KCC2 is the mature neuronal chloride extruder; its selective loss marks an inhibitory-neuron chloride-homeostasis or maturation defect rather than a direct readout of PI4P abundance.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The empirical Pi4ka neighbours were vesicle/lysosome-linked or unrelated state perturbations, not strong same-complex phenocopies.
finding_consequence: Atp6v0c, Pitpna, and Cltc were the top positive neighbours despite tiny cosines and no exact 3-gene FDR overlap; the strongest negative neighbours also failed to provide a mechanistic inverse, emphasizing how restricted the Pi4ka signature is.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Pi4ka loss produced only three downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 22 measured cell groups, all confined to 191 MB P MY GABA and 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
finding_consequence: A core lipid kinase did not trigger a cortex-wide or pan-neuronal nuclear program after P16 mosaic mutation; the recovered biology is a pair of small, anatomically restricted survivor-state signatures.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Pi4kb, PI3K/PTEN nodes, DAG kinases, and PI phosphatases largely failed to phenocopy Pi4ka in the matching cell groups.
finding_consequence: The expected phosphoinositide-pathway relatives were measurable and mostly rejected, arguing that the Pi4ka snRNA phenotype is not a generic PI4P or PI3K-pathway transcriptional state.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA; 217 P MY Pineal Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Core clathrin and actin perturbations produced FDR-significant signatures in matched groups, whereas Prepl did not.
finding_consequence: The lack of Prepl downstream DE is not explained by a global inability to detect vesicle or cytoskeletal injury; it suggests PREPL is buffered or peripheral to the core Cltc and Actb modules in this acute neuronal setting.
literature_rationale: Significant Prepl reduction makes its null downstream surface informative in five groups, while Cltc is an active matched comparator with a specific trafficking bridge. The Actb relationship and broader claims of pathway peripherality are not mechanistically supported and are excluded.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The screen-wide residual signature for Prepl was extremely weak and did not nominate any robust FDR-supported convergent module.
finding_consequence: This prevents overinterpretation of nominal Prepl genes: the largest absolute screen-centered correlation was only 0.124, and leading neighbors were safe-target or weak singleton signatures.

finding_summary: Neither Prepl nor direct respiratory-chain perturbations generated a broad OXPHOS or mitochondrial-stress transcriptional module in this screen.
finding_consequence: PREPL-dependent mitochondrial dysfunction is plausible biochemistry, but this assay is poorly aligned to respiratory-chain enzymatic outputs; absence of OXPHOS DE after Prepl loss is therefore not strong evidence against a mitochondrial role.

finding_summary: The postnatal neuronal null narrows PREPL disease modeling away from broad acute neuronal transcriptional toxicity and toward neonatal, endocrine, NMJ, peripheral, and biochemical axes.
finding_consequence: PREPL inhibitors or complete genetic loss should not be de-risked by this flat snRNA surface alone; the clinically dominant phenotypes live in compartments that were earlier, peripheral, secretory, or non-transcriptional relative to this assay.

finding_summary: Literature-obvious Prep and Camkmt comparators did not phenocopy Prepl, and AP-1 subunit screen targets produced only isolated singleton DEGs.
finding_consequence: PREPL should not be grouped by paralog similarity, contiguous-deletion neighborhood, or generic AP-1 membership when interpreting this neuronal Perturb-seq surface; those measurable relatives were empirically rejected as convergent comparators.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Sparse loss of wild-type Prkcg did not reproduce the broad signaling or proteostatic consequences expected from dominant pathogenic SCA14 missense alleles, so the two perturbation classes are not mechanistically interchangeable.
finding_consequence: Pathogenic PRKCG mutations can perturb autoinhibition and cerebellar phosphosignaling in ways not modeled by the weak mRNA-loss signatures here.
literature_rationale: Target-specific studies establish that prominent SCA14 mechanisms arise from altered properties of mutant PKCγ rather than simple wild-type dosage reduction. Thus, the sparse response to wild-type Prkcg loss supports the stated allele-class distinction, although the experiment did not directly test a mutant allele.

finding_summary: Unbiased all-screen neighbors of Prkcg were near-zero vectors: the top positive non-self scores were 0.023-0.029, the strongest real-gene anti-neighbors were -0.010 to -0.013, and none shared the three Prkcg FDR hits.
finding_consequence: A nearest-neighbor search across the full 2046-target surface fails to nominate a robust Prkcg module; the few ranked neighbors should be kept as rejected exploratory comparators rather than promoted to pathway biology.

finding_summary: Prkcg LoF generated an extremely sparse, cell-type-restricted transcriptomic surface: only L5-6 IT glutamatergic, CNU-HYa/HY GABAergic, and cerebellar GABAergic groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and each had exactly one.
finding_consequence: The dominant phenotype in this juvenile sparse-CRISPR screen is not a broad PKCγ transcriptional program but isolated Sestd1, Speg, and Etv5 responses that should be treated as cell-group markers rather than a multi-gene pathway module.

finding_summary: The SPG72/HSP implication of REEP2 is not recapitulated as early pan-neuronal nuclear RNA remodeling after sparse juvenile LoF.

literature_rationale: The references provide a specific REEP2 disease and membrane-mechanism bridge but do not predict the assayed early RNA response. Thus, the observed lack of downstream DEGs refines rather than directly confirms or contradicts the documented biology.

literature_rationale: The references provide a specific RETREG1-to-ER-phagy mechanism, while the experiment informatively shows no canonical UPR induction after engaged knockdown. Because the literature primarily documents ER morphology, turnover, flux, and stress susceptibility rather than a required basal transcriptional response, the null RNA result is not a directional contradiction.

finding_consequence: FAM134B loss-of-function causes hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type 2, whereas these brain neurons showed target knockdown without a broad stress transcriptome; that points to peripheral-neuron, chronic, or non-transcriptional vulnerability rather than a generic acute UPR across all neurons.
literature_rationale: The disease and ER-phagy literature is target-specific, but its documented phenotypes involve peripheral sensory neurons, chronic degeneration, ER structure, turnover, and apoptosis. Those findings do not decisively predict a broad acute CNS transcriptional response, so the milder RNA phenotype refines rather than opposes the literature.

finding_summary: In the two best-engaged glutamatergic groups, Scn2a loss did not induce an RNA-level compensatory program involving sodium-channel paralogs, AIS machinery, KCNQ channels, or nominated synaptic-disease neighbors.

finding_summary: Scn2a produced only a three-gene FDR response, all up-regulated, split between Dgkd/Slc6a8 in L4/5 IT cortex and Stn1 in MH-LH TH glutamatergic neurons.
finding_consequence: The positive surface is real but sparse: it supports a restricted lipid/creatine-buffer response in one cortical excitatory group and an isolated Stn1 response in one subcortical glutamatergic group, not a broad neuronal stress, translation, proteostasis, or synaptic-downregulation program.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut

finding_summary: The closest positive restricted-signature neighbors were not sodium-channel paralogs; Kcnb1 ranked fourth and drove a stronger L4/5 IT activity-like up-program than Scn2a.
finding_consequence: The screen can register an excitability-related state in the same cortical class: Kcnb1 loss up-regulated Bdnf, Vgf, and Nptx2 at FDR<0.10, while Scn2a had only Dgkd and Slc6a8 at FDR<0.10 and left those activity genes sub-threshold.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Ank3 and Grin2b were among the strongest negative neighbors of Scn2a in the matched responder signature even though Ank3 scaffolds sodium channels and Grin2b is a glutamatergic disease comparator.

finding_summary: Voltage-gated sodium paralogs, Scn1b, intracellular FGF channel adaptors, and KCNQ2/3 did not phenocopy Scn2a across the same screen.

finding_summary: The SCN2A LoF disease prior is not accompanied by a robust basal snRNA-seq disease program after mosaic juvenile CRISPR loss in most neuronal groups.
finding_consequence: SCN2A is strongly associated with epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders, but this LoF screen shows that the relevant phenotype in postmitotic neurons is likely electrophysiological, allele-directional, developmental, or subtype-specific unless a secondary activity program is strong enough to cross the RNA readout.

finding_summary: Selenoi loss activates a compact sterol-feedback module in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: Insig1, Msmo1 and Fdft1 are up-regulated while the target transcript itself is significantly reduced.
finding_consequence: The positive signal is not a generic stress response; it nominates ER cholesterol/sterol feedback as the detectable transcriptional compensation to an ER PE/plasmenyl-PE enzyme in this postmitotic thalamic glutamatergic context.
literature_rationale: Significant target reduction accompanies coherent induction of three sterol-feedback genes. The supplied lipid-defect-to-SQLE evidence is signed and target-relevant but does not establish the complete coordinated module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The upstream Kennedy-pathway perturbation Pcyt2 is the top positive Selenoi signature neighbor and phenocopies the 151 TH sterol response, up-regulating Insig1, Msmo1, Fdft1, Hmgcr, Hmgcs1, Sqle and Ldlr.
finding_consequence: Convergence of Pcyt2 and Selenoi shows that the sterol signature is tied to CDP-ethanolamine/PE-pathway stress rather than to an idiosyncratic Selenoi guide effect.
literature_rationale: Pcyt2 has an informative matched response and phenocopies the Selenoi sterol program. The supplied linear Kennedy-pathway chain predicts convergence without requiring exact neuronal DEG replication.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Selenoi sits opposite Srebf2 and alongside Marchf6/Chp1 in the 151 TH sterol module: Srebf2 knockdown represses Selenoi-induced sterol genes, whereas Marchf6 and the data-driven neighbor Chp1 induce a broader version of them.
finding_consequence: The inverse Srebf2 signature validates the induced genes as SREBP2-output genes, and Marchf6 convergence links the module to ER sterol enzyme turnover rather than to PE synthesis alone.
literature_rationale: Informative Srebf2 and Marchf6 perturbations provide supported opposite- and same-direction relationships to the sterol module. Chp1 is also active and concordant but lacks a target-specific literature bridge, so the combined comparator claim remains incomplete.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Nos1ap is the single robust down-regulated non-sterol transcript in the Selenoi 151 TH response and is not a shared Kennedy/SREBP comparator gene.
finding_consequence: It is a thalamic Selenoi-loss marker candidate separated from the sterol module, but by itself it is insufficient to claim a broader synaptic or nitric-oxide signaling program.

finding_consequence: ATF4 is a known output of many mammalian mitochondrial stresses; its absence here prioritizes post-transcriptional, metabolic, longer-latency, or threshold effects over an immediate neuronal ISR in this screen.
literature_rationale: The references form a target-specific chain from NDUFA10 dysfunction to Complex-I impairment and from mitochondrial stress to an ATF4-dominated response. The absent RNA program conflicts with that expectation, although stress type, response threshold, and latency limit confidence.

finding_summary: Ndufa10 perturbation produced a single CNU-MGE GABA downstream response, up-regulation of the mitochondrial translation termination factor Mtrf1l.
finding_consequence: The positive response points to mitochondrial gene-expression control rather than a broad nuclear stress response, and it is the only downstream FDR<0.10 signal in the entire Ndufa10 surface.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA

finding_summary: Data-driven restricted-signature neighbors of Ndufa10 were weak and did not produce a robust shared downstream program.
finding_consequence: This records the unbiased comparator result: the small Ndufa10 signature does not support strong convergence with Park7, Map1lc3a, Ifih1, Ndufb8, Sdha, or the other top nominal neighbors.

finding_summary: Same-Complex-I and assembly-factor perturbations almost never produced robust transcriptional signatures and did not phenocopy the Ndufa10 Mtrf1l hit.
finding_consequence: The expected physical neighbors were measured directly, so their failure to converge argues that postnatal snRNA-seq is below a shared OXPHOS stress threshold for this module, not simply that Ndufa10 guides failed.

finding_summary: Ndufs3 produced a real but minimal two-gene response restricted to 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut: Abhd14b increased and Camkv decreased at FDR 0.0964.
finding_consequence: The only corrected downstream signal is neither a global OXPHOS signature nor a pan-neuronal stress program; it localizes the acute postnatal transcriptional consequence to one hypothalamic/hypothalamic-mammillary glutamatergic class.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: Ndufs3 did not phenocopy other directly measured Complex-I subunits or assembly factors.
finding_consequence: Physical membership in Complex I was a poor predictor of the acute single-nucleus signature: the 25 other NDUF/NDUFAF targets produced only 19 total downstream gene-cell calls and no comparator shared the Abhd14b/Camkv pair in the Ndufs3 responder class.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: Expected mitochondrial ISR, UPR, glycolysis/serine, protease and autophagy-lysosome marker transcripts were absent across the measured Ndufs3 surface.
finding_consequence: The negative result is mechanistically informative: strong mitochondrial dysfunction can induce Atf3/Atf4/Atf5, Ddit3, Fgf21/Gdf15, one-carbon and protease programs, and these RNAs were measured, but none survived FDR correction in this P16 sparse Ndufs3 LoF screen.

finding_summary: The data-driven Ndufs3 signature neighbors were weak and did not reveal a robust compensatory module.
finding_consequence: The strongest positive 110-neighbor, Pou3f3, had only one unrelated FDR<0.10 gene in the matched cell group, while Mphosph9, Rlim, Atp6v0c, Crx and Ufsp2 had none there; this rejects an obvious cross-target phenocopy for the two-gene Ndufs3 signal.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: FDR-supported Nefm depletion did not induce compensatory Nefl, Nefh, or Ina transcription in engaged neuronal groups.
finding_consequence: Neurofilament subunits are interdependent at protein and filament levels, but this screen did not reveal reciprocal transcriptional buffering among the core subunit genes.
literature_rationale: The literature specifically supports the nominated subunit-compensation hypothesis but does not predict compensatory mRNA induction or unchanged transcript abundance, so the informative RNA-level absence is not a directional contradiction.

finding_summary: The textbook Nefm network did not reveal a hidden common nuclear signature: Nefl, Nefh, Kif5a, Mapt, Tubb3, and Stmn2 were all null or near-null in the same screen.
finding_consequence: This rejects the simple model that every neurofilament or axonal-transport perturbation in this dataset converges on a shared stress or cytoskeletal-replacement transcriptome.

finding_summary: Nefm depletion did not induce transcriptional replacement of other neurofilament, microtubule, or regeneration genes: Nefl, Nefh, Ina, Tubb3, Tuba1a, Mapt, Kif5a, Stmn2, and Gap43 were FDR=1.0 in all 207 tested Nefm gene-by-cell-group rows.
finding_consequence: The expected cytoskeletal adjustment after NF-M loss is therefore likely to be polymer stoichiometry, protein turnover, ultrastructure, or transport, not a straightforward soma-level mRNA swap to another axonal cytoskeleton transcript.
cell_types: all 23 measured groups

finding_summary: A phenotype-first neighbor search found no strong convergent or anti-convergent Nefm module anywhere in the screen: the best positive and negative restricted-signature cosines were only +0.129 and -0.0957.
finding_consequence: The Nefm surface behaves like a globally buffered signature rather than like a weak projection of a strong module represented elsewhere in the screen.

finding_summary: Nfic perturbation induced the BMP/TGF-β feedback regulator Bambi in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The only robust non-target transcriptome change after Nfic perturbation is a regulator of BMP/TGF-beta signaling, focusing follow-up on one thalamic excitatory class instead of a pan-neuronal Nfic program.
literature_rationale: The citations connect NFIC and BAMBI to the same signaling axis, making the bridge biologically specific, but the required perturbational and directional link to Bambi induction is absent.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Septin5 and Dbn1 nominate a small synaptic-vesicle/dendritic-actin component of the thalamic Nfic response.
finding_consequence: The marker pair gives the neuronal part of an otherwise non-neuronal NFIC literature a concrete follow-up hypothesis in Prkcd/Grin2c thalamic neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The screen-wide Nfic signature neighbors were weak and noncanonical; the top neighbor Gigyf2 had Xbp1/RNA-processing hits in 151 but no Bambi, Septin5, or Dbn1 response.
finding_consequence: This prevents the restricted Nfic signature from being assigned to the strongest global neighbor without direct matched-cell validation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Nfic has a single FDR<0.10 downstream response in the 23 measured neuronal groups: Bambi up, Septin5 up, and Dbn1 down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The phenotype is real but narrow; it should be interpreted as a thalamic three-gene response rather than a broad NFI developmental program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The Bambi induction is not a general TGF/BMP/Hedgehog/tooth-root phenocopy: 21 screened receptors, Smads, Gli/Ptch/Smo, Sox9, Runx2, and Sp7 comparators did not reproduce the Bambi-Septin5-Dbn1 triad in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

finding_summary: Nfia, Nfib, and Nfix did not phenocopy Nfic in this assay; the paralogs were flat or nearly flat and did not move the 151 triad.

finding_summary: Cross-perturbation convergence around Nfyc was limited to a Resp18/Ivd/Myh14 marker overlap with broad, unrelated perturbations rather than to an NF-Y-specific module.

finding_summary: The screen could not test NF-YA/NF-YB directly, and measured stress/proteostasis relatives did not phenocopy Nfyc.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Acute Nfyc loss produced a real but very small transcriptional response that was restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The screen does not support a pan-neuronal NFYC transcriptional requirement at P16-P37/44; its one robust effect is a four-gene down-state in a thalamic glutamatergic class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The Nfyc responder did not recover the ER-chaperone, UPR, p62/autophagy, or proteasome program expected from NF-Y stress literature.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Ogdh perturbation induced the mitochondrial peroxide-detoxifying transcript Prdx5 in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
finding_consequence: PRDX5 is a mitochondrial peroxidase and OGDHC can generate ROS, so Prdx5 is biologically plausible, but the missing Ogdh target FDR in the same cells makes off-target sampling or a rare-state effect equally plausible.
literature_rationale: The literature supplies specific OGDHC-to-ROS and PRDX5-to-peroxide-detoxification links, but the signed bridge from Ogdh loss to Prdx5 induction is missing. The single response arose on a surface without significant target depletion.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut

finding_summary: Target-engaged Ogdh perturbation did not induce the alternative E1 transcript Ogdhl.
finding_consequence: If KGDHC flux was buffered, the buffering was not visible as compensatory up-regulation of the brain E1 isoenzyme transcript, focusing follow-up on pre-existing OGDHL protein, DLST/DLD stoichiometry, substrate supply, or post-transcriptional control.
literature_rationale: The target-engaged dataset informatively excludes Ogdhl mRNA induction, but the cited biology nominates OGDHL only as a possible substitute and supplies no directional compensation expectation.

finding_summary: The screen argues that mild, postmitotic Ogdh attenuation is buffered below the level needed for a genome-wide mitochondrial stress response.
finding_consequence: Human OGDH disease demonstrates that severe biallelic impairment is pathogenic, but the P16 sparse CRISPR screen shows that an acute partial perturbation in surviving juvenile neurons is usually transcriptionally silent, refining the disease expectation by strength and timing.
literature_rationale: Strong Ogdh RNA reduction in 155 and 191 makes the absence of a detectable downstream mitochondrial-stress program informative at the assayed RNA level. Literature supports threshold-dependent consequences but does not directly predict this absence after partial postmitotic attenuation.

finding_summary: Ogdh induced a single-gene mitochondrial peroxide-buffering response, Prdx5 up-regulation, only in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
finding_consequence: Prdx5 is the only robust redox gene recovered from the expected OGDHC stress space, making the response narrow and cell-type restricted rather than a broad oxidative-stress transcriptome.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut

finding_summary: Ogdh up-regulated Borcs7 in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, nominating a BORC/lysosomal-trafficking marker in a second cell group.
finding_consequence: The hit points to organelle-positioning biology rather than canonical TCA or ISR genes and generates a testable hypothesis that partial OGDHC stress can be coupled to neuronal lysosome transport in thalamic/hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut

finding_summary: Same-complex OGDHC perturbations Dlst and Dld did not phenocopy the Ogdh signature.
finding_consequence: The result prevents over-interpreting Prdx5 or Borcs7 as a generic OGDHC-loss transcriptome; in this partial postnatal screen, E1o loss is separable from E2/E3 perturbation at the transcriptional level.

finding_summary: Plxna2 perturbation produced a single robust downstream transcript, Med15, and only in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.

finding_summary: The canonical semaphorin/plexin transcriptional neighborhood was absent from the Plxna2 loss-of-function surface.

finding_summary: Screened semaphorin/plexin relatives failed to phenocopy Plxna2 and instead generated isolated hits in different cell groups.
finding_consequence: Direct return-to-data comparison rejected a common A-class plexin transcriptomic module: Nrp1, Plxnc1, Plxnd1, and Fyn were downstream-null; Plxna1, Plxna4, Nrp2, Sema6a, and Rac1 each had only one- or two-gene responses, none in the Plxna2 responder group and none involving Med15.

finding_summary: Pnkd failed to copy the transcriptomic response of the synaptic fusion factor Stxbp1, while most other release-machinery targets were also nearly flat.
finding_consequence: The contrast localizes the Pnkd negative result: some synaptic perturbations can remodel neuronal mRNA in this assay, but RIM-adjacent release factors such as Unc13a and Cacna1a do not automatically do so without activity or a stronger secondary state.

finding_summary: The null surface specifically uncoupled Scn8a knock-out from transcriptional channel compensation: immediate-early/activity genes, other sodium-channel alpha and beta genes, Ank3/Ank2, Nfasc/Cntnap2 and intracellular Fgfs all stayed below FDR<0.10 after Scn8a perturbation.

Literature specifically links Scn8a loss to reduced firing but does not establish that the proposed transcriptional compensation is necessary or predict its direction.

finding_consequence: Scn8a and Ank3 occupy the same Nav1.6/AIS neighborhood, but the scaffold has a thalamic transcriptional consequence not phenocopied by deleting the pore-forming channel.
literature_rationale: Within the same high-power thalamic group, both targets were depleted, Ank3 generated a coherent 163-gene response, and Scn8a had no non-self program. This is an informative divergence, although the direct AIS relationship does not predict the observed transcriptomic difference.

finding_summary: Textbook sodium-channel comparators also failed to phenocopy a broad transcriptomic module: Scn1a, Scn2a, Scn3a, Scn9a, Scn1b, Fgf12, Fgf13, Fgf14 and Ank2 produced at most a handful of isolated downstream genes across the screen.
finding_consequence: The Scn8a null is not an idiosyncratic failed channel perturbation; a substantial measured subset of the Nav alpha/beta/FGF neighborhood is largely buffered on the snRNA-seq axis.

finding_summary: The expected mitochondrial dynamics, cristae/OXPHOS, ISR/UPRmt and mitophagy marker programs were absent after Slc25a46 perturbation.
finding_consequence: SLC25A46 biology predicts mitochondrial hyperfusion, cristae and respiration defects, and autophagy accumulation; their canonical nuclear stress sentinels did not activate, so the major phenotype in this P16 mosaic assay is not a broad mitochondrial-stress transcriptome.
literature_rationale: This is a powered tested-absence claim in the three groups with significant target depletion, adequate cells, favorable recovery baselines, and matched assay capability. Sources establish mitochondrial structural and respiratory defects but do not require the specified nuclear ISR, UPRmt, mitophagy, or dynamics-marker program.

finding_summary: A core V-ATPase perturbation, Atp6v0c, generated 1086 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in the same screen, whereas Clcn4 generated none.
finding_consequence: The Clcn4 null is not explained by a universal inability of snRNA-seq to see endolysosomal-acidification stress; stronger disruption of vesicle acidification is transcriptionally visible in overlapping postmitotic neurons.
literature_rationale: Atp6v0c is strongly active where Clcn4 is engaged yet downstream-null, making the measured non-phenocopy informative; the source does not predict their differential transcriptomic breadth.

finding_summary: The human CLCN4 disease prior does not translate into a broad acute mouse-neuron LoF transcriptome.
finding_consequence: CLCN4 pathogenic variants can alter ion transport, trafficking, or ClC-3 association in allele-specific ways; the flat CRISPR LoF result warns against treating Raynaud-Claes biology as a generic, cell-autonomous postmitotic transcriptional stress program.
literature_rationale: The absence of a broad acute RNA program is informative in the three engaged, adequately powered groups, but heterogeneous disease mechanisms do not specifically predict that tested absence.

finding_summary: The obvious ClC relatives did not converge on a hidden Clcn4-like transcriptome: single Clcn3 and Clcn5 perturbations were also downstream-null wherever they were recovered.

finding_summary: In Cox4i1-depleted midbrain and hindbrain neuronal profiles, the expected COX4I2/HIF1/LONP1-glycolytic compensation program was not induced.

literature_rationale: COX4I1-deficient and knockdown fibroblast models directly support the nominated compensatory direction. Its absence in responsive neuronal surfaces is therefore opposite to the documented expectation, with moderate confidence because transportability and low neuronal Cox4i2 expression may limit the response.

finding_summary: In MB Glut neurons, Ctnnbl1 perturbation coupled Unc13a up-regulation with nominal Snap25 down-regulation, nominating a narrow presynaptic-vesicle remodeling response.

finding_summary: Ctnnbl1 perturbation recurrently increased Arhgef1 across analyzed subcortical contexts, with FDR support in TH Prkcd/Grin2c neurons.

literature_rationale: The supplied sources describe the two proteins independently. General splicing biology and ARHGEF1's RhoA function do not support the observed recurrent signed edge.

finding_summary: Paxbp1 up-regulation is a selective 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA marker of the Ctnnbl1 perturbation.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Ctnnbl1 up-regulated the presynaptic vesicle-priming gene Unc13a in 155 MB Glut.
finding_consequence: The hit links the sparse Ctnnbl1 response to a synaptic effector with neuronal function, but cross-perturbation recurrence is mixed and therefore hypothesis-generating.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Ctnnbl1 produced only three corrected downstream genes across 22 recovered neuronal groups, each in a different subcortical group.
finding_consequence: The target is measurable but the biology is not a broad neuronal PRP19/splicing transcriptional collapse; the response is sparse and cell-class restricted.

finding_summary: Ctnnbl1 showed no beta-catenin or alpha-catenin phenocopy in the matched neuronal screen.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The ASD/ID relevance of CTNND2 is not mirrored by a broad acute P16-P44 basal neuronal transcriptome.
finding_consequence: Human loss-of-function disease links and germline mouse synaptic phenotypes can be real while still being displaced to dendritic architecture, receptor localization, physiology, or earlier developmental windows that this sparse postmitotic nuclei assay does not directly score.
literature_rationale: The two engaged, highly responsive groups support the narrow tested absence of a broad acute basal RNA program. The further claim that disease biology is displaced specifically to architecture, physiology, or development is not established and should be excluded.

finding_summary: Ctnnd2 produced a one-gene downstream response, Elfn2 up-regulation, only in 155 MB Glut.
finding_consequence: The only FDR<0.10 downstream change points to a narrow postsynaptic-adhesion compensation rather than the broad cadherin, Rho, Wnt, stress, or translation programs that would have created a multi-gene signature.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The canonical cadherin/catenin, Rho-family, beta-catenin/Wnt, and postsynaptic scaffold genes expected from CTNND2 biology were absent from the Ctnnd2 DE surface.

finding_summary: Acute postnatal Dlg4 depletion caused target loss without a broad nuclear RNA-state collapse, distinguishing this perturbation from the developmental mechanisms of human DLG4 synaptopathy.
finding_consequence: Human DLG4 loss-of-function variants are neurodevelopmental, but the mouse single-cell data suggest downstream biomarkers may be electrophysiologic, proteomic or structural instead of robust nuclear mRNA markers.
literature_rationale: The literature directly places the principal consequences of Dlg4 disruption at postsynaptic function and stabilization; mutant mice also showed severe functional phenotypes without changes in several measured receptor-expression or structural features. This aligns with on-target Dlg4 repression accompanied by little broad nuclear RNA-state change, although the cited studies did not perform an equivalent transcriptome-wide assay.

In this assay, receptor loss can cross the nuclear threshold, whereas PSD-95 perturbation remains buffered or physiological.

literature_rationale: The literature directly distinguishes dominant aggregating disease alleles from simple wild-type transcript depletion, supporting the conclusion that the sparse acute knockdown signature should not be treated as a CLN4 phenocopy or inhibition-safety result.

The other listed receptor-subunit comparators are excluded because the supplied evidence does not establish their relevant active surfaces.

finding_summary: Gigyf2, the 4EHP-binding paralog, did not phenocopy Gigyf1: its global score-vector correlation with Gigyf1 was 0.0078, it had no FDR<0.10 hits in the two Gigyf1 responder groups, and its own 42-gene response was shifted to Pvalb, hypothalamic, thalamic, and midbrain glutamatergic neurons.

The screen instead saw zero FDR-significant sterol/SREBF2 target genes under Hmgcr perturbation, while Srebf2 perturbation itself repressed sterol genes in the same assay.

Exact informative cell-group identities are not enumerated in the supplied finding, so no cell-resolved placement is assigned.

finding_summary: The measured JIP1-JNK pathway relatives also failed to induce downstream expression programs: Mapk8, Mapk9, and Map3k7 each had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in their recovered groups.

finding_consequence: This separates JIP1 cargo-adaptor biology from detectable steady-state transcription: the assay was a poor match for local APP/JIP1 vesicle transport even when a transport cargo such as App was strongly depleted.

finding_summary: Mapk8ip1 had no strong data-driven signature neighborhood; the largest positive Wilcoxon-score correlation across the screen was only 0.032 and the most negative was -0.014.

finding_summary: Most screened synaptic-vesicle and SNARE relatives were also transcriptomically flat or singleton-scale, rather than converging with Stx1b or with the stronger Stxbp1 response.
finding_consequence: The broad lack of RNA responses among Snap25, Vamp1, Cplx, Unc13, Syn, Syt2, and Syp perturbations supports the interpretation that acute presynaptic vesicle-fusion defects mainly displace off the nuclear-transcriptomic axis in this juvenile screen.

finding_summary: STX1B fever-epilepsy genetics did not translate into a shared postnatal RNA signature with ion-channel and GABAergic epilepsy comparators.
finding_consequence: The lack of convergence with Scn1a, Scn1b, Kcnq2, Gabrg2, Gabrb3, or Slc6a1 perturbations argues that their clinical convergence is network excitability rather than a common tonic cell-autonomous transcriptional state at P37-44.

finding_summary: Tm2d1 loss induced the neuronal surface-recognition genes Epha10 and Pcdhb21 in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
finding_consequence: The phenotype is not a broad pan-neuronal stress or amyloid-like program; downstream interpretation should be anchored to sparse cell-type-restricted hits.
literature_rationale: The cited amyloid, APP, G-protein, and family-level Notch findings establish general TM2D1 biology but provide no target-specific bridge to the observed RNA program.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut

finding_summary: Thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons showed a one-gene Tm2d1 response, R3hdm2 up-regulation.
finding_consequence: The TH signal is real by FDR but not a pathway-scale program; preserving it as a single-gene response prevents over-interpreting it as a generic stress or synaptic module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The strongest negative data-driven neighbor, Ap2s1, robustly drove R3hdm2 in the opposite direction in the exact thalamic population where Tm2d1 induced it.
finding_consequence: This converts the weak global anticorrelation into a measured biological contrast: loss of an AP-2 endocytic subunit produces a broad 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c program and represses R3hdm2, whereas Tm2d1 gives an isolated R3hdm2 increase.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The only multi-gene Tm2d1 response was induction of Epha10 and Pcdhb21 in L5 extratelencephalic cortical glutamatergic neurons.
finding_consequence: The two significant genes encode neuronal surface-recognition molecules, suggesting a tiny L5 ET-restricted membrane identity or wiring adjustment rather than a broad stress or amyloid-response cascade.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut

finding_summary: Amyloid/Presenilin/Notch comparators in the screen did not phenocopy Tm2d1.
finding_consequence: APP, Psen1, Adam10, Notch2, and Trem2 were flat in their measured neuronal groups, and the few Notch1/3/4/Lrp1 hits did not include Epha10, Pcdhb21, or R3hdm2; thus the sparse Tm2d1 signature is not a disguised gamma-secretase, APP, or Notch signature in this P16 loss-of-function assay.

finding_summary: The L4-5 intratelencephalic cortical group that was weak for Tm2d1 was capable of resolving an excitability-like Bdnf/Vgf/Scg2 program after Kcnb1 perturbation.
finding_consequence: A potassium-channel perturbation and Kcnq2 self-knockdown produced FDR-level or near-FDR Bdnf induction in the same cell class where Tm2d1 had no FDR genes, arguing that Tm2d1 does not simply trigger the activity-response program detected for ion-channel targets.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Trmt1 loss failed to induce the Asns/Atf4/amino-acid-stress program that Elp1 and Elp2 perturbations robustly induced in the same TH Prkcd/Grin2c neuronal group.
finding_consequence: The cell type is capable of mounting a tRNA-perturbation-associated ISR-like mRNA program, but the response is coupled to Elongator loss rather than to Trmt1 loss.
literature_rationale: TRMT1-dependent tRNA modification, redox phenotypes, and shared broad involvement in tRNA biology do not alone bridge the target to the focal absence of the Elongator-associated stress program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The only L4-5 IT cortical response was Coq2 up-regulation, a mitochondrial ubiquinone-biosynthetic gene, at a permissive FDR threshold.
finding_consequence: A CoQ/redox-associated hit is directionally compatible with prior TRMT1 redox biology but shows that any mitochondrial compensation in this assay is narrow rather than a broad oxidative-stress state.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: The only pontine/medullary/pineal glutamatergic response was up-regulation of Prkcsh, the ER glucosidase-II beta subunit used in N-glycan processing.
finding_consequence: This nominates a small ER glycoprotein-quality-control compensation rather than the Ddit3/Herpud1/Slc7a1 stress module seen after the rank-4 data-driven comparator Lonp1 in the same group.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Genome-wide signature neighbors of Trmt1 were essentially flat: the best non-self full-score cosine was only 0.043, the most negative cosine was -0.016, and the top neighbors did not reproduce Coq2, Slc9a8, or Prkcsh at FDR<0.10.
finding_consequence: The screen provides no evidence that Trmt1 sits in a reusable perturbation module in juvenile neurons; the isolated hits should not be over-interpreted as a broad shared state.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 022 L5 ET CTX Glut; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Layer-5 extratelencephalic neurons showed the only negative Trmt1-regulated hit, a selective decrease of the Golgi/TGN ion exchanger Slc9a8.
finding_consequence: The strongest absolute logFC in the Trmt1 surface was confined to one projection-neuron class and points to trafficking or pH-control biology rather than tRNA-modification targets directly.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut

finding_summary: Other screened tRNA-modification enzymes did not phenocopy Trmt1: Nsun2 and Alkbh8 were fully flat in matched groups, and the closest known vertebrate paralog Trmt1l was not a perturbation target.
finding_consequence: The absence of family convergence argues against a generic tRNA-modifier stress state in this P16 neuronal assay and qualifies any attempt to generalize from one RNA-modification enzyme to another.
cell_types: all 22 Trmt1-measured neuronal groups

finding_summary: Trps1 produced a real but extremely focal response: only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had any downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and the recovered signature was Tnc up, Atp6ap2 up, and Pid1 down.
finding_consequence: The target is not globally inert, but the post-P16 neuronal consequence is confined to a three-gene thalamic sentinel rather than a broad pan-neuronal transcriptional-regulator phenotype.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The thalamic genes recovered after Trps1 loss mark extracellular-matrix and endolysosomal/V-ATPase biology, whereas the canonical chondrocyte, BMP/TGF-beta, FOXA1/EMT, and GATA/GLI axes were absent.
finding_consequence: It prevents over-reading the screen as a miniature cartilage or kidney TRPS1 program and shows that the few P16 neuronal responders are a different molecular surface.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Data-driven follow-up kept Apc as the strongest non-self positive neighbor because it up-regulated both Tnc and Atp6ap2 in the same thalamic group, while Ppp2r1a, Wac, Ctnnb1, and Tcf7l2 inverted the Atp6ap2/Pid1 arm.
finding_consequence: The top relationships were not textbook RNF4/GLI3/GATA relatives; they point, exploratorily, to a Wnt/beta-catenin and V-ATPase-adjacent axis around the Atp6ap2 sentinel.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Literature-obvious TRPS1 comparators did not phenocopy Trps1: Gli3, Runx2, Stat3, Sox9, Ext1, BMP-receptor genes, and GATA-family factors were flat in the responding thalamic group and globally sparse across the screen.
finding_consequence: A same-pathway negative is informative here: the chondrocyte/GATA/GLI/BMP cassette that explains much of TRPS biology is not operating as an acute postmitotic neuronal module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The broad neuronal null refines TRPS1 pathogenicity away from an acute, cell-autonomous postmitotic neuronal transcriptome and toward earlier or non-neuronal developmental lineages.
finding_consequence: TRPS1 is a Mendelian developmental-disease gene, but 3-4 weeks of sparse LoF in NeuN-positive juvenile neurons did not recreate the chondrocyte, renal, hair-follicle, or EMT programs known from the literature.

finding_summary: The entire FDR-supported Tshr response consisted of Kcnj4 down in L5-6 IT neurons, Stxbp1 up in NP/CT/L6b/OB glutamatergic neurons, and Arfgef3 down in Pvalb GABAergic neurons.
finding_consequence: These three genes are the only measured positive biology to carry forward; their isolation argues for local, cell-restricted candidates rather than a shared TSHR transcriptional module.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut; 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut; 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: Whole-screen signature neighbors of Tshr were tiny and non-overlapping: Fbxo11, Dnajb4, Tnpo3, Zfp322a, Pde1c, and Taok1 shared no FDR responder gene with Tshr in the matching responder groups.
finding_consequence: The neighbor calculation rules out a hidden strong convergent module and shows that Tshr sits closer to sparse rank noise than to a coherent perturbation family.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut; 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut; 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: Fshr and Lhcgr, the screened glycoprotein-hormone receptor paralogs most obvious from brain-atlas literature, were completely flat and did not phenocopy Tshr.
finding_consequence: Family membership and sparse atlas expression did not translate into shared P16 NeuN+ loss-of-function transcriptional states, so receptor paralogy is not a useful substitute for direct measurement in this screen.

finding_summary: Canonical GPCR/cAMP, beta-catenin, and thyroid-axis perturbations were non-convergent with Tshr, even though Ctnnb1 and Creb1 produced detectable responses elsewhere in the same screen.
finding_consequence: This distinguishes a true absence of the expected Tshr-to-Wnt transcriptional program in the assayed hippocampal bins from total assay blindness to Wnt/beta-catenin or CREB biology.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut; 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Usp9x loss in thalamic glutamatergic neurons produced a coordinated nominal decrease in RNA-processing factors Pabpn1, Srrm2, Hnrnpu, and Srsf11.
finding_consequence: This preserves a noncanonical molecular hypothesis: USP9X loss in adult thalamic glutamatergic neurons may stress RNA-processing factors even when developmental signaling components do not dominate the DE table.
literature_rationale: The references document USP9X biology and separately identify the measured genes' functions, but none supplies a target-specific USP9X-to-RNA-processing-transcript relationship. The observed nominal program therefore has no specific literature bridge in the dossier.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Pcsk1n down-regulation in 191 MB P MY GABA is the sole robust Usp9x-induced transcript and is therefore a cell-restricted, low-width biomarker rather than a pathway signature.
finding_consequence: The only FDR<0.10 target response should be preserved, but a one-gene signature cannot support a broad proSAAS/neuropeptide-processing program without more FDR genes.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The nearest screenwide Usp9x signature neighbors were only weakly correlated and did not share Pcsk1n, so the data-driven neighbor list is best read as non-convergence.
finding_consequence: This prevents over-interpreting rank neighbors that arise when the query signature is nearly zero; Tpr, Ufc1, Uba5, Tnpo3, and Naa20 were much stronger perturbations in 191 MB P MY GABA but did not reproduce the Usp9x hit.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA; all 19 measured Usp9x groups

finding_summary: Usp9x did not behave like an upstream driver of Wnt, Notch, TGF-beta/SMAD, or mTOR transcriptional programs in the P16 postmitotic assay.
finding_consequence: Ctnnb1, Tsc1, Tsc2, and Pten all produced measurable signatures in the same cell-group universe, whereas Smad4, Rptor, most Notch receptors, and Usp9x were flat; the literature coupling of USP9X to progenitor signaling is therefore not recovered by acute loss in differentiated neurons.
cell_types: all 19 measured Usp9x groups

finding_summary: The ankyrin-repeat dendritic-spine axis of USP9X is not captured as an Ank2/Ank3/Dcx/Shank transcriptomic phenocopy.
finding_consequence: Published Usp9x phenotypes center on ANKRD protein stabilization, axon growth, migration, aggregation, and spine density; the comparator query shows that those cytoskeletal/synaptic disease mechanisms are displaced to protein localization and morphology rather than a shared nuclear RNA response in this screen.
cell_types: cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic groups; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Opa1 and Dnm1l perturbations show that mitochondrial-dynamics stress programs are detectable in matched groups, but Vps13d does not engage them.
finding_consequence: This rejects a generic readout-mismatch explanation for missing ISR genes and argues that acute Vps13d editing failed to reach the same organelle-stress state as direct fission/fusion perturbations.
literature_rationale: Opa1 and Dnm1l provide active matched surfaces, while Vps13d was target-engaged in 151 and 191 without the ISR program. This makes the RNA-level absence informative, but VPS13D mitochondrial roles do not specifically predict that program; unengaged 066 and zero-DEG 155 are excluded.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The only downstream Vps13d FDR-significant hit was Tmx3 up-regulation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
finding_consequence: The lone effect maps to an ER redox/contact-site gene, making it a focused candidate for the earliest detectable response to VPS13D contact-site perturbation in this assay.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: VPS13 and Miro/Parkin/fission relatives do not phenocopy Vps13d in the postnatal nuclear readout.
finding_consequence: The screen directly tested the textbook comparison set and found that Vps13a, Vps13b, Vps13c, Rhot1, Mff, Prkn, Park7, Atp13a2, and Atp13a3 were also downstream-flat, so the shared VPS13/Miro organelle-contact axis is not a recurrent transcriptional module in this context.

finding_summary: Vps53 perturbation induced a compact Rhoq–Ddit3 endomembrane-remodeling and stress program in hindbrain GABAergic neurons.
finding_consequence: The dataset does not show a pan-neuronal Vps53 transcriptomic phenotype; the few conventional hits are restricted to one hindbrain GABAergic and one cortical glutamatergic class despite broad VPS53 brain expression annotations.
literature_rationale: The literature provides a specific mechanistic setting for the phenotype: VPS53 is required for endomembrane trafficking, RHOQ acts on recycling endosomes, and DDIT3 marks ER stress. However, these separately relevant facts do not complete a directional bridge predicting increased Rhoq and Ddit3 after Vps53 perturbation.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Rhoq and Ddit3 were co-induced in 191 MB P MY GABA after Vps53 perturbation.
finding_consequence: Ddit3 nominates a CHOP-like stress branch and Rhoq nominates recycling-endosome cytoskeletal remodeling, making this cell group the only Vps53 class with a two-gene adaptive/stress signature.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Proteasome and clathrin perturbations were the strongest positive Vps53 signature neighbors and recapitulated the Ddit3 stress axis.
finding_consequence: Cross-perturbation convergence argues that the Ddit3 component of Vps53 is a general proteostasis/trafficking stress response, not a specific molecular readout of GARP tethering.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Vps53 produced only 3 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 21 measured neuronal groups, confined to 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
finding_consequence: The result is not a pan-neuronal GARP/EARP transcriptional collapse; it is a sparse, cell-class-selective postnatal response consistent with strong buffering of many primary vesicle-trafficking defects.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Farp1 was the sole FDR<0.10 gene in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
finding_consequence: FARP1 is a postsynaptic Rac1/F-actin synaptogenic regulator, so its isolated induction suggests a cortical synaptic or actin-compensatory response rather than the lysosomal stress program expected from severe GARP loss.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: The measured GARP/SNARE/COG relatives did not phenocopy Vps53; direct GARP partner Vps54 responded in a different thalamic group while Vps53 was flat there.
finding_consequence: This prevents over-interpreting Vps53 as a generic GARP loss signature and shows that physical proximity in the trafficking apparatus did not translate into matched juvenile-neuron transcriptomes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Vps53 did not induce a broad lysosomal-cargo, transferrin-recycling, UPR, sterol, or sphingolipid transcriptional program.
finding_consequence: Canonical GARP/EARP loss can cause lysosomal and lipid-routing defects, but this postmitotic snRNA response contained Ddit3 without coordinated M6PR/TFRC/lysosome/UPR markers, warning that Ddit3, Rhoq, and Farp1 are not faithful biomarkers of the PCCA2 lipid-trafficking mechanism.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Wnk3 perturbation in Pvalb interneurons coupled Stim1 down-regulation with Syt3 up-regulation, forming a narrow calcium-store and secretion-related RNA program.
finding_consequence: The two FDR hits are both linked to Ca2+-dependent neuronal secretion or store-operated Ca2+ entry, placing the only multi-gene Wnk3 response in a fast-spiking inhibitory class that is relevant to GABA physiology.
literature_rationale: STIM1 and SYT3 annotations show that the two observed genes have calcium-related functions, while WNK3 references concern chloride cotransport and excitability. Functional compatibility among the endpoints does not constitute a documented WNK3-to-program bridge.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: Wnk3's sparse Pvalb and thalamic responses were not transcriptionally interchangeable with perturbations of Wnk1, Stk39, Slc12a2, or Slc12a5 in the same responsive classes.
finding_consequence: Although these genes occupy a coherent WNK-SPAK/OSR1-cation-chloride cotransporter network, the Perturb-seq readout argues against treating their transcriptional signatures as interchangeable.
literature_rationale: A specific WNK3-to-SPAK/OSR1-to-SLC12 mechanistic bridge is well documented. Because that bridge does not supply a directional expectation for cross-perturbation transcriptomic similarity, the observed non-equivalence is a pathway refinement rather than direct agreement or contradiction.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Wnk3 loss produced its clearest corrected response in Pvalb interneurons, where Syt3 increased and Stim1 decreased.
finding_consequence: The screen nominates a narrow synaptic-vesicle and ER-calcium-store module rather than a global chloride-cotransporter transcriptional module; the two genes are plausible excitability modifiers but the signature is only two genes.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: The only thalamic Wnk3 hit was down-regulation of Ppp2cb, the PP2A catalytic beta phosphatase transcript.
finding_consequence: A single phosphatase DEG is directionally consistent with the idea that WNK3 biology is organized around phosphorylation balance, but it is an exploratory transcript marker, not evidence that PP2A is a WNK3 substrate or regulator.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The expected WNK chloride-transporter axis did not phenocopy Wnk3 in the transcriptome.
finding_consequence: Wnk1, Stk39/SPAK, and Slc12a2/NKCC1 were fully or nearly flat, while Slc12a5/KCC2 evoked a 10-gene thalamic Nr4a1/Dusp1/Fos response that did not overlap the Wnk3 Pvalb pair and was much broader than Wnk3's single Ppp2cb hit in the same thalamic class.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The robust Zbtb38 markers point to small adaptive ER/calcium and oxidized-protein-repair readouts rather than to DNA replication or pluripotency genes.
finding_consequence: Rcn2 and Msra give concrete biomarkers for the only recovered neuronal response, while the absence of chaperone and autophagy sentinels argues against a full UPR or autophagy state.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Zbtb38 produced a two-cell-group, three-gene FDR response: Rcn2 in L2/3 IT ENT/PPP/RSP glutamatergic neurons and Msra plus Abhd12b in TH Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons.
finding_consequence: The measurable postnatal neuronal consequence of Zbtb38 loss is sharply restricted rather than a brain-wide transcription-factor program.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The strongest data-driven neighbors of the Zbtb38 whole measured signature were extremely weak and had no FDR-level matched response.
finding_consequence: Zbtb38 is not embedded in a common postnatal neuronal CRISPR response module; the three FDR genes are not recurrently reproduced by the nearest cosine neighbors.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Measured methyl-DNA and autophagy/pluripotency comparators did not phenocopy Zbtb38 in the matched responder groups.
finding_consequence: DNMT3A and MBD2 were flat, MECP2 produced a different TH signature, RB1CC1 lowered ER chaperones, and SOX2 lowered Tnnt1/Stam, so the Zbtb38 surface is not a generic methyl-CpG-reader or RB1CC1-autophagy signature.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The expected ZBTB38 loss programs—MCM10/DNA replication, Nanog/Sox2 pluripotency, Myog myogenesis, and RB1CC1/autophagy or ER-stress transcription—were absent from the Zbtb38 surface.
finding_consequence: The flatness is mechanistically informative: the P16 mosaic neuronal experiment did not simply miss a large stress response that snRNA-seq should have captured, but uncoupled postmitotic neurons from pathways defined in proliferating, embryonic, muscle or injury contexts.

finding_summary: Htt perturbation triggered a sterol/lipid response that Zdhhc17 did not reproduce, despite the biochemical HTT-HIP14 connection.
finding_consequence: HTT can regulate HIP14 enzymatic activity, but the matched Perturb-seq surface separates postnatal Htt loss from Zdhhc17 loss: Htt induced Fasn/Hmgcs1 in 151 TH and a Srebf2/Ldlr/Sqle/Fdft1/Dhcr24/Cyp51 module in 155 MB, whereas Zdhhc17 had no robust 155 MB downstream genes and only Tubb3 in 151 TH.
literature_rationale: Htt has an active signed sterol response on the measured surface that Zdhhc17 does not reproduce, but the biochemical HTT-HIP14 connection does not predict convergence or divergence for this transcriptional program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The only reproducible Zdhhc17-like transcript across data-driven neighbors was a restricted 151 TH Tubb3 decrease shared with Chp1 and Slc17a5, while whole-surface similarity to every target was negligible.
finding_consequence: This keeps the data-driven convergence honest: the screen does not nominate an HIP14 complex, but it does show that the Tubb3 signal is not unique to Zdhhc17 because independent non-HIP14 perturbations can converge on the same thalamic cytoskeletal readout.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Zdhhc17 loss produced one robust downstream transcript in the whole screen: Tubb3 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The only FDR-supported neuronal mRNA phenotype is a thalamic class-III beta-tubulin decrease, not a broad canonical synaptic or stress program, so the screen localizes Zdhhc17's acute transcriptional footprint to a very narrow cytoskeletal marker.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Canonical HIP14 synaptic substrates and palmitoylated glutamate-receptor perturbations did not copy the Zdhhc17 Tubb3 response, and Grin1/Grin2b showed that synaptic targets can be transcriptionally visible where Zdhhc17 is almost flat.
finding_consequence: The expected SNAP25/CSP/GAD65/PSD-95/AMPA/NMDA axis is largely post-translational for Zdhhc17 here: Dlg4, Dnajc5, Gad2, and the AMPA subunits were flat or nearly flat, Snap25 had a different one-gene 151 TH response, and Grin1/Grin2b drove broad DE without sharing Tubb3.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Zfp612 perturbation increased Notum in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut without inducing the broader Axin2/Nkd1 feedback response seen with Apc perturbation, indicating a focused Wnt-modulatory output rather than global canonical Wnt activation.
finding_consequence: NOTUM is a secreted Wnt antagonist, and Apc and Ctnnb1 perturbations validate Notum as Wnt-responsive in the same cell class; selective Notum induction therefore points to a focused Wnt-modulatory output rather than global canonical Wnt activation.
literature_rationale: The literature separately establishes a general KRAB-ZFP repression mechanism, a different direct Zfp612 target, and NOTUM biology. General family mechanism plus downstream-gene function does not constitute a target-specific Zfp612-to-Notum bridge.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Zfp612 loss produced a one-gene Notum increase in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, while most other neuronal groups were FDR-flat.
finding_consequence: The strongest brain response is not the known Il1rl1 sensory-neuron program but a highly restricted Notum/Wnt-output fragment in one thalamic-related glutamatergic class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut cells carried the only multi-gene Zfp612 response, with Nrcam down and Impact up.
finding_consequence: This shows that Zfp612 is not completely silent in postnatal brain neurons, but the two significant genes are a marker-level adhesion/translation-regulator pair rather than a coherent stress or chromatin-collapse program.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: The restricted Zfp612 signature converged with Apc and opposed Ap2s1/Ctnnb1 through Notum in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
finding_consequence: Cross-perturbation pins the Zfp612 151 hit to a Wnt-sensitive Notum axis: Apc perturbation also increased Notum, whereas Ap2s1 and Ctnnb1 drove Notum down in the same cell group.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Setdb1 did not phenocopy Zfp612 despite direct literature placing SETDB1 in a ZFP612 repressive complex.
finding_consequence: The expected same-complex comparator was measurable and active in the screen, yet it left Notum, Nrcam, and Impact flat; therefore the brain response is unlikely to be a simple generic failure of SETDB1-dependent repression.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Zic3 loss produced a small but FDR-supported response only in 308 CB GABA, where Pkd2, Galnt16, and Tspyl1 were all up-regulated.
finding_consequence: The result preserves the one true responder rather than treating Zic3 as completely flat; it localizes postmitotic sensitivity to a cerebellar GABA population and shows that the response is an isolated up-regulatory tail, not a broad transcription-factor collapse.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: The CB GABA response contains one left-right/ciliary echo, Pkd2 up-regulation, but not the canonical Zic3 Wnt, Nodal/Smad, Gli, or PCP transcriptional program.
finding_consequence: Pkd2 links the postnatal neuronal hit to the same cilia/left-right disease space as Zic3, while the absence of Axin2, Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, Gli1/2/3, Smad2/3/4, Nodal, and Vangl2 shows that the heterotaxy program is not replayed after P16 neuronal knockout.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: The measured Zic paralogs were not interchangeable with Zic3: Zic1, Zic2, and Zic4 each had zero CB GABA downstream genes and at most a single downstream hit elsewhere.
finding_consequence: This rejects a simple family-level phenocopy in the screen; the Zic3 CB GABA Pkd2/Galnt16/Tspyl1 signature is not reproduced by the paralogs present in the library.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The Wnt endpoint perturbations Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 were readily detected in thalamic glutamatergic cells, whereas Zic3 was flat in the same cell group.
finding_consequence: Because the snRNA-seq/Wilcoxon workflow can register hundreds of DE genes for Wnt transcriptional components in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the absence of a Zic3 Wnt-like program there is a biologically informative uncoupling rather than a universal readout failure.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut

finding_summary: Data-driven neighbors placed Zic3 near a Wdr26-dominated CB GABA signature rather than near Zic paralogs, but the convergence is weak and restricted to Galnt16 at FDR<0.10.
finding_consequence: This preserves an unbiased screen-derived relationship while preventing overinterpretation: Wdr26 is a broad CB GABA responder that shares Galnt16 induction, whereas top anticorrelated responders Ranbp2, Neo1, and B9d1 do not form a clean inverse of Pkd2/Galnt16/Tspyl1.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
