finding_summary: Dnajc13 loss induced a single robust downstream hit, Spred1, in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and this Spred1 induction was unique to Dnajc13 among 1982 perturbations tested for Spred1 in that cell group.
finding_consequence: The only FDR-level downstream response is a clean, cell-restricted candidate marker of an adaptive growth-factor/MAPK feedback state rather than a broad endolysosomal collapse.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut

finding_summary: Retromer, WASH, HSC70/J-domain, and Parkinson endolysosomal comparators did not converge on Dnajc13: Vps35, Hspa8, and Cltc were stronger responders in 151, while other measured pathway comparators lacked the 145 Spred1 response.
finding_consequence: Dnajc13 is linked to this machinery biochemically, but the perturbational transcriptome shows pathway uncoupling rather than a linear same-complex phenocopy.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The screen did not provide a dopaminergic or PD-like Dnajc13 signature: 215 MB Dopa was missing for Dnajc13, and PD/endolysosomal comparators failed to phenocopy the only Dnajc13 effect.
finding_consequence: The result cautions against treating sparse juvenile CRISPR LoF as a negative test of the reported dominant p.Asn855Ser Parkinson mechanism.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 215 MB Dopa

finding_summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Dpm1 produced a clipped ER-folding response whereas Dhdds and Manf perturbations generated substantially broader chaperone and stress programs.
finding_consequence: The contrast argues that the screen was capable of detecting chaperone induction, but that partial Dpm1 knockdown did not phenocopy a stronger disturbance to ER glycoprotein homeostasis.
literature_rationale: The references make the cross-perturbation comparison biologically specific, but shared ER or dolichol biology alone cannot determine relative response breadth. Thus the clipped Dpm1 response is an informative dataset result rather than a documented literature contradiction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Dpm1 perturbation induced Pdia6 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, consistent with a weak ER protein-folding response to impaired Dol-P-Man-dependent glycosylation.
finding_consequence: The two-gene response is small but biologically directional because Pdia6 is an ER protein-disulfide-isomerase gene, consistent with a weak protein-folding consequence of perturbing Dol-P-Man-dependent glycosylation.
literature_rationale: The references establish DPM1 as the catalytic source of Dol-P-Man, connect that donor to ER glycosylation, and identify PDIA6, HSPA5, PDIA3, and DDIT3 as ER folding or stress-response components. Together these links form a complete same-direction chain to the observed narrow proteostasis program; failure to establish a full canonical UPR or the exact TH selectivity lowers confidence but does not break the chain.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The Dpm1 151-group signature converged with Dhdds and, more broadly, with Gfpt1 on a glycan-stress axis.
finding_consequence: Dhdds is upstream in dolichol production and reproduced both Dpm1 genes at FDR<0.10; Gfpt1 produced a larger UPR/ISR signature and significantly up-regulated Pdia6, placing the Dpm1 signal in a lipid-sugar / donor-flux neighborhood rather than among arbitrary transcriptomic neighbors.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Measured branch genes Stt3b, Pign, Fktn, and Atf6 did not phenocopy the Dpm1/Dhdds two-gene signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: DPM1 feeds N-glycan, GPI-anchor, and O-mannose biology, but hitting one downstream branch or ATF6 did not recreate Pdia6 up/Ttyh3 down. The Dol-P-Man-axis signal is therefore not a generic consequence of any glycosylation-branch perturbation in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: In 308 CB GABA, Dstyk perturbation produced a nominally coordinated synaptic and ion-handling RNA program spanning glutamate receptors and scaffolds, calcium and excitability genes, alongside Dach1 down-regulation.
finding_consequence: The cell-type restriction nominates cerebellar GABA neurons as the main place to follow up Dstyk in this dataset and avoids diluting the signal into a nonexistent pan-brain response.
literature_rationale: General CNS expression and neurological phenotypes do not provide a target-to-transcriptomic-program bridge, and the documented signaling mechanisms do not predict this gene set.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: In 308 CB GABA, Dstyk and Wdr26 shared Dach1 down-regulation, whereas Ranbp2 shifted Dach1 in the opposite direction.
finding_consequence: The strongest cross-perturbation structure for Dstyk did not come from FGF receptors or MAPK components, so it is the main unexpected signature-neighbor result to preserve.
literature_rationale: The cross-perturbation axis is an informative dataset observation, but the references explicitly provide no demonstrated DSTYK relationship to these signature neighbors.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Dstyk produced only two FDR<0.10 downstream hits: Coro1a down in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and Dach1 down in 308 CB GABA.
finding_consequence: The measured biology is a sparse, cell-type-restricted two-gene surface rather than a broad ERK, Wnt, lysosomal, stress, or synaptic program.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: A data-driven CB GABA Dach1 axis emerged: Wdr26, the top positive Dstyk neighbor, strongly down-regulated Dach1, whereas the negative neighbor Ranbp2 up-regulated Dach1 at FDR<0.10.
finding_consequence: Cross-perturbation recurrence makes Dach1 in 308 CB GABA the only component of the otherwise tiny Dstyk signature with independent same-cell-type support, while the Ranbp2 inversion separates this axis from generic cerebellar GABA noise.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: FGF-ERK, Wnt/β-catenin, and mTOR/STING relatives in the screen did not phenocopy Dstyk in its responder groups, and several responded where Dstyk was null.
finding_consequence: The canonical DSTYK pathways were assay-detectable through related perturbations, so their absence after Dstyk loss is a Dstyk-specific uncoupling in juvenile postmitotic neurons rather than a blanket inability to measure these pathways.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut; 308 CB GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Edar loss produced a one-gene Rptor-up signature restricted to 155 MB Glut.
finding_consequence: The strongest measured Edar effect is not a canonical EDAR/NF-kappaB target but an isolated midbrain-glutamatergic Rptor transcript increase; it should be treated as an exploratory cell-state marker, not as evidence for a broader Rptor or EDAR pathway switch.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The only cortical/olfactory-association Edar responder was Zmym3 up-regulation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
finding_consequence: This preserves the second real signal without over-expanding it into a pathway: the 009 response is statistically significant but consists of one transcript and lacks a matching NF-kappaB, Wnt, Shh, or Fgf20 program.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut

finding_summary: Edar had no high-confidence whole-screen signature neighbor.
finding_consequence: The top global positive neighbors Kmt2b and Sv2a and the top biological negative neighbors Kif2a and Cltc had near-zero cosine similarity and did not share either Edar FDR gene, so cross-perturbation analysis rejects a broad convergent module.

finding_summary: The canonical EDA-EDAR/NF-kappaB ectodermal program was not recovered downstream of Edar, and measured Eda/NF-kappaB comparators were flat.
finding_consequence: Because the screen directly tested Eda and several NF-kappaB-pathway genes, their lack of transcriptional phenocopy argues that the two Edar marker genes are off-canonical neuronal events rather than a weak recovery of the textbook EDAR cascade.

finding_summary: Eif4h loss increased Hexim1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with same-gene convergence from Eif4e perturbation in that group.
finding_consequence: HEXIM1 marks a transcription-elongation brake and is a compact, FDR-passing thalamic readout of EIF4H perturbation even though a full stress or translation program was absent.
literature_rationale: The FDR-supported Hexim1 increase is strengthened by the supplied positive Eif4e comparator, satisfying the sparse-claim standard through internal replication. No target-specific literature bridge establishes the EIF4H-to-HEXIM1 edge, so the interpretation remains narrow.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Eif4h produced an exploratory one-gene Syt1 up-signature in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
finding_consequence: Syt1 is a synaptic-vesicle calcium sensor, so the only hypothalamic glutamatergic hit points to a narrow synaptic-release state rather than a broad translation-collapse response.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: Among measured eIF4F/translation relatives, only Eif4e converged with Eif4h on Hexim1 in 151, while Eif4a2 and Eif4g1 did not phenocopy Eif4h.
finding_consequence: The result converts a textbook same-initiation-complex expectation into a ranked in vivo postnatal contrast: cap-binding EIF4E has a broad thalamic transcriptional footprint; EIF4H and EIF4A2/G1 are much more buffered in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Eif5a perturbation selectively up-regulated the ErbB4 ligand Nrg3 in Pvalb GABA neurons.
finding_consequence: The only strong positive hit points to a synapse-adhesion ligand that is already linked to excitatory input onto parvalbumin interneurons, nominating Nrg3 as a Pvalb-specific reporter rather than a generic translation-stress marker.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: Eif5a weakly but FDR-significantly down-regulated Dgkz in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons.
finding_consequence: DGKζ couples postsynaptic DAG turnover to spine maintenance; a thalamic Dgkz decrease nominates synaptic lipid signaling as the second, much weaker, Eif5a-responsive marker in the screen.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Expected translation-factor neighbors did not phenocopy Eif5a.
finding_consequence: Although Eef2 was the top positive whole-screen neighbor and is physically/functionally adjacent to eIF5A on the ribosome, its cosine to Eif5a was only 0.046 and it produced 1119 significant genes, while the two Eif5a marker genes were not reproduced by Eef2.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Other translation-related perturbations were either nearly flat or regulated Eif5a marker genes in conflicting directions.
finding_consequence: The measured translation neighborhood separates Eif5a from generic changes in elongation, initiation, ISR sensing, and ribosome rescue: Eif4g1 and Eif2ak4 were completely flat, Eif4a2/Eif4h/Hbs1l had only two FDR hits each, Eif4e converged with Dgkz down, and Eef1a2 drove Dgkz up.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Eif5a did not induce a detectable ISR/UPR/proteostasis bounce-back program, despite the assay being capable of detecting broad stress states.
finding_consequence: The absence of Atf4/Ddit3/Hspa5/Xbp1-like stress induction argues that P16 Eif5a-edited surviving neurons are not simply running an unobserved ER-stress program; this absence is informative because Psmc1 and Psmb4 perturbations generated thousands of FDR<0.10 genes in the same screen.

finding_summary: In the responsive 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut surface, Epha5 perturbation decreased Lnpep but did not recover the literature-nominated NMDAR/PSD-95 synaptogenic transcriptional program.
finding_consequence: The limbic class aligns anatomically with known hippocampal EphA5 biology, but the measured mRNA response points to an atypical distal marker rather than a simple loss of the published early-development NMDA/PSD95 program.
literature_rationale: A specific EphA5-to-synaptogenic-program bridge exists, but it is based mainly on ligand-driven developmental or physiological activation. The absence of a coherent RNA program is not itself directional disagreement, and the sole significant Lnpep effect lacks literature linkage.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut

finding_summary: Data-driven Epha5 signature neighbors were weak and were rejected as FDR-level phenocopies after direct remeasurement.
finding_consequence: The nearest-neighbor exercise is informative because it shows that neither the top whole-screen neighbors nor the top 012-restricted neighbors recreate the only robust Epha5 feature, arguing against a hidden broad co-perturbation module.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut

finding_summary: Epha5 has a single robust downstream transcriptomic effect, Lnpep down-regulation in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
finding_consequence: This preserves the one true FDR-level response instead of diluting it into a mostly null screen-wide surface; the positive result lies in a hippocampal/amygdala glutamatergic class that is plausible for EphA5 biology, but it is much narrower than an axon-guidance transcriptome.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut

finding_summary: The Epha5-Lnpep response is uncoupled from the literature-obvious Eph receptor family and from screened Fyn/Rac/PAK/LIMK/Ras/SHP effector nodes in the same 012 cell group.
finding_consequence: EphA5 is a canonical Eph/ephrin receptor, but the screen shows that this postnatal nuclear RNA response is not a simple family-wide Eph-loss phenotype or a broad transcriptional collapse of the usual cytoskeletal effector arm.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut

finding_summary: Known EphA7 downstream nodes, especially Tsc1/Tsc2 and MEK/ERK-linked genes, did not phenocopy Epha7.
finding_consequence: Tsc1 and Tsc2 were strongly transcriptional in the same platform, so the Epha7 null is not because this screen cannot detect mTOR/lysosomal homeostatic states; Epha7 simply did not engage such a state at P16-P44.
literature_rationale: The references establish specific downstream EphA7 signaling mediators, but not the RNA-level expectations tested by this unit. Consequently, the measured nonconvergence and lack of ligand/effector transcriptional feedback do not oppose a documented directional prediction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The full-screen, feature-centered Epha7 signature had no strong positive or negative neighbor.
finding_consequence: The strongest correlations were only about five percent and involved weak or control-like profiles, indicating that Epha7 is not hiding in a coherent recurrent perturbation module.

finding_summary: Screened EphA and EphB receptor paralogs did not form an acute neuronal Eph transcriptomic module with Epha7.
finding_consequence: The expected same-family comparison was directly measurable: receptor paralogs were largely flat or had isolated singleton hits, while the ephrin ligands that dominate the EphA7 interaction prior were not perturbed in this screen.

finding_summary: Erbb4 had no substantive global signature neighbor: the strongest dense-score cosines were <0.04 in magnitude except a limited-coverage Fbxo11 anticorrelation, and the robust Chp1 sterol module was absent from Erbb4.
finding_consequence: The data-driven search did not nominate a hidden module to explain Erbb4; even the closest positive neighbor, Chp1, produced a clear SREBF/cholesterol response that Erbb4 lacked.

finding_summary: The screened ERBB-family and neuregulin relatives did not phenocopy Erbb4: Erbb3 and Nrg3 had no FDR<0.10 response, Nrg1/Nrg2 were tiny responders, and all four had dense-score cosine |cos|<=0.022 to Erbb4.
finding_consequence: Biochemical ligand-receptor relationships did not translate into a shared cell-autonomous postnatal snRNA signature; this is consistent with NRG ligands acting in trans across synapses rather than in the same nucleus as Erbb4.

finding_summary: Canonical intracellular ERBB4 effectors and partners were measured but remained nearly orthogonal to Erbb4: Dlg4, Mapk1, Pik3ca, Pik3r1, Raf1, Stat5b, Adam10 and App had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and Mtor had only six.
finding_consequence: The expected activity of ERBB4 through MAPK, PI3K, STAT, PDZ and proteolytic coupling is not represented as a shared steady-state snRNA program in this P16-P37/44 assay.

finding_summary: The only cortical FDR<0.10 response was Slc2a3 up-regulation in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
finding_consequence: The signal is narrow, but it nominates neuronal glucose transport rather than a classical oxytocin or serotonin transcript as the cortical marker of Esr2 loss in this assay.

finding_summary: The strongest Esr2 response was Jmjd6 up-regulation in 155 MB Glut.
finding_consequence: Jmjd6 is an RNA/chromatin-associated dioxygenase, so the responder midbrain glutamatergic population shows a compact nuclear-processing marker rather than a neuropeptide transmitter switch.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The data-driven Esr2 neighbors were statistically weak and mostly rejected by exact shared-gene testing.
finding_consequence: The best neighbor correlations over the responder groups were only r≈0.08 or -0.06; Tpr shared Jmjd6 up-regulation but also caused a 3109-gene MB Glut response, showing that Esr2 is not embedded in a robust recurrent perturbation module.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Estrogen/steroid-receptor and related nuclear-receptor perturbations did not phenocopy Esr2 in the two responder groups.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Etv6 loss produced a single robust Kdm4c induction in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut

finding_summary: Etv6 loss produced a single robust Adora1 induction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

finding_summary: Kmt2a is a responding ETV6-network chromatin comparator, but it diverges from Etv6 rather than sharing the Adora1/Kdm4c reporters.
finding_consequence: Kmt2a produced 25 FDR<0.10 genes in the same thalamic class where Etv6 produced only Adora1, showing that this cell group can mount a broad chromatin-regulator transcriptomic response and that the Etv6 result is not a generic Kmt2a-like chromatin phenotype.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut

finding_summary: The neuronal Etv6 signature is uncoupled from the canonical TEL/ETV6 hematopoietic, vascular, and FLI1-linked repressor programs.
finding_consequence: Despite all 23 neuronal groups being tested, 21 had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes and the two responders had only Kdm4c or Adora1, so acute postnatal neuronal loss does not recreate the embryonic yolk-sac, bone-marrow, erythroid, or lymphoid programs that dominate Etv6 biology.

finding_summary: Other ETS factors and ETV6-associated hematopoietic or fusion-network genes did not phenocopy Etv6 in neurons.
finding_consequence: Ets1, Elf2, Erf, Spi1, Ntrk3, Pbx1, Flt3, Gata2, Ebf1, Pax5, Pdgfrb, Phf6, Runx2, and Runx3 were directly measurable but did not induce Kdm4c in 027 or Adora1 in 151, converting an expected-family comparison into a measured rejection.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Fam120a loss yields only a narrow Luc7l3 decrease in 155 MB Glut and does not reproduce the broad Srsf1 perturbation response, placing FAM120A as a buffered or upstream contributor rather than a limiting core splicing regulator in basal neurons.
finding_consequence: This weakens the hypothesis that FAM120A is a limiting core splicing regulator in basal post-mitotic mouse brain cells, while leaving open a context-specific role under mTORC1/lipogenic stimulation.
literature_rationale: The literature supplies a specific FAM120A–SRSF1 splicing mechanism and identifies LUC7L3 as a splicing factor, but it does not complete the bridge to the observed Luc7l3 decrease or the perturbation-response asymmetry.

finding_summary: In Pvalb interneurons, Fam120a loss produced a singleton but FDR-significant induction of the ESCRT-0/endosomal sorting gene Hgs.
finding_consequence: The only robust Pvalb responder points to receptor/endosome handling rather than the canonical SREBP, AGO2 or oxidative-stress pathways, so it is best treated as a Pvalb-restricted endosomal compensation marker to validate, not as a pathway-wide response.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: In midbrain glutamatergic neurons, Fam120a loss down-regulated Luc7l3, a U1 snRNP/prespliceosome-associated splicing gene; the direct U1-70K perturbation Snrnp70 also strongly reduced Luc7l3 in the same cell group.
finding_consequence: This is the only point where Fam120a touches its curated RNA-splicing biology in the screen, and Snrnp70 convergence makes the singleton biologically plausible while showing that Fam120a is far upstream or buffered relative to core spliceosome disruption.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Fam120a loss did not recover the SREBP/lipogenic target program, even in cell groups where Srebf2 perturbation directly produced sterol-gene decreases.
finding_consequence: The result separates FAM120A from being a required neuronal cofactor for basal SREBP2-dependent sterol transcription; this assay could see Dhcr24/Insig1/Msmo1/Ldlr-type responses when the sterol regulator itself was perturbed.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Neither unbiased neighbors nor literature-obvious partners formed a strong Fam120a-like signature module.

finding_summary: Fbxo38 perturbation did not recover the expected KLF7-axis transcriptional response, including Klf7 and Cdkn1a, in the thalamic group where direct Klf7 perturbation was transcriptionally active.
finding_consequence: Prior FBXO38/MoKA literature motivates a KLF7-axis expectation, but the Perturb-seq signatures show near-zero Fbxo38-Klf7, Fbxo38-Fbxw7, and Fbxo38-Fbxo11 correlations and no adjusted response of Klf7 or Cdkn1a after Fbxo38 perturbation.
literature_rationale: Target-specific studies directly identify FBXO38 as a KLF7 coactivator and show that an FBXO38 disease variant impairs KLF7 target-gene activation. The observed lack of a KLF7-axis RNA response is directionally opposite to that expectation, but weak perturbation engagement makes the dataset result non-informative under the governing rule.

finding_summary: Fbxo38 perturbation induced Hdac2 in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, where Hdac2 was the only FDR<0.10 downstream transcript.
finding_consequence: The most significant Fbxo38 response nominates a chromatin-deacetylase state, not the canonical FBXO38-PD-1 or FBXO38-KLF7 genes, as a cell-restricted candidate readout.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Fbxo38 was almost flat across the screen: only 2 of 22 measured cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and each responder had exactly one.
finding_consequence: The phenotype is not a broad SCF, stress, or axon-growth program; interpretation must start from the two singleton responses and the much larger null surface.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Fbxo38 downregulated Trappc11 in 191 MB P MY GABA, and Trappc11 is a high-ranking STRING functional partner of mouse Fbxo38.
finding_consequence: The only significant GABA/brainstem-associated response touches a vesicle-trafficking gene that is network-proximal to Fbxo38, suggesting a trafficking candidate rather than a random tail gene.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The expected FBXO38-KLF7 axon-growth transcriptional program was absent after Fbxo38 perturbation in every measured cell group.
finding_consequence: Cdkn1a, L1cam, Ntrk1, Ntrk2, and Gap43 are direct transcriptional readouts that snRNA-seq should detect if this pathway were engaged in the assayed neurons; their uniform FDR 1.0 makes the negative result biologically interpretable.

finding_summary: Cirbp was induced in Sst GABA nuclei after Fgf14 perturbation.

finding_summary: Scarb2 was induced in L5 extratelencephalic cortical glutamatergic neurons.

finding_summary: Fgf14 did not phenocopy same-family FHF paralogs, Nav-channel genes, or Ank3 on the transcriptomic axis.

finding_summary: The screen-wide top positive and negative Fgf14 neighbors were weak and non-robust.

finding_summary: The juvenile snRNA surface is flat where FGF14 ataxia biology predicts ion-channel and cerebellar physiology rather than broad nuclear remodeling.

finding_summary: Genetic Fkbp1a depletion was transcriptomically non-equivalent to loss of calcineurin-pathway components in an informative thalamic surface.
finding_consequence: It separates loss of FKBP12 protein from the FKBP12-FK506 drug complex that inhibits calcineurin, limiting any interpretation that Fkbp1a CRISPRi is equivalent to calcineurin-inhibitor treatment.
literature_rationale: The literature directly distinguishes unliganded FKBP12 from the FKBP12–FK506 inhibitory complex. The observed lack of convergence between Fkbp1a depletion and engaged calcineurin-pathway perturbations therefore matches the documented mechanism.

finding_summary: A data-first search found only weak restricted-signature neighbors, led by Ski in the positive direction and Htr7/Pi4ka/Foxj3 in the negative direction.

finding_summary: Fkbp1a loss did not phenocopy the drug-induced FKBP12-mTOR or FKBP12-calcineurin axes; direct Mtor/Rptor and calcineurin-subunit perturbations themselves were weak and did not converge with Fkbp1a.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: The embryonic TGF-beta/BMP/Notch receptor neighborhood of FKBP12 was not reconstituted in postmitotic neurons.
finding_consequence: The known Fkbp1a developmental cardiac/endocardial mechanism is displaced from this assay in both lineage and stage; weak Acvr1, Tgfbr2, and Notch1 single-gene responses contrasted with a zero-gene Fkbp1a surface.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut; 054 CNU-MGE GABA

finding_summary: Flrt3 acute loss produced a very narrow L2/3 excitatory surface: Dapk1 was up in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and Odc1 was up in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, while every other measured class had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.

cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

finding_summary: The two Flrt3 responder groups did not recover a pathway-proximal FGF/MAPK, immediate-early, FLRT-receptor, or synaptic-activity transcriptional program.
finding_consequence: The assay detected Dapk1 and Odc1 but not the transcripts most directly expected if postnatal Flrt3 loss were driving a somatic FGF or FLRT-UNC5/latrophilin response, refining the result toward a sparse secondary state rather than canonical pathway activation.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

finding_summary: Direct receptor-axis comparators were flat where Flrt3 responded: Adgrl1, Adgrl2, Adgrl3, Unc5c, and Unc5d each had zero FDR<0.10 downstream genes in both L2/3 responder groups and did not induce Dapk1 or Odc1.
finding_consequence: Physical FLRT3 binding partners are first-pass comparators, but their acute cell-autonomous transcriptional profiles do not phenocopy Flrt3, consistent with ligand-receptor sidedness, developmental timing, or synaptic effects that are not captured as a shared soma-wide RNA program.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

finding_summary: Fmn2 produced a two-cell-type, one-gene-up signature: Ss18 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and Pign in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
finding_consequence: The only robust downstream effects are narrow sentinel transcripts, not a broad actin, stress, synaptic, or Wnt module; Pign is an FDR<0.10 but not FDR<0.05 hit, so this is a hypothesis-generating cell-type-selective response.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA

finding_summary: The unbiased nearest neighbors of the Fmn2 whole-transcriptome surface were not biological convergers.
finding_consequence: Nearest-neighbor analysis returned very small cosine values and the top positive and negative neighbors had no FDR<0.10 genes in the two Fmn2 responder groups, preventing a noise-level global correlation from being elevated into a mechanistic module.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA

finding_summary: The canonical Fmn2 actin-nucleation, Spire-vesicle, growth-cone, and Wnt/β-catenin expectations were not converted into an FDR-level postmitotic nuclear transcriptome.
finding_consequence: This is an informative negative result: Fmn2 is a cortical and adult-brain actin regulator, but acute P16 mosaic LoF did not elicit the stress, cytoskeletal, Wnt, or synaptic-gene cascade that would have been visible in snRNA-seq if it were a major secondary response.

finding_summary: Measured formin/Wnt/HDAC5 comparators did not phenocopy Fmn2: Fmn1 was flat, while Ctnnb1 and Lrp6 produced thalamic Wnt-like signatures rather than an L4/5 IT or CNU-LGE signature.
finding_consequence: The screen can detect a Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional readout when core Wnt nodes are removed, so Fmn2's failure to move Axin2 or many other Wnt targets is specific to postmitotic Fmn2 perturbation rather than a global inability of the dataset to read Wnt biology.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The FMN2 disease surface is best read as structural/developmental rather than as a broad acute neuronal nuclear-DE liability in this juvenile screen.
finding_consequence: Human FMN2 loss and Fmn2 animal models affect intellectual disability, synaptic density, memory, growth-cone mechanics, and circuit wiring; the near-flat P16-to-P37 snRNA-seq phenotype argues that those liabilities can occur without a large cell-autonomous transcriptional collapse in surviving postmitotic forebrain and brainstem neurons.

finding_summary: Fntb perturbation produced a coordinated Nefl/Nefh/Nefm neurofilament upshift in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, with Nefl FDR-supported.
finding_consequence: A cell-restricted axonal-cytoskeletal marker is more interpretable than a single isolated Nefl row and is directionally compatible with literature showing that neuronal farnesyltransferase can influence neuronal morphology or AD-related neuronal signaling.
literature_rationale: The literature provides a target-specific neuronal perturbation bridge, but the required directional step from altered neurite or neuronal signaling biology to neurofilament transcriptional upregulation is absent.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: The two Fntb responder groups were one-gene islands rather than a shared program: Lhfpl4 was up in CA3/CA2-fasciola cinerea/dentate glutamatergic neurons, and Nefl was up in pontine/myelencephalic/pineal glutamatergic neurons.
finding_consequence: The observed positives are useful as a restricted-signature hypothesis for tetraspan-membrane and axonal-cytoskeletal genes, but they should not be inflated into canonical farnesyltransferase pathway recovery.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: The data-driven full-vector neighbors were not biologically retained as Fntb-like phenotypes: top neighbors Mpc1 and Fmn1 were themselves FDR-flat, Med15 responded elsewhere, and the lowest-ranked Psmc1/Psmb4 signatures were broad proteasome-subunit responses rather than anti-Fntb programs.
finding_consequence: The cross-perturbation calculation shows that an almost-null target can have apparent neighbors in the unthresholded logFC manifold while failing the matched FDR-surface test.

finding_summary: Screened Ras/mevalonate comparators did not phenocopy Fntb: Hras, Kras, and Rala were FDR-flat, and Hmgcr, Rac1, and Cdc42 had only isolated one-gene or three-gene outputs.
finding_consequence: The expected CAAX/RAS route is not hidden in another canonical perturbation in this dataset; within the same P16 neuronal assay both the farnesyltransferase node and several pathway relatives are transcriptionally weak.

finding_summary: Degs1 was the sole FDR<0.10 responder in Pvalb interneurons after Gata2 perturbation.
finding_consequence: DEGS1 links the only Pvalb hit to sphingolipid desaturation and nominates a narrow lipid-metabolic marker rather than a GABAergic identity switch.

finding_summary: Mlec was selectively down-regulated in 145 MH-LH TH Glut nuclei after Gata2 perturbation.
finding_consequence: MLEC places the strongest Gata2 hit in an ER N-glycan quality-control component, but as a one-gene module it is a marker hypothesis rather than a demonstrated unfolded-protein response.

finding_summary: The data-driven Gata2 nearest neighbors were very low-cosine and failed exact marker-level convergence on Degs1 and Mlec.
finding_consequence: This prevents over-reading Kansl1, Dip2b, Tubb4a, Eif4e, Nhs, Cnot1, or Pde10a as mechanistic Gata2 partners; their ranking reflects diffuse weak covariance across a nearly flat signature.

finding_summary: GATA-family and developmental comparators did not phenocopy Gata2 in matched postnatal neurons.
finding_consequence: The absence of convergence from Gata3, Gata1, Gata4, Gata6, Lmx1b, and Zfpm2 shows that the weak Gata2 effects are not a shared GATA-fate signature in this assay.

finding_summary: Embryonic Gata2 neuronal fate markers were absent from the postnatal Gata2 DE surface.
finding_consequence: The assay would have detected a transcriptional maintenance requirement for GABAergic or serotonergic fate genes, so their FDR=1.0 values argue the canonical Gata2/Gata3 developmental cascade is not active in the assayed nuclei.

finding_summary: Canonical glutathione/NFE2L2 antioxidant transcripts were not induced after Gclm perturbation.
finding_consequence: GCLM belongs to the rate-limiting GSH-synthesis enzyme and is an NFE2L2-response gene, so the absence of Gclc, Gsr, Gss, Hmox1, Nqo1, Slc7a11, Slc3a2 and Txnrd1 responses shows that basal postnatal neuronal Gclm loss did not cross a transcriptional redox-stress threshold.
literature_rationale: Broad sentinel coverage across responsive groups, together with consistently reduced Gclm RNA, makes absence of the expected antioxidant program informative. Chronic Gclm deficiency directly predicts the opposite outcome: induction of redox-regulated genes.

finding_summary: Gclm produced only two downstream FDR<0.10 events: Fam91a1 up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Epha7 up in 308 CB GABA.
finding_consequence: The positive biology is a sparse, cell-restricted pair of responses rather than a widespread oxidative-stress state; both singleton genes should be treated as markers of responder compartments, not as full pathways.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Screenwide Gclm signature-neighbor analysis did not nominate a high-correlation module.
finding_consequence: The strongest correlations were near zero, so the cross-perturbation landscape independently supports the interpretation that Gclm is a near-null RNA perturbation in this assay.

finding_summary: Same-pathway perturbations Gclc, Gpx4 and Nfe2l2 failed to converge with the two-gene Gclm surface in the matched screen.
finding_consequence: The most obvious GSH-pathway relatives were directly measurable, and their flat or nearly flat surfaces argue that this experimental context suppresses a shared glutathione/ferroptosis transcriptional module rather than letting Gclm reveal one.

finding_summary: Wdr26, the strongest broad negative Gclm neighbor, drove Epha7 in the opposite direction from Gclm in 308 CB GABA.
finding_consequence: The only cerebellar GABA marker induced by Gclm is not a generic positive stress marker; an unrelated broad perturbation significantly represses it in the same cell group.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Acute P16 Gclm loss did not reproduce the Pvalb-vulnerable redox phenotype associated with developmental glutathione deficiency.
finding_consequence: The schizophrenia/PV literature is best interpreted as a chronic developmental redox-circuit model; this screen shows that sparse removal of Gclm after neuronal specification is insufficient to trigger a Pvalb nuclear transcriptome within 3-4 weeks.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

finding_summary: The only two Ghsr downstream calls were noncanonical cortical IT singletons: Cplane1 decreased in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and Slc17a5 increased in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
finding_consequence: The two signals nominate ciliary/CPLANE and lysosomal or vesicular-acidic-amino-acid transport genes as weak, cell-class-restricted biomarkers rather than as a broad ghrelin output program.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

finding_summary: The full-screen score-vector neighbors of Ghsr were essentially uncorrelated with it, with the strongest positive r only 0.033 and complete anti-neighbors near -0.012.
finding_consequence: The apparent Ghsr response is not a member of a recurring screen-wide transcriptional module; the genome-wide surface behaves like a sparse singleton phenotype.

finding_summary: Literature-obvious appetite and neuromodulatory GPCR comparators did not phenocopy Ghsr in the two responder cortical groups.
finding_consequence: Ghsr's weak Cplane1/Slc17a5 surface is not a generic consequence of perturbing orexigenic receptors, dopamine receptors, opioid receptors, or proximal GPCR second messengers in this assay.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

finding_summary: Ghsr loss did not recover the expected hypothalamic Agrp/Npy/Pomc neuropeptide axis in the broad hypothalamic-enriched groups.
finding_consequence: The canonical feeding circuit is displaced from this bulked cell-class, unstimulated snRNA endpoint; the absence of Agrp, Npy and Pomc DE is informative rather than a reason to mine nominal genes for a hidden program.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 145 MH-LH TH Glut

finding_summary: Gli1 perturbation yielded sparse noncanonical effects without the expected Hedgehog/GLI feedback program in the responding neuronal groups.
finding_consequence: GLI1 is normally a transcriptional effector in the Hh network; the FDR-null pathway genes and near-zero related-target correlations argue that the observed neuronal response is uncoupled from canonical Hh feedback.
literature_rationale: The literature specifically places GLI1 in Hedgehog transcription and documents substantial GLI1–GLI2 functional redundancy. These facts make the observed lack of a canonical program biologically interpretable, but they do not form an unambiguous directional bridge to the tested transcriptomic absence.

finding_summary: The Amph decrease in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut recurred after perturbing Psmc5, Psmc1, and Psmb4, nominating a local Amph-centered response that Gli1 shares with proteasome-subunit perturbations.
finding_consequence: Cross-perturbation recurrence makes Amph less likely to be an isolated barcode accident and links the hypothalamic Gli1 hit to a broader perturbational state, although not to the canonical HH pathway.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: Gli1 loss produced only two robust downstream hits in the whole 23-class neuronal screen: Mctp1 decreased in 052 Pvalb Gaba and Amph decreased in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
finding_consequence: The actual Gli1 phenotype is a sparse, cell-type-restricted vesicle/endocytic signature rather than a broad Hedgehog target-gene program; because each responder contains only one FDR-level gene, the biological program is hypothesis-generating.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: Measured Hedgehog relatives did not phenocopy Gli1: Gli2, Gli3, Ptch1, Ptch2, Gpr161, and Prkaca were completely flat, and Smo and Cdon produced only isolated effects in other cell groups without changing Mctp1 or Amph.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

finding_summary: Despite FDR-supported Gnptg depletion in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 155 MB Glut, canonical lysosomal hydrolase, receptor, membrane, and TFEB-axis transcripts showed no coordinated response.
finding_consequence: GNPTG disease biology is proximal to post-translational hydrolase mannose-6-phosphorylation, not necessarily to a cell-autonomous lysosomal transcriptional stress signature, so transcriptional panels alone are likely insensitive proximal biomarkers.
literature_rationale: The references form a complete mechanistic bridge from gamma-subunit loss to partial, substrate-selective post-translational targeting defects rather than wholesale lysosomal transcriptional activation, aligning with the absence of a coordinated RNA panel response.

finding_summary: Large V-ATPase and mTOR-axis responses in the same parquet contrast with Gnptg: Atp6v0c, Tsc1, and Tsc2 had 1086, 1617, and 636 downstream FDR<0.10 calls, respectively, while Gnptg had zero.

finding_summary: The screen showed the same transcriptional buffering for several GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase, M6P-receptor/sortilin, lysosomal cargo, and lysosomal membrane comparators: Gnptab, Igf2r, Sorl1, Arsb, Psap, and Ctsb each had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.

finding_summary: Detectable Gns RNA depletion in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 155 MB Glut produced no FDR-supported secondary transcriptional response, separating acute neuronal target depletion from the chronic lysosomal-storage expression phenotype.

literature_rationale: Target-specific mouse studies complete the chain from Gns deficiency through substrate storage and lysosomal disruption to brain pathology. The acute transcriptional absence is directionally opposite to that established deficiency program, with reduced confidence because residual enzyme, cross-correction, and shorter latency could buffer an RNA response.

finding_summary: The top raw signature neighbors of GNS had score-cosines no larger than 0.030 and failed cycle-back validation as real GNS-like responders.

finding_summary: Rab7 and Atp6v0c elicited hundreds to thousands of DE genes in the same screen while GNS was flat in the same thalamic and midbrain groups.

finding_summary: Canonical GPRASP2-linked programs were absent from the Gprasp2 DE surface: mGluR5/synaptic markers, Smoothened-Hedgehog targets, and lysosomal-stress markers all had FDR=1.0 across the measured groups.
finding_consequence: The screen did not recover a hidden transcriptomic version of the known GPCR- or SMO-trafficking biology; it places the acute neuronal phenotype, if present, upstream of basal nuclear RNA abundance.

finding_summary: The closest positive full-screen neighbors were UFMylation and ER/ribosome-quality-control perturbations, especially Uba5 and Ufc1, but they were dramatically broader than Hbs1l and shared none of its two FDR anchor genes.

finding_summary: The canonical PELO/ABCE1/HBS1L machinery could not be tested as same-complex perturbations, and the indirect translation targets that were present—Rack1, Eif5a, Eif2ak4, and Nsun2—did not converge with Hbs1l.
finding_consequence: This prevents an over-read of missing phenocopy: the screen mainly lacked the direct HBS1L rescue partners, while the available translation comparators had zero shared FDR anchors with Hbs1l.

finding_summary: Hdac5 loss produced a single robust downstream event, Chd5 up-regulation, only in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
finding_consequence: The lone FDR-significant response links HDAC5 perturbation to a neuronal chromatin-remodeler transcript in a hippocampal/amygdalar glutamatergic compartment, not to a broad pan-neuronal stress or synaptic program.

finding_summary: The Hdac5 perturbation did not induce the expected NPAS4, immediate-early, or NPAS4-target gene program.
finding_consequence: This separates the juvenile basal CRISPR phenotype from stimulus-evoked HDAC5 biology in which HDAC5 gates activity-responsive transcription.

finding_summary: Hdac4, the only assayed class-IIa HDAC paralog, was flat and did not phenocopy Hdac5.
finding_consequence: The paralog contrast argues against a simple interchangeable class-IIa-HDAC loss signature in this in vivo screen.

finding_summary: MEF2C perturbation was detectable but diverged from Hdac5.
finding_consequence: A MEF2-family transcriptional program can be recovered by this assay, yet HDAC5 loss did not release that program, placing basal HDAC5 upstream of neither the cortical nor Pvalb Mef2c dependency captured here.

finding_summary: Measured CaMK and 14-3-3 perturbations did not converge on the Hdac5 Chd5 response.
finding_consequence: The upstream phosphorylation/export circuitry described for HDAC5 is signal-gated; constitutive single-gene LoF of available Camk or 14-3-3 paralogs was not equivalent to deleting Hdac5 in the basal screen.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut; 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

finding_summary: Rack1 up-regulation is the only robust cortical output of Herc2 loss in the screen.
finding_consequence: Rack1 marks the L5 ET CTX Glut response without invoking an unsupported broad ribosome or translation program; it is a candidate single-gene reporter of HERC2 perturbation in corticofugal neurons.

finding_summary: Dlat up-regulation is the only FDR-supported thalamic output of Herc2 perturbation.

finding_summary: Htr2a loss increased Kcnma1 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, consistent with a focal calcium/excitability-feedback adaptation.

finding_summary: The stronger member of the Htr2a response was up-regulation of Kcnma1, a Ca2+-activated potassium-channel gene, in MGE-derived GABAergic neurons after removal of a Gq/IP3/Ca2+-coupled serotonin receptor.

finding_summary: Akr1a1 increased in the lone Nr1i2-responsive LSX GABA population.

finding_summary: Nr1i2 loss produced an extremely sparse downstream surface, with FDR<0.10 genes only in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.

finding_summary: Nr1i2 perturbation did not recover the expected CYP/ABC/UGT/SLCO xenobiotic-response cassette.

finding_summary: Screened NR1I, RXR, coactivator, and xenobiotic-receptor comparators did not reproduce the Nr1i2 LSX signature.

finding_summary: Adpgk was the lone FDR-supported pineal-containing response to Nrl perturbation and was up-regulated 1.07 logFC in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: Engaged Nrxn2 perturbations did not induce compensatory Nrxn1, Nlgn2, Nlgn3, or Dlg4 mRNA changes.
finding_consequence: The known trans-synaptic Nrxn2 adhesome appears post-transcriptionally or structurally coupled in this assay rather than being rewired by reciprocal changes in Nrxn1, Nlgn2, Nlgn3, or Dlg4 mRNA.
literature_rationale: Binding and network membership establish an adhesome, not a target-specific transcriptional compensation mechanism. The engaged negative result is informative experimentally, but it has no documented literature expectation to agree with or contradict.

finding_summary: Nrxn2 separates surface synaptic adhesion from the stronger nuclear signatures seen for selected intracellular synaptic machinery perturbations.
finding_consequence: Stxbp1 produced 140 FDR<0.10 genes across 8 measured groups, including L4-5 IT cortex, Pvalb interneurons, and midbrain glutamatergic neurons, while Nrxn2 had none. Thus a synaptic-gene perturbation can be transcriptionally visible in this assay, but Nrxn2's surface adhesion biology is not obligatorily coupled to the same nuclear response.
literature_rationale: The defensible relationship is narrowed to target-engaged group 155 and the active Stxbp1 comparator. The mostly weak additional synaptic comparators cannot carry a generalized non-phenocopy claim, and literature does not directly establish Nrxn2 transcriptional flatness.

finding_summary: The physical neurexin adhesion network did not reappear as a shared transcriptomic module: paralogs and binding-partner perturbations were flat or only single-gene responders.
finding_consequence: Nrxn1, Nrxn3, Nlgn1/2/3, Cask, Dag1, Grid1/2, Lrrtm1/3/4, and Cntnap1/2 were expected comparators from neurexin complex biology, yet score correlations with Nrxn2 were effectively zero and total FDR<0.10 signatures were 0 to 2 genes for each target. finding_summary: The obvious neurotrophin receptor comparators did not phenocopy Ntrk3.

finding_summary: Paqr7 had only weak, noncanonical cross-screen neighbors.

This quantitative neighborhood supports treating the Paqr7 surface as near-null rather than as a hidden PAQR-family module.

finding_consequence: mPRβ/Paqr8, the nuclear progesterone receptor Pgr, Pgrmc1 and Adipor2 were obvious comparators from the PAQR/progesterone literature, yet none induced Arnt or any downstream gene at FDR<0.10 in 191 MB P MY GABA, and their restricted Paqr7-signature cosines were only 0.013-0.047.

finding_summary: Canonical PARK7 redox, Nrf2, ISR/UPR, and autophagy/mitophagy markers were absent after Park7 perturbation even though Hspa9 perturbation triggered a large Shmt2/Cyb5r1/Chac1/Herpud1 stress-like program in the same TH and MB glutamatergic populations.

literature_rationale: The claim is a powered absence test on two locally capable RNA surfaces, not a cell-selectivity claim. Hspa9 supplies an active stress-response control, but conflicting target-specific Nrf2 evidence and absent direct PARK7 protein engagement prevent a direct-opposite assignment.

finding_summary: Pde4b loss produced an isolated Map2k2 transcript increase in 155 MB Glut nuclei.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Pde4b loss produced an isolated Snx14 increase in 191 MB P MY GABA nuclei.
finding_consequence: The call nominates a specific ER/endolysosomal-lipid homeostasis transcript in a hindbrain/midbrain GABAergic context, but the perturbation did not induce a broader lysosomal or autophagy module.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Basal Pde4b perturbation did not induce the expected CREB/immediate-early/Bdnf transcriptional program.
finding_consequence: This separates a constitutive P16-to-P37 neuronal Pde4b knockout from the CREB-gene induction seen after broad PDE4 inhibition or strong PDE4B catalytic impairment, and it argues that any CREB effect is gated by activity, drug context, or phosphorylation rather than always converted into snRNA-detectable mRNA.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: In-screen PDE4 and cAMP-pathway relatives did not phenocopy Pde4b.
finding_consequence: The comparator pass rejects a simple model in which the Pde4b signature is a generic consequence of any PDE, adenylyl-cyclase, PKA, dopamine-receptor, EPAC, or ERK-node perturbation in the same neurons.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: The only Pdhb downstream hit was Galt induction in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
finding_consequence: The one FDR<0.10 transcript falls in carbohydrate handling rather than an overt mitochondrial-stress module, making Galt a very narrow, hypothesis-generating candidate marker of pyruvate-entry limitation in this limbic/hippocampal excitatory aggregate.

finding_summary: Pdha1, Pdhx, Dlat, and Dld did not phenocopy the Pdhb Galt response or form a shared PDC transcriptional module.

finding_summary: The only robust Pex1 responders were singleton, target-specific markers: Cabp1 up in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut and Tceal9 down in 308 CB GABA.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: Por loss failed to elicit the sterol-feedback, P450/heme-redox, or ER-stress programs that a strong disruption of its canonical enzymology might secondarily trigger.

The other tested program absences are not independently contradicted by the cited literature.

finding_summary: Por produced a single robust downstream hit: Mzt1 was down-regulated only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

finding_summary: The screen did not reproduce POR-deficiency developmental or steroidogenic disease biology after P16 neuronal CRISPR.

finding_summary: The DFNX2 inner-ear mesenchyme program was expected but absent from this neuronal Pou3f4 screen.

finding_summary: Pou3f4 produced an extremely sparse response: only two of 22 measured cell groups had any downstream gene at FDR<0.10, and both hits were decreases in GABA classes.

finding_summary: The closest screened POU-family perturbations and Tbx1 did not phenocopy Pou3f4 in the two responding GABA groups.

finding_summary: Prickle1 was a sparse responder: all 23 cell groups were represented, but only 001 L5-6 IT Glut and 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut had any downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
finding_consequence: The measured phenotype is therefore cell-type restricted and buffered rather than a pan-neuronal consequence of losing a core PCP scaffold.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut; 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut; 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

finding_summary: The nearest cross-screen neighbors were weak rank-level matches rather than robust Ptpn1 phenocopies.

finding_summary: Rab3gap2 loss did not reproduce the robust transcriptional responses of Snap25 or Stxbp1 perturbation despite their shared connection to regulated synaptic-vesicle exocytosis.

literature_rationale: The references provide a specific biochemical connection to Rab3-regulated exocytosis, making the comparison biologically grounded, but they do not predict the observed absence of a shared transcriptional program.

finding_summary: The only robust Rab3gap2 downstream hit was Ttbk1 up-regulation in 191 MB P MY GABA.
finding_consequence: A one-gene, FDR-significant Ttbk1 signature nominates a narrow hindbrain/midbrain GABA-class readout rather than a global Rab3GAP stress program.

finding_summary: Rab3gap1 and Rab18 did not phenocopy the Rab3gap2 Ttbk1 response even in the shared 191 MB P MY GABA responder.

finding_summary: Rack1 loss reduced Ppp2r1a RNA in TH Prkcd/Grin2c neurons but did not phenocopy the much broader response to direct Ppp2r1a perturbation.
finding_consequence: RACK1 can bind PP2A, yet a small Ppp2r1a transcript decrease after Rack1 perturbation is not equivalent to disrupting the PP2A scaffold gene itself.
literature_rationale: A specific RACK1–PP2A biochemical bridge is documented, but the directional transcriptional link to Ppp2r1a and the expected similarity of the two perturbation response surfaces remain unestablished.

finding_summary: Rack1 produced a real but extremely sparse 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response: only Aplp2 and Ppp2r1a were significant, both down-regulated, and the other 22 measured cell groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
finding_consequence: The primary positive biology is a cell-state-restricted two-gene signature, not a broad translation, Wnt/Shh, or stress program. The restricted surface prevents treating Rack1 as a pan-neuronal transcriptional regulator in this P16 mosaic loss-of-function assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The 151 Rack1 signature points toward the PP2A scaffold transcript Ppp2r1a, but Ppp2r1a knockout is far broader and does not reduce to a Rack1 phenocopy.
finding_consequence: RACK1 can biochemically scaffold PP2A; the screen recovers Ppp2r1a as the strongest same-direction neighbor on Aplp2/Ppp2r1a, yet direct loss of the PP2A A subunit produces thousands of DEGs across groups where Rack1 is flat. That contrast places the Rack1 hit downstream or adjacent to a PP2A-sensitive state rather than making Rack1 a general PP2A surrogate.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut; 155 MB Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Ribosome-associated Rack1 loss did not look like loss of cap-initiation factor Eif4e in the only Rack1-responsive cell group.
finding_consequence: Ribosome-bound RACK1 is reported to support eIF4E recruitment and capped-mRNA translation. Eif4e was highly active in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but it induced a 234-gene Hexim1/Rsrp1-containing signature and left Aplp2/Ppp2r1a nonsignificant, whereas Rack1 induced only Aplp2/Ppp2r1a. The assay therefore separates partial Rack1 deletion from a generic cap-initiation transcriptional state.

finding_summary: Literature-obvious RNA-granule comparators did not phenocopy Tia1 even when they were active in the same neuronal atlas: Tardbp, Fus, and Matr3 produced broad FDR signatures, Eif4e was the #6 full-screen cosine neighbor, but none reproduced Dpm1 or Zyg11b.
finding_consequence: This rejects the simple expectation that knocking down any stress-granule or ALS-linked RNA-binding protein yields the same transcriptional state in these neurons; Tia1 is buffered relative to Tardbp/Fus/Matr3 and only weakly aligned with Eif4e.

finding_summary: The healthy juvenile LoF signature does not recapitulate the TIA1 ALS/FTD phase-separation mechanism.
finding_consequence: ALS/FTD LCD mutations delay stress-granule disassembly and trap TDP-43; an acute CRISPR LoF that leaves only Dpm1 and Zyg11b as FDR hits supports treating those variants as specific stress-granule dynamics alleles rather than assuming haploinsufficiency in unstressed postmitotic neurons.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba; 191 MB P MY GABA

finding_summary: Timp3 loss produced a single robust downstream RNA change in the entire measured screen: Syp down-regulation in 046 CTX-CGE GABA.
finding_consequence: The positive phenotype is real but extremely narrow; it nominates a CTX-CGE presynaptic-vesicle marker rather than the broad ECM, inflammatory, or stress programs expected from TIMP3 biology.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA

finding_summary: Wac and Psmc1, rather than TIMP-family perturbations, were the robust CTX-CGE neighbors that converged with Timp3 on Syp down-regulation.
finding_consequence: The recurrence argues that the Syp decrease is a reproducible vulnerable output in this dataset, while the lack of many shared genes keeps it to a one-gene, hypothesis-generating module.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA

finding_summary: Timp2, the only TIMP paralog present in the screen, did not phenocopy Timp3.
finding_consequence: A same-family perturbation with measurable self-depletion in multiple regions had no CTX-CGE Syp decrease and only one downstream hit elsewhere, separating the Timp3 Syp response from generic TIMP-family loss.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA; 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut

finding_summary: The APP, Notch, presenilin, and TNF-receptor comparators did not reconstruct a TIMP3 sheddase pathway in neuronal snRNA-seq.
finding_consequence: TIMP3's canonical ADAM10/17 biology is proteolytic and ligand-shedding based; the measured downstream partner perturbations were self-only or nearly flat, explaining why Timp3 loss did not yield a canonical APP/Notch/TNF transcriptional program here.

finding_summary: The only reproducible-looking Tlk2 transcriptional effects were cell-class singletons: Cab39 decreased in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and Ppp2r2d increased in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
finding_consequence: Both calls encode phosphorylation-network regulators rather than ASF1, histone, cell-cycle, or DNA-damage transcripts, suggesting a restricted compensatory phospho-signaling response rather than a canonical chromatin-collapse program.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut; 054 CNU-MGE GABA

finding_summary: Measured TLK2-proximal chromatin comparators did not phenocopy Tlk2: Chd8 had a stronger, anatomically different response, Chd7 was almost flat, and H3f3a was completely flat.
finding_consequence: This separates TLK2's weak postnatal neuronal loss-of-function surface from CHD7/CHD8 neurodevelopmental chromatin biology and from histone H3.3 dosage in the same assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 155 MB Glut; 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut; 054 CNU-MGE GABA

finding_summary: The top data-driven Tmem163 neighbors had tiny restricted cosines and were rejected as a convergent module after direct DE-surface inspection.
finding_consequence: It keeps Prep, Syngap1, Arnt2, Slc52a2, Prnp, Dnmt3a, Hoxc13, Hivep3, Zic4, and Agps from being overcalled as mechanistic relatives of a null target.

finding_summary: The neuronal Tmem163 null does not recover the hypomyelinating-leukodystrophy program expected from oligodendrocyte and missense-variant studies.
finding_consequence: It prevents interpreting the brain-wide neuronal zero as contradiction of the HLD genetics; the expected biology is displaced into non-neuronal myelinating cells and possibly specific dominant missense alleles.
cell_types: 21 measured neuronal cell groups

finding_summary: P2rx2, the only assayed P2X-family target, was a weak rank-18 Tmem163 neighbor but was itself flat in all 21 matched cell groups.
finding_consequence: This rejects a robust P2X-family transcriptional module while remaining compatible with literature showing TMEM163 regulates P2X receptor channel function.
cell_types: 21 measured neuronal cell groups

finding_summary: Atp1a3 is the clearest single-gene marker of the MB Glut Tnrc6a response and nominates neuronal Na+/K+ pump homeostasis as a hypothesis rather than a broad ion-transport module.
finding_consequence: Atp1a3 encodes a neuronal pump subunit needed to maintain electrochemical gradients; its up-regulation provides a concrete follow-up biomarker for the otherwise sparse Tnrc6a signature.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Ptges2 was the second MB Glut Tnrc6a FDR<0.10 hit, but it appeared as an isolated prostaglandin/lipid-enzyme candidate rather than a coordinated inflammatory program.
finding_consequence: The NeuN-enriched screen largely lacks glia, so a Ptges2 increase in 155 MB Glut should be followed as a neuronal lipid-metabolic clue, not over-read as neuroinflammation.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The strongest anti-neighbors, Wdr26 and Camta1, drove Atp1a3 and Atp1b1 down in 155 MB Glut, opposite to the Tnrc6a direction at the same pump genes.
finding_consequence: The opposite direction in two broad MB Glut perturbations shows that Atp1a3 up-regulation is not a universal consequence of midbrain glutamatergic stress or loss of transcriptomic health.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Tnrc6a loss produced a real but very narrow 155 MB Glut-only response: Atp1a3 and Ptges2 were up at FDR<0.10, whereas the other 20 measured cell groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
finding_consequence: A GW182/TNRC6 scaffold could have produced broad miRNA-target de-repression; instead, this postnatal sparse CRISPR screen recovers one restricted midbrain glutamatergic pocket and no genome-wide mRNA-destabilization collapse.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The measured miRISC neighbors did not phenocopy Tnrc6a: Tnrc6b, Dicer1 and Ago2 were FDR-flat in matched groups, Ago1 and Eif4a2 responded only outside 155 MB Glut, and Cnot1 gave a different 155 MB Glut signature.
finding_consequence: Cross-perturbation data argue against interpreting the two Tnrc6a hits as a generic shutdown of miRNA biogenesis, AGO loading, or the whole CCR4-NOT deadenylase arm.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 191 MB P MY GABA; 308 CB GABA

finding_summary: In Sst GABA neurons, Trak1 loss selectively up-regulated Nop56, a box C/D snoRNP and ribosome-biogenesis factor.
finding_consequence: Nop56 nominates a nucleolar/rRNA-processing stress or compensation marker in the only cortical inhibitory class with an FDR-level Trak1 response, not a classical mitochondrial-transport gene.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba

finding_summary: In midbrain glutamatergic neurons, Trak1 loss selectively up-regulated Synj1, a synaptic phosphoinositide phosphatase needed for synaptic-vesicle endocytosis and recycling.
finding_consequence: The strongest MB Glut response points to membrane/synaptic-vesicle adaptation rather than a canonical mitochondrial transcript, consistent with a neurite-compartment perturbation that may be compensated at synapses.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: Trak1 produced a trace, cell-restricted nuclear response: exactly one FDR<0.10 downstream gene in Sst GABA neurons and exactly one in midbrain glutamatergic neurons, with no robust down-regulated genes anywhere.
finding_consequence: The phenotype is not a broad mitochondrial-stress signature; it is a survivor-state readout with two isolated positive genes over a 22-cell-group postnatal neuronal surface.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba; 155 MB Glut

finding_summary: The Miro/kinesin partners assayed in the same screen, Rhot1, Kif5a and Kif5c, did not phenocopy Trak1: each had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes and near-zero cosine similarity to Trak1.
finding_consequence: A direct physical pathway relationship was measurable but not enough to create a matched nuclear signature, arguing that the Trak1 singleton genes are not a generic readout of weakening the mitochondrial motor-adaptor chain.

finding_summary: Expected secondary mitochondrial stress, autophagy/mitophagy, OXPHOS and mitochondrial-biogenesis markers were absent from the Trak1 DE surface.
finding_consequence: TRAK1 deficiency is linked to defective mitochondrial movement and respiration in severe models, yet the surviving P16-perturbed neuronal nuclei did not mount an Atf4/Ddit3, Hspa5/Xbp1, Pink1/Prkn, Sqstm1/Map1lc3, or Ppargc1a/Nrf1/Tfam-type nuclear program.

finding_summary: In the Trim2-responsive thalamic surface, App and Cntn1 decreased without induction of Nefl, Nefm, or Nefh transcripts.
finding_consequence: Published TRIM2 loss-of-function disease mechanisms center on failure to ubiquitinate NEFL protein; this Perturb-seq response instead reads out App/Cntn1 down-regulation without Nefl, Nefm or Nefh mRNA accumulation.
literature_rationale: The literature provides a highly specific Trim2-to-neurofilament mechanism, but its measured endpoint is protein ubiquitination and accumulation rather than transcription. Thus it supports the claimed mechanistic distinction without decisively predicting the observed RNA directions.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Trim2 perturbation produced a compact concordant decrease of the axonal and cell-surface-associated genes App and Cntn1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
finding_consequence: The positive biology in this screen is not a broad E3-ligase stress response; it is a thalamic, axon/surface-associated two-gene response that would be missed if the target were summarized only as null.
literature_rationale: The concordant compact response provides an experimentally supported biological interpretation beyond listing unrelated DEGs. Confidence is limited by absent Trim2 target-RNA significance, lack of a target-specific literature bridge, and the high response propensity and larger sample of group 151.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Pre-literature whole-screen neighbors did not form a robust Trim2 module: the nearest active-gene correlations were near zero and none reproduced the thalamic App/Cntn1 signature.
finding_consequence: This rejects an attractive but artifactual network interpretation of the two-gene Trim2 signature; Trim2 is isolated in DE space rather than embedded in a strong co-perturbation cluster.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The canonical TRIM2-NEFL disease axis was not recovered as Nefl/Nefm/Nefh mRNA regulation or as a proteostasis/UPR/autophagy transcriptome in the responding thalamic neurons.
finding_consequence: It separates TRIM2's known substrate biology from a nuclear RNA phenotype: a post-translational neurofilament-clearance defect can be highly disease-relevant yet nearly invisible in this 3-4 week snRNA readout unless it crosses a secondary-stress threshold.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Basal Trim2 loss did not collapse onto the ERK/MAPK transcriptional branch that is active in the same thalamic class after Braf or Map2k1 perturbation.
finding_consequence: TRIM2 can act downstream of ERK-phosphorylated Bim in ischemic tolerance, but Braf and Map2k1 loss in this dataset down-regulated Vgf, Ptpn5, Unc13a and related genes without changing App or Cntn1; the basal Trim2 phenotype is therefore not a generic MAPK/Bim transcriptomic state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Gsk3a down-regulation was the sole FDR-significant Trpv1 response in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
finding_consequence: This preserves the only robust negative cortical hit while avoiding overcalling a one-gene GSK3 pathway; the screened paralog Gsk3b did not phenocopy in the same cell group.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut

finding_summary: Cep120 up-regulation was the sole FDR-significant Trpv1 response in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
finding_consequence: The hit nominates a centrosome/ciliogenesis-associated transcript as a narrow GABAergic sentinel without implying that a complete ciliary program was activated.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Screened thermoTRP relatives did not phenocopy Trpv1 in brain neurons: Trpa1 was flat and Trpm3/Trpv4 each responded only in one non-matching cell class.
finding_consequence: A paralog-family expectation generated by pain literature was directly rejected in matched cell groups, supporting peripheral sensory lineage mismatch over an interchangeable central thermoTRP module.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; 145 MH-LH TH Glut; 053 Sst Gaba

finding_summary: Tspan12 did not phenocopy the measurable Norrin/FZD4/LRP5/β-catenin pathway surface: Fzd4 and Lrp5 were flat, whereas Ctnnb1, Apc, Tcf7l2, Lrp6, and Gsk3b responded in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut without sharing B4gat1.
finding_consequence: This separates the receptor-layer Tspan12 null from a generic failure to detect Wnt/β-catenin transcription and localizes the expected disease biology to the vascular Norrin context rather than postmitotic neurons.
literature_rationale: The corrected claim is restricted to group 151 and the highly active downstream beta-catenin perturbations, which did not reproduce the sparse Tspan12 response. Literature directly supports TSPAN12 dependence of Norrin-FZD4 signaling but not generic Wnt-driven beta-catenin output. Flat Fzd4/Lrp5 comparisons and the uninformative group-217 pathway surface are excluded.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: Tspan12 produced only two singleton FDR<0.10 downstream calls: B4gat1 up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and AI854703 up in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
finding_consequence: The measured response is not a canonical Norrin/Wnt, stress, proteostasis, or synaptic module; the two genes should be treated as narrow biomarker candidates rather than a pathway-level phenotype.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 217 P MY Pineal Glut

finding_summary: The ADAM10/APP comparator axis was transcriptionally flat and did not converge with Tspan12.
finding_consequence: It prevents over-interpreting a post-translational TSPAN12-ADAM10 APP-cleavage mechanism as a missing mRNA program in snRNA-seq.

finding_summary: The only known presynaptic family response was Rimbp2 down-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
finding_consequence: RIM-BP2 is the closest measured transcript to the canonical RIM-BP1 active-zone mechanism, so its selective decrease links the singleton DEG to the correct protein family while arguing against a simple compensatory Rimbp2-up model.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA

finding_summary: Tmem131l was the sole FDR-supported up-regulated transcript in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA after Tspoap1 perturbation.
finding_consequence: The result nominates a compact, cell-class-restricted marker of a noncanonical Tspoap1 response for follow-up, distinct from the RIM-BP active-zone prior.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Tspoap1 perturbation produced an extremely sparse transcriptional response: one downstream FDR<0.10 gene in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, one in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and zero in the other 21 measured cell groups.
finding_consequence: The result reframes Tspoap1 as a largely buffered or nontranscriptional presynaptic perturbation in this P16 acute snRNA-seq assay, not as a broad neuronal stress or identity regulator.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Neither unbiased two-feature neighbors nor measured active-zone comparator targets robustly phenocopied the Tspoap1 signature.
finding_consequence: This prevents apparent raw neighbors or textbook partners from being over-interpreted: the two FDR features were unique to Tspoap1 in the full screen, and Cacna1a, Unc13b, Snap25, and Syn1 did not reproduce them in matched responder groups.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Canonical synaptic and TSPO/mitochondrial priors were not recovered as broad transcriptional programs.
finding_consequence: The negative program test localizes the expected effect away from nuclear mRNA abundance: the RIM-BP literature predicts active-zone Ca2+-release coupling, and Reactome's TSPO:BZRAP1 cholesterol reaction has an undetermined TSPOAP1 role, but this screen recovered only Rimbp2 and Tmem131l and no mitochondrial or cholesterol-module cascade.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA; 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Vsx1 loss produced one real brain response: a two-gene, up-regulated signature in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
finding_consequence: The effect proves that the perturbation was not globally flat, but the recovered program is tiny and ectopic relative to Vsx1 retinal biology: Zc3h13 marks nuclear m6A/RNA-processing machinery and Atp1b2 marks a Na/K-ATPase beta subunit rather than an OFF-cone bipolar differentiation cascade.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Proteostasis and RNA/glycosylation perturbations move the Vsx1 066 markers in the opposite direction.
finding_consequence: Psmb4, Pomp, Ogt, and Hnrnpu each caused a broader 066 response and FDR<0.10 movement of at least one Vsx1 marker in the opposite direction, separating the Vsx1 two-gene up-shift from states that suppress Atp1b2 or Zc3h13.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: The expected retinal cone-bipolar program was absent from the Vsx1 brain DE surface.
finding_consequence: Vsx1 germline mutants are expected to lose late OFF-cone bipolar markers, yet Rcvrn, Tacr3/NK3R, Neto1, Cabp5/CaB5, and other visual-circuit genes never moved at FDR<0.10 in any sampled brain group, showing that the P16 NeuN+ brain assay did not reconstitute the retinal differentiation state in which Vsx1 is canonical.

finding_summary: The measurable retinal relatives Vsx2, Ptf1a, and Isl1 did not phenocopy the 066 Vsx1 signature.
finding_consequence: Vsx2 is the Chx10 paralog that directly represses Vsx1 in retina, and Ptf1a/Isl1 are STRING-nominated Vsx1 retinal-network genes; their flat 066 Atp1b2/Zc3h13 measurements reject a simple shared retinal-TF module in this postnatal brain screen.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Atp1b2, but not Zc3h13, places Vsx1 near the broad Zbtb7a response.
finding_consequence: The top positive restricted-signature neighbor was not a retinal paralog; it was Zbtb7a, whose 066 response contains 98 FDR genes and recurrent Atp1b2 induction across 15 cell groups, implying that Atp1b2 is a generic adaptive marker that the tiny Vsx1 effect touches rather than a Vsx1-specific effector.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

finding_summary: Ywhae did not converge with LIS1/NDEL1/dynein comparators even though Dync1h1 and Dctn1 generated clear sterol/lipid responses in matched groups.
finding_consequence: This localizes the postnatal sterol-bounce response to dynein/dynactin motor disruption, not to every upstream migration regulator in the embryonic Ywhae pathway.

finding_summary: Ywhae perturbation did not mimic TSC/mTOR or RAF/MAPK transcriptional states.

finding_summary: The Ywhae null surface refines 17p13.3 disease interpretation toward developmental dosage and away from an acute postnatal basal transcriptome mechanism.
finding_consequence: Human YWHAE lesions are developmental CNVs/deletions; lowering Ywhae after neurons are specified did not recapitulate those syndromes as a broad neuronal DE program.

finding_summary: Engaged Ywhaz loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut did not mobilize the nominated RAF/MAPK or catenin/Rho/LIMK transcriptional outputs.
finding_consequence: The assayed RAF/MAPK, catenin/Rho/LIMK, apoptosis, and NMDAR-related effector transcripts stayed below even relaxed FDR thresholds, fitting a model in which Ywhaz acts mainly through phosphorylation-dependent binding, localization, or synaptic protein trafficking.
literature_rationale: The literature provides target-specific pathway mechanisms, but it does not yield a decisive RNA-level expectation against which the absence of pathway transcript changes can be called opposite.

finding_summary: Ywhaz loss did not induce transcriptional compensation by other 14-3-3 isoform genes in the engaged thalamic context.
finding_consequence: If acute isoform buffering explains the muted Ywhaz phenotype, it is not visible as transcriptional upregulation of Ywhae, Ywhag, Ywhah, Ywhaq, Ywhab, or Sfn in this dataset.
literature_rationale: The target–paralog relationship is specific, but dimerization and functional association do not establish transcriptional compensation; the observed lack of isoform induction therefore refines an unevaluated mechanism rather than agreeing or disagreeing with a documented direction.

finding_summary: Ywhaz loss produced a single FDR-qualified downstream transcriptomic hit, Pfn2 up-regulation, in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
finding_consequence: Pfn2 is an actin- and synaptic-vesicle regulator, so the one recovered gene falls in a plausible cytoskeletal/synaptic effector space for a 14-3-3 scaffold rather than in a generic stress signature.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

finding_summary: Genome-scale Ywhaz signature neighbors had absolute score correlations below 0.04 and failed to share the 008 Pfn2 hit.
finding_consequence: The strongest data-driven neighbors, Kcnb1/Frrs1l/Ndufs8 and Npy1r/Fbxo11/Atp6v1e1, are near-zero correlations rather than a convergent module, so downstream interpretation should stay anchored to the singleton Pfn2 response and the broad null surface.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; 308 CB GABA; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

finding_summary: The acute postnatal Ywhaz signature did not converge with catenin/Rho/LIMK or RAF/ERK comparators that are known 14-3-3-associated pathways.
finding_consequence: Ctnnb1 and Braf could produce FDR-significant transcriptional responses in the same screen, including the same 151 thalamic group where Ywhaz mRNA was significantly depressed, but their programs were absent after Ywhaz perturbation.

finding_summary: The screen argues against a broad, cell-autonomous postmitotic stress-transcription model for sparse Ywhaz loss across juvenile neurons.
finding_consequence: Ywhaz is linked to developmental wiring and synapse phenotypes, but 20 of 21 measured groups lacked downstream FDR<0.10 genes and curated apoptosis, UPR/ISR, TFEB-lysosome, catenin/Rho, and ERK/IEG sentinels were absent, focusing disease interpretations on developmental timing, phosphoprotein scaffolding, or paralog-combinatorial mechanisms.

finding_summary: The only FDR<0.10 hit in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut was Sccpdh up-regulation.
finding_consequence: This is a small, cell-restricted metabolic marker candidate for Zfhx4 loss in a hypothalamic glutamatergic class, not a broad Zfhx4 transcriptional module.
